News.title: Death row killer Christa Pike in critical condition & receiving life-saving care after ‘disturbing’ botched execution
News.content:
Next

CHRISTA Pike remains in a critical condition and is receiving life-saving hospital care after surviving a “deeply disturbing” botched execution.

The death row killer, 50, is feared to have suffered major injuries after reportedly being left scared she was “going to burst” while strapped to the gurney.



Pike’s attorney Randy Spivey said on Thursday night: “We don’t have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment.

“But we know she is alive right now.”



No other major updates on her condition have been revealed since she was rushed to hospital.

Spivey called the failed double injection “cruel and torturous” as he claimed Pike was pierced with seven needles as docs couldn’t find a viable vein.



Dr Joel Zivot, a professor at the Emory University School of Medicine has been closely following Pike’s case and warned of the dangers of lethal injection pre-execution.

He told The Sun that he suspects a botched insertion led to the fiasco as the lethal dose of pentobarbital likely infiltrated her surrounding arm tissue rather than entering her bloodstream directly.



He said: “She very likely has a significant burn on one or both arms from the pentobarbital that I expect went into the tissues.

“That will require care for a period of time. She might have a weakened heart now.”

Zivot also told the BBC that he believes doctors didn’t act fast enough to avoid Pike suffering from long-lasting health issues.

He said: “It’s very possible that as a consequence of the delay of the beginning of resuscitation she will have a brain injury.”

Debate is now raging on over what will happen to Pike should she recover.



Spivey has called on Tennessee Governor Bill Lee to change Pike’s death sentence to life in prison.

What is pentobarbital? CHRISTA Pike was given two doses of what should have been fatal pentobarbital by executioners. Pentobarbital is a strong, short-acting barbiturate drug that slows down activity in the brain and nervous system. It is the common drug of chose used to put animals to sleep and is often used for euthanasia and lethal injections. In small doses it can be given to hospital patients to help put them to sleep or put them into a medically induced coma. Some doctors use it to treat seizures and convulsions. In America, pentobarbital is known by its brand name, Nembutal. Pentobarbital being used on death row cons has sparked controversy for years over if the drug is actually painless. The Biden administration had previously removed pentobarbital from the federal protocol for single-drug lethal injections over concerns about the potential for unnecessary suffering. So far this year, 14 inmates have been executed by pentobarbital in Texas, Missouri and Georgia.

He said Christa has endured punishment “greater than any other person in the history of the American death penalty”.

Lee is yet to make any decision on Pike’s future but has halted all executions in the state for the remainder of the year.

An independent review into Pike’s attempted execution is ongoing.



It comes as Donald Trump weighed in on the issue of the botched execution saying: “How does that happen?

“Should be easy to do. It shouldn’t be very difficult.”

He was quizzed if the government had any official say on where the case goes next but simply responded: “You’re going to have to speak to Tennessee about it. Whether or not they’re going to go forward.”

The failed lethal injection was the second time this year Tennessee officials were unable to put a death row inmate to death.

Tony Carruthers’ execution was abandoned in May after officials were unable to establish the necessary IV access.



Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.

She was just 18 when she killed Slemmer, a fellow student at a job-training program in Knoxville, on January 12, 1995.

She planned the deadly attack alongside then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, as they beat, tortured and killed the 19-year-old.



Pike lured Slemmer to a wooded area before using a box cutter and large chunk of asphalt to attack her.

What happens next? CHRISTA Pike survived two doses of lethal infection, creating extraordinary questions for the state and its death penalty protocol. Following Pike’s failed execution, a third-party review has been launched to investigate what happened inside the chamber. All scheduled executions across Tennessee have been cancelled for the rest of the year while the investigation takes place. The investigation is expected to examine what happened during the execution. Meanwhile Pike’s lawyers have moved to prevent Tennessee from making another attempt. Tennessee execution protocol calls for a secondary set of drug syringes to be administered “if the inmate is not deceased” after the first set. But it does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set. The Supreme Court confronted the issue 80 years ago in Louisiana ex rel. Francis v. Resweber. In 1947 Willie Francis survived an attempted execution in Louisiana’s electric chair after the equipment malfunctioned. The Supreme Court allowed the state to attempt the execution a second time, rejecting claims that another effort would violate double jeopardy or amount to cruel and unusual punishment. That reasoning has guided later cases involving prisoners who survive an execution attempt. But Pike’s unique circumstances could force courts to examine where that precedent stops applying.

Prosecutors said she feared Slemmer was trying to steal her boyfriend.

Shipp carved a pentagram, a star-shaped symbol associated with Satanism, into Slemmer’s body.

Shipp was just 17 when the crime happened and received a sentence of life in prison with the possibility of parole.



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Pike was sentenced to death and has never denied the killing but said she was “a mentally ill 18-year-old kid”.

Since being jailed in 1996, Christa Pike has been kept in solitary confinement for 29 years.

News.title: Three quarters of people aim to keep their ‘future self’ happy, new poll finds
News.content:
Next

THREE quarters of people aim to keep their ‘future self’ happy – but say it’s not always easy to think beyond the day-to-day.

A poll of 2,000 adults found 77 per cent believe in the mantra “a stitch in time saves nine” – embracing small habits today in the hope of making life straight forward further down the line.



Ways in which people help their future selves include building up loyalty points with favourite brands (47 per cent) and planning meals in advance to make ingredients go further and cut down on waste (41 per cent).

Meanwhile, 23 per cent have considered switching banks for better deals, and 17 per cent round up and save the difference each time they make a purchase.



But 60 per cent said it can be hard to think too far ahead – because of unexpected expenses (46 per cent).

Technology is helping many people think ahead, with 28 per cent revealing they use tech to keep track of household spending.



Television presenter Anthea Turner, expert on practical living and home organisation, said: “Life can be busy, so it’s always satisfying when you’ve done something that makes things a bit easier for yourself further down the line.

“Whether it’s planning meals, switching from an analogue prepay meter to a smart meter so you can top up from home or shopping around for a better deal on insurance, small decisions can add up over time.

“The research shows how many people are already taking steps to help their future selves.

“It doesn’t have to be big changes. Sometimes it’s the small habits that can make a difference later on.”



It also emerged, with winter bringing higher energy costs alongside extra spending at Christmas, 73 per cent think it’s important to start preparing ahead of time.

While the research carried out through OnePoll found 63 per cent are most concerned about their energy bills in the winter months, with 84 per cent already taking practical steps to build a financial cushion ahead of the colder months.

These include buying Christmas gifts when they see them (30 per cent) or building up emergency savings (28 per cent).

Victoria Bacon, director at Smart Energy GB, which commissioned the research, said: “The findings show many people are looking for simple ways to stay one step ahead and feel more prepared for what’s around the corner.

“If you prepay for your energy, upgrading to a smart meter can help.



“Smart prepay meters enable you to top up from home rather than having to make a journey to the shops, and the display helps you keep track of your remaining credit.

“Having a clearer view of your energy use and credit can make it a bit easier to plan ahead and stay in control, especially when managing household budgets.”

News.title: Shocking moment policewoman is chase, kicked to ground & beaten by vicious mob as violent protests rage across France
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment a policewoman is chased down and kicked to the ground by a furious mob as teen-led riots rage across France.

Violence has escalated across the nation after initially peaceful protests over rat and cockroach-infested classrooms spiralled into chaos.



Schools have been set on fire, streets barricaded and teachers allegedly attacked in a wave of senseless brutality.

Disturbing footage shows several suspects dressed in all black chasing down a policewoman in the suburbs of Paris.





She is kicked to the ground – where she rolls over from the force of the impact – before being surrounded by youths in backpacks.

A sickening caption says that they have “swept over a policewoman” followed by a barrage of crying-with-laughter emojis.



One viewer slammed the incident, saying: “The situation is catastrophic.

“No one should condone this.”

Former leader of France‘s hard-right National Rally party Marine Le Pen also chimed in on X to condemn the attack.

She said: “The image of this young policewoman, pursued by a howling mob screaming its hatred, thrown to the ground and assaulted, is unbearable.

“These acts deserve exemplary punishments. Let her know that tonight, millions of French people offer her their warm support.”



Almost 2,000 suspects – including several under 16 – were arrested on Thursday following clashes with the police, according to Interior Minister Laurent Nunez.

Nunex blasted the “unbridled violence” and said condemned “the targeting of law enforcement officers, the throwing of missiles, acts of violence, verbal abuse, attempted arson, and all-round urban violence”.

The shock protests started on September 21 over demands for more teachers and funding and complaints over dilapidated classroms.



Rioting has since erupted on the streets – with Paris and Marseille bearing the brunt of the assault.

In one horrific attack a headteacher in Marseille’s Victor Hugo School was doused in petrol and set on fire, prosecutors claim.

Hundreds of protestors then surrounded a fire truck that came to put out the flames at the school – forcing firefighters to flee – before setting the vehicle alight.

Another headsteacher was struck in the leg by a firework at the Jean-Pierre Timbaud school in Paris in one suspected assault.

Shocking clips also appeared to show a fireman engulfed in flames after an aerosol can exploded outside a Bordeaux school.



The Nelson Mandela High School in Nantes was going up in a raging blaze in separate clip.

Cops have launched teargas into the swarms of protestors in desperate efforts to quell the violence.

More than 400 schools will stay closed on Friday following days of terrifying unrest, confirmed Education Minister Edouard Geffray.



At least 150 pupils and students have also been injured since the chaos broke out – including one pupil who blew up part of his hand while launching a firework.

Allegations of police brutality have also surged amid the chaos.

A student, 14, reportedly lost several teeth after an officer fired a tear-gas grenade into his jaw from point-blank range.

Police have launched an investigation into the ordeal – with prosecutors arguing the teen had allegedly assaulted a policewoman beforehand.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

French president Emmanuel Macron has called for an end to the violence.



Raging protests have spread beyond Paris and into several French cities including Lille, Bordeaux, and Lyon.

News.title: Teen welder turned into ‘human fireball’ in workplace explosion that left him in a coma with ‘melted face’
News.content:
'LIKE A BOMB' Teen welder turned into ‘human fireball’ in workplace explosion that left him in a coma with ‘melted face’







Next

A TEENAGE apprentice whose face melted after being turned into a “human fireball” in a workplace explosion has secured a six-figure pay out.

Horrific pictures show Dwayne Bell, 17, with his face blackened and skin peeling away after the blast at a steel yard in Manchester.



The now 22-year-old has secured a six-figure compensation settlement following the horror attack in March, 2021.

After suffering from third-degree burns, he spent a week in a medically induced coma.



Dwayne said: “I shouldn’t be here talking to you. I am lucky to be alive.

“It was so hot I feared I was going to be blinded the heat was so intense.



“This was an accident waiting to happen. I’m trying to move on. But I’m living in a body that feels like a prison.”

He attended Knowsley Tech College for one day a week, and spent the other four days being an apprentice at Qualfab Steel Ltd.



He said: “I was just a kid, doing what I was told. I was the youngest on site by 20 or 30 years.

“I never had any real training on the dangers of what I was doing or given any PPE safety goggles – I was just left to it.”

At the Wigan plant, Dwayne was asked to perform the routine task of burning rubbish – something he had seen his colleagues do “a hundred times”.



But disaster struck when he added paint thinner to try and ignite some damp wood in the metal barrel.

He failed to notice sparks which had already caught under the wood, which caused the cylinder filled with paper and cardboard to explode into flames.

He said: “The next thing I knew, the world just turned orange. The sound was like a jet engine.



“I was standing in the middle of a massive flame. As soon as I felt the whoosh of heat I shut my eyes as I didn’t want to go blind. It was like a bomb exploding in my face.”

Dwayne’s clothes then began to melt on him as colleagues scrambled to save his life.

He asked colleagues to take pictures of him, stating that in the moment he “felt no pain” and did not know how bad the situation really was.

He said the end of his nose “melted” and he was rushed to Whiston Hospital.



He added: “I was being constantly sick due to the breathing tubes, I couldn’t sleep because of the bleeping and I felt like I was on fire whenever I moved.

“I looked at the nurses and I just begged them to let me die.

“I couldn’t see a future. I was wrapped in bandages, I couldn’t move, and the pain was the worst I had ever experienced so I asked the nurses just to turn the machines off and let me go.”

After three weeks in hospital, his mum had to care for him.



Having ears burned to a crisp, the teen could not sleep on his side and his skin would constantly break – he called it a “living nightmare”.

Dwayne later had three skin grafts and will need further surgery.

Now, the 22-year-old has negotiated a six-figure settlement for the traumatic blast.

Senior Associate Neil Sagar, Express Solicitors, said: “Dwayne has made a miraculous recovery from his life changing injuries.

“But he still lives with the consequences of what happened everyday and his ongoing scars will affect his future career.



“Businesses need to make sure appropriate supervision and training is given to apprentices, especially when working with dangerous disposal methods.”

Dwayne is now an apprentice welder at another firm.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

He said: “I have to live with the consequences of what happened there everyday. Now I just want to try and live as normal life as possible.”

Qualfab Steel Ltd has been approached for comment.

News.title: Man, 56, charged with murder after body of  woman, 51, ‘found in bike shed’ in residential street
News.content:
GRIM END Man, 56, charged with murder after body of woman, 51, ‘found in bike shed’ in residential street







Next

A MAN has been charged with murder after a woman’s body was found dumped in a bike shed.

Mackala Higgins was found dead at an address in Bournemouth earlier this year.



Despite the best effort from emergency services, the 51-year-old was pronounced dead at the scene.

Now, 56-year-old Richard Sean Ball of Bournemouth has been charged with murder.



He was previously charged with preventing the lawful and decent burial of a dead body following his arrest.

Ball, a British national, is remanded in custody and is next due to appear at Southampton Magistrates’ Court later today.

Officers also arrested a woman aged in her 30s on suspicion of assisting an offender.

She remains released under investigation as enquiries continue.

Detective Chief Inspector Nicola Jenkins said: “Our thoughts remain very much with the family and loved ones of Mackala Higgins and we have continued to keep the family updated with developments in the investigation.

“Following further and extensive enquiries, we have liaised with the Crown Prosecution Service and it has authorised an additional charge of murder.



“I would like to issue a reminder that this matter remains the subject of active court proceedings and it is vital that the judicial process is allowed to follow its course.

“We would urge members of the public to refrain from any commentary, particularly online and on social media, that could potentially prejudice these proceedings.”

Detectives are continuing to urge anyone with information that might assist their investigation to contact Dorset Police online or by calling 101, quoting occurrence number 55260097894.

Alternatively, independent charity Crimestoppers can be contacted anonymously online using its website or by calling Freephone 0800 555 111.

News.title: Who was Gypsy Rose Blanchard’s fiance Ken Urker?
News.content:
Next

GYPSY Rose Blanchard’s fiance has died at the age of 34 after being found unresponsive at a home in Louisiana on his birthday.

Ken Urker, a former Texas detention officer, maintained a relationship with Gypsy twice, first connecting while she was serving a prison sentence.



Here is everything you need to know about the man who won Gypsy’s heart from behind bars, and how their story unfolded.

Who was Ken Urker?

Ken Urker was the two-time fiance of Gypsy Rose Blanchard and the father of her daughter. He died on his birthday.



The alarm was raised after Gypsy grew concerned when Ken failed to reply to a simple “happy birthday” text message.

The Lafourche Sheriff’s Office confirmed the news, stating: “We responded to a residence in Raceland today after receiving a call at 6.15pm.

“Kenan Urker, 34, was found dead upon arrival. At this time, we are continuing the death investigation.”

Raised in Texas alongside four siblings, Ken lived across several states including California, Florida, and Washington, before relocating to Louisiana.

Professionally, he once worked as a bartender and served as a detention service officer in Dallas County in 2023.

Ken and Gypsy met after he wrote a letter to the then-inmate upon watching the HBO documentary Mommy Dead and Dearest.



The film told the story of Gypsy’s traumatic early life and the medical child abuse she suffered at the hands of her mother, Clauddine “Dee Dee” Blanchard.

Dee Dee had spent years drugging her daughter and convincing her and the world that she was severely mentally and physically ill.

Gypsy eventually developed an online relationship with Nicholas Godejohn. As she realised the severity of her abuse, the pair hatched a plan to kill her mother.

On June 14, 2015, Dee Dee was found stabbed to death, leading to lengthy prison sentences for both Gypsy and Godejohn.

Moved by the abuse she had endured, Ken reached out.



The pair quickly formed a bond, and Ken proposed during a prison visit in October 2018, but they did not go through with the marriage and went their separate ways.

During their time apart, Gypsy married Ryan Scott Anderson in an infamous prison wedding in July 2022.

After serving seven years of her sentence, Gypsy was released in December 2023 and public interest in her life skyrocketed.

But her marriage to Ryan proved short-lived, and she filed for divorce just three months later, saying she had no regrets, but wished she hadn’t gotten married “in prison so fast”.

In April 2024, Ken and Gypsy rekindled their romance and got engaged for a second time.



Despite the media attention surrounding their relationship, Ken remained a private figure who kept his personal life away from the spotlight.

Did they have children?

Ken and Gypsy had one child together, a daughter, Aurora Raina Urker, who was born in December 2024.

Following Ken’s death, Gypsy told People magazine: “Ken loved our daughter, Aurora.

“She is a beautiful reflection of his enduring spirit, and through her, a part of him will always remain with us.

“I will make sure she grows up knowing how deeply her father loved her.”



RECOMMENDED STORIES

Speaking to TMZ, she described him as an “amazing father and a man who was deeply loved.”

She added: “He will forever be my soulmate and my red string, a connection that time, distance, and even death can never erase.”

News.title: Woman, 38, ‘showed schoolboy how to kiss and have sex then told him to keep it secret’
News.content:
TEEN HORROR Woman, 38, ‘showed schoolboy how to kiss and have sex then told him to keep it secret’







Next

A WOMAN showed a teen boy how to kiss and have sex before telling him to keep it a secret, a court heard.

Kirsty Slater, 38, is accused of three counts of sexual activity with the boy, who was under 16 at the time.

Jurors heard the alleged abuse took place when Slater was alone with the boy one night, Lancs Live reports.

He told police he felt “fuzzy” because he had been drinking beer so she suggested they go outside and look at the sky.





The boy said he then asked Slater how to kiss, adding: “When I said that, she just says ‘just come on then’ and goes close to me and kisses me.

“Then she stops and sits back down. I was like ‘what’s just happened?’.”

Preston Crown Court heard they began listening to music and he asked for another drink before “everything got a bit weirder”.

The boy continued in his video interview: “The atmosphere just felt off.

“I was like ‘that was weird, what just happened?'”

He claimed Slater then kissed him again and said he could touch her breasts, jurors heard.

The court was told the pair had sex before Slater allegedly told him to keep it a secret.

Continuing his statement, the boy added: “It was kind of like… surreal. Like ‘did that actually happen or am I just imagining it?’. It was very weird.



“Afterwards I felt, like, disgusting, if you know what I mean? I felt more like, inhumane. It’s very weird but that’s how I felt. So, yeah.”

The court heard the alleged abuse came to light when the teen told a counsellor.

Kristian Cavanagh, defending, told him: “Kirsty Slater will say she hasn’t kissed you; you haven’t touched her breasts; and she hasn’t had sex with you.

“She didn’t get undressed in front of you and she didn’t tell you this was your little secret.”

“That’s false,” the teenager replied.



Slater, of Oswaldtwistle, Lancashire, denies three counts of sexual activity with a person aged 13 to 15.

The trial continues.

News.title: Moment four ‘dine & dashers’ including ‘two regulars who got engaged at table’ flee restaurant after racking up £200 tab
News.content:
Next

THIS is the shocking moment four “dine and dashers” allegedly leave a table without paying their £200 bill after ordering steak and cocktails.

Two of the party were said to be regulars at the Bistro and had even got engaged in the restaurant, according to one manager.



The CCTV footage from around 9pm on Saturday, September 26, shows a younger couple leave the table and head to the exit.

Once they walk out the door a second woman quickly walks out leaving a man to finish his drink.



Halfway House has reported the incident to Essex Police who are investigating.

Speaking to The Sun, the general manager of The Halfway House in Brentwood, Essex, said after the younger pair walked out, “the older couple went out for a cigarette and then left”.



In later footage the group are seen walking across the restaurant car park – which uses an ANPR – to a nearby business where they had reportedly left their car.

A spokesperson for bar and restaurant said: “On Saturday evening, four individuals visited our restaurant, enjoyed a meal and drinks, and then, unbelievably, left without paying their £200.40 bill.”



They continued: “They have visited our restaurant several times before and even got engaged at one of our tables.

“You would think that after being welcomed back time and time again, the least we could expect would be the courtesy of paying their bill.”

The restaurant said they reached out to the diners via Instagram, giving them the benefit of the doubt.

However, they responded: “Not sorting f**k out with yous” and reportedly blocked the restaurant’s account.

One of the party then claimed they had left money on the table on their social media page.



The employee said: “let’s be absolutely clear, no money was left on the table”.

They added: “We are a small family run business and with the cost of living crisis at the moment customer numbers have reduced and this is just a kick in the teeth.”

They posted the CCTV clip of the diners on social media so: “hopefully they’ll have a conscience”.



A photo of the group’s bill reveals they ordered cocktails and two rump steaks alongside other mains and starters, bringing their total to £200.40.

A spokesperson for the force said: “We are investigating a report of making off without payment at the Halfway House restaurant in West Horndon.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“The report was made to us at around 9.35pm on Saturday 26 September, after a group reportedly left the restaurant without paying the bill.

“Our enquiries are ongoing.”

News.title: Hidden heroes of FlyDubai flight from 6-year-old's brave signal to plucky plumber in cockpit
News.content:
Hidden heroes of FlyDubai flight from 6-year-old's brave signal to plucky plumber in cockpit

Faced with a seemingly inescapable situation thousands of feet up in the air, a heroic group took back control of the hijacked FlyDubai flight FZ1073, showing extraordinary resourcefulness as they took the alleged attacker down

View 5 Images A heroic group took back control of the hijacked FlyDubai flight FZ1073

When FlyDubai flight FZ1073 started to drop down 'like a rollercoaster' two and a half hours after take-off, passengers on board had no clue that they were about to find themselves in a living nightmare.

Harrowing scenes erupted on Wednesday's flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv after a captain was stabbed at 34,000ft - allegedly by his co-pilot in an attempted hijacking.

As injured Indian captain Smit Machchhar was fighting for his life, he opened up the cockpit to a group of brave passengers who managed to fight the alleged attacker to the ground and tie him up, while others jumped to regain control of the plummeting aircraft.

Initial findings from Saudi officials investigating the horror incident show the co-pilot "assaulted the captain". Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has stated that he believes Iran may be connected to the co-pilot - a possibility which a senior Israeli official has confirmed has so far been ruled out.

Many questions remain as to what exactly happened in the sky this week, but the stories of jaw-dropping bravery have begun to emerge. Here, we look at the heroes who helped save the lives of more than 170 people on board...

Pint-sized hero

View 5 Images Nina Manes, 6, speaking to media in Tel Aviv (Image: X)

A courageous six-year-old girl and her mother sounded the alarm, unwittingly helping fellow passengers enter the cockpit as chaos unfolded.

Little Nina Manes asked mum Tali to accompany her to the bathroom, at the precise moment the co-pilot allegedly stabbed Indian captain Smit Machchhar, in an attempt to seize control over the plane.

It was then that Tali heard alarming sounds coming from the cockpit, making it clear that something was very wrong. Speaking later with the Israeli Channel 12, Tali recalled: "There was blood all over the cockpit and very, very sharp fighting moves."

"I screamed, ‘He is stabbing the pilot, he is stabbing the pilot, come help!’ People looked at me and didn’t understand.”

Alerted to the commotion, Nina’s father, Tzvika, ran to grab Nina from the bathroom. He remembered: “The shrieks of my daughters when the plane nosedived [are still with me]. They said, ‘Dad, we don’t want to die.’ [Their cries] were the triggers that caused me to run inside the cockpit.”

It was then that Tzvika and two other passengers rushed inside the cockpit, where they were thankfully able to neutralise the suspect, but not without a struggle.

Fearless dentist

View 5 Images Dr Shota Musaev was among those who bolted into the cockpit (Image: Getty Images)

Georgian Jewish dentist Dr Shota Musaev was among those who bolted into the cockpit, where the alleged extremist knifeman begged the have a go heroes to 'kill' him after being pinned down.

The 47-year-old told of how the seemingly ordinary flight descended into a nightmare. "Everything was going smoothly when, suddenly, we felt the aircraft drop sharply. We thought it was just turbulence."

"I took out my camera and started filming. Exactly half a minute later, we heard noises from the front: shouting, and a woman screaming, 'Knife! Knife!'. That was when I got up. I realised it was a terrorist attack and joined the people ahead of us, who were the first to rush into the cockpit and pull the terrorist out."

Dr Musaev told the Daily Mail that he and three other men "grabbed the attacker by the neck" and pulled him from the cockpit, binding him with headphone cords and plastic zip-ties. He continued: "We tied the terrorist up, binding his hands and feet. [The attacker said] nothing apart from begging us: 'Kill me'."

It was then that the group attended to the injured Captain Machchhar, thinking quickly to save his life. Dr Musaev remembered how the captain, who was "losing a lot of blood", begged, "Save me. I don't want to die here."

He said: "His arm was badly slashed, as was his neck, and he had a very deep wound at the back of his head. Everything in the cockpit was covered in blood, but he was conscious. We were effectively left without first-aid supplies. Somehow, we managed to stop the bleeding with pieces of cloth."

In a separate interview with CNN, Dr Musaev outlined the severity of Captain Machchhar's injuries, while highlighting just how close they came to complete catastrophe. He recalled: “He was covered in cuts – his head, his hands – they were practically sliced open, almost severed in two … he had lost a lot of blood and was in bad shape.

"I think that if we had waited even a few more moments, we would have lost him. His blood pressure had plummeted, he suddenly lost consciousness, and there was blood everywhere.”

‌



Dr Musaev, who had been travelling with his family, also praised his wife for her "tremendous strength" in the face of unimaginable terror. He explained: "My wife usually gets frightened quite easily, but at that moment she found tremendous strength and was helping absolutely everyone there, every single person.

"When we met Prime Minister Netanyahu today, people mentioned it there, too. Everyone said they had received the greatest possible psychological support from my wife."

Quick-thinking pilot

View 5 Images Thinking quickly, Captain Machchhar was able to open the cockpit door (Image: Smit Machchhar/LINKEDIN)

‌



Captain Machchhar thankfully survived his horror ordeal, having been airlifted from a hospital in the Saudi Arabian city of Tabuk, a city in north-western Saudi Arabia, to Abu Dhabi, where he remains in a stable condition.

He has since gone on to tell his side of the story, including how he managed to open the cockpit door so as to allow passengers to enter and stop what could have been a mass tragedy.

Speaking via video call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Captain Machchhar spoke of how he was on the ground, being allegedly attacked by the co-pilot when he realised the aircraft was plummeting. There was no time to waste.

‌



He revealed: "I was lying on the floor injured, but I told myself to go for one last push to open the door from inside. Others came in and also played a role [in controlling the situation]. I was, of course, fighting for my own life, but at the same time I knew I was not going to let others die."

Hailing Captain Machchhar as a hero in a post shared on X, Mr Modi wrote: "In the face of the gravest danger and despite being seriously ‌injured, he showed immense courage and an unwavering resolve to protect the lives of others. His valour helped save hundreds of lives and avert a great tragedy."

In another statement, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said: "My salute to the Indian pilot Captain Smit Machchhar for his extraordinary bravery. Despite being stabbed and seriously injured, he fought back… preventing a catastrophic mid-air disaster. He saved the lives of 174 people, including Israeli citizens and other nationals.”

‌



Brave plumber

View 5 Images Yaniv Hayoun's love of Aircraft Investigations proved highly useful (Image: Kobi Gideon/GPO)

Plumber Yaniv Hayoun was among those who rushed to defend his fellow passengers against the attacker, and amazingly, was reportedly able to regain control over the craft thanks to his love of the aviation TV show, Aircraft Investigations.

Speaking with Prime Minister Netanyahu, who greeted him with a hug at Tel Aviv airport, Yaniv told of how it was initially difficult to open the cockpit door, as the injured pilot was slumped against it. He explained: "I pushed the door; the pilot who was stabbed was simply very close to the door, so it was hard for us to open. We pulled him out – it was a matter of seconds.

‌



"We pinned him down to keep him secure, and then I jumped into it (the cockpit) and pulled the controls.” An off-duty pilot then advised Yaniv that he could take control from there. The plane dropped by more than 17,000ft (5,200m) before the plucky group managed to get back on course in the nick of time.

When asked by Mr Netanyahu how exactly he knew what to do with the controls, which included pulling in a backwards motion, Yaniv simply replied: “I watch Air Crash Investigations, Mr Prime Minister.”

News.title: 'Reassurance' for drivers UK can cope with Trump diesel ban threat amid fears of shortages and price hikes
News.content:
'Reassurance' for drivers UK can cope with Trump diesel ban threat amid fears of shortages and price hikes

A minister has taken to the airwaves to insist the UK's diesel supply chain is 'resilient' - despite the risk of Trump banning US exports and Europe considering tapping into emergency stocks

View 3 Images Transport minister Keir Mather has insisted diesel drivers would not face shortages even if there was a ban on US exports of the fuel (Image: Getty)

A government minister has insisted the UK could cope with President Trump's threatened ban on US diesel exports without it leading to shortages.

‌



‌



Transport minister Keir Mather sought to reassure Britain's near 10 million diesel drivers, as well as the countless hauliers that rely on diesel. Diesel drivers were already the hardest hit by a surge in pump prices since the start of the Iran war at the end of February this year. It follows a leap in oil prices due to the conflict, as well as a hit to refineries that convert oil into diesel.

‌



The nationwide average for diesel is within a whisker off the £2 a litre barrier, according to the RAC, a record high and with many forecourts selling the fuel for far more than that. It now costs almost £110 to fill-up an average diesel car, about £32 more a go than before the US-Iran war began.

‌



To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

View 3 Images The nationwide for diesel has jumped to almost £2 a litre - with some forecourts charging well over that (Image: Finnbarr Webster, Getty Images)

Tesco launches 8p off a litre fuel deal while fears grow over deepening diesel crisis READ MORE :

Fears diesel could be rationed as price of fuel hits record high READ MORE :

“I want to reassure people this morning that the United Kingdom has got a diverse range of supply when it comes to diesel," Mr Mather told Sky News. “We have resilience built into our system for that reason. We are working very closely with our US counterparts to stress the importance of that relationship, and the importance of sustaining flows of diesel around the world."

‌



He added that the government was in talks with other European countries, as well as through the International Energy Agency. Despite his attempt to calm fears, the UK remains worryingly exposed given its reliance on imports. That is because, unlike unleaded, the country now buys 55% of its road diesel from abroad, compared with just 14% in 2003. And nearly a third of Britain’s diesel imports came from the US last year - up from 18% the year before.

Britain has only about 40 days’ worth of diesel in reserve, one of the lowest levels in Europe, according to data from the International Energy Forum. The UK has held emergency talks with other European countries about the potential release of diesel reserves given President Trump's threat to ratchet-up the pressure on already strained stocks by banning on the export of US-produced diesel.

The potential move is widely seen as an attempt the Trump administration to try to lower pump prices in the States ahead of next month’s crunch mid-term elections. US Treasury secretary Scott Bessent said European countries should “immediately” begin to use their reserves.

‌



View 3 Images Donald Trump has said he was “thinking” about introducing a ban on exports of US diesel (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The looming diesel crisis threatens to get even worse after the UK’s biggest refinery has shut production for up to 10 weeks. Fawley refinery, in Hampshire, will be closed until November for maintenance, adding to concerns about the flow of fuel supplies across the country. The site, operated by ExxonMobil, makes almost one fifth of the fuel used on UK roads and also supplies jet fuel to Heathrow.

In 2025 alone, the closures of the Grangemouth refinery in Scotland and Lindsey refinery in Lincolnshire wiped out almost a quarter of total UK refining capacity. The average price of a litre of diesel in the UK stood at 199.79p on Thursday, according to figures compiled by the RAC. The previous record high was 199.09p, in June 2022, after Russia’s invasion of Ukraine.

‌



The UK, as a member of the International Energy Agency, is required to keep oil stocks equal to at least 90 days of net oil imports in reserve. It is thought these can be used to respond to severe supply disruptions in the global market.

Mr Trump has said he was “thinking” about introducing a ban on exports of US diesel. This would force Britain to compete with other countries for an alternative.

In a post on X on Thursday, Mr Bessent said: “Our European partners should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions. American farmers, truckers, and businesses should not be left carrying the burden of a global diesel shortage. America is doing its part. We look to our allies to match their commitments with action.”

Article continues below

EU member states will meet with European Commission on Friday to discuss the issue. Mr Mather was asked by Nick Ferrari on LBC whether he agreed with Mr Trump about Europe using their diesel reserves. He said: “We’re working closely with our European partners on diesel supply. It means we’re continuing those discussions about how we retain our resilience and robustness of our supply chains.

“President Trump is welcome to make those comments, we’ve got to focus here at home about ensuring that we have diversity of supply into our economy. Our European partners are absolutely central to that, particularly the flows of diesel coming through the Netherlands.”

News.title: Lone tenant is 'last man standing' as he refuses to give up home to make way for UK Universal theme park
News.content:
Lone tenant is 'last man standing' as he refuses to give up home to make way for UK Universal theme park

Ritchie Wood, 55, faces eviction from his rented cottage in Kempston Hardwick, Bedfordshire, after his landlord obtained a possession order. His home is one of 12 due to be demolished for the Universal UK theme park.

View 8 Images Ritchie Wood is the final resident on his street which has been earmarked for destruction to make way for the Universal United Kingdom Resort

A solitary tenant remains the final resident on a Bedfordshire street earmarked for demolition to pave the way for one of Europe's largest theme parks.

‌



‌



Ritchie Wood, 55, is holding out until the last possible moment before leaving Manor Road in Kempston Hardwick, Bedfordshire, as 12 properties are set to be flattened to accommodate the £5billion Universal United Kingdom Resort. Six properties have already been emptied, while a further five are understood to have sold their homes to Universal under non-disclosure agreements - with demolition scheduled for Christmas, according to an anonymous local.

‌



While the park has been championed by the Government as delivering "opportunity and long‐term prosperity for Britain", Ritchie is stubbornly refusing to vacate his three-bedroom cottage, which he has rented for 11 years.

‌



View 8 Images Homes on Manor Road in Kempston Hardwick, Beds, are set to be bulldozed for the new park

Chancellor John Healey urged to end housing benefit freeze hitting low-income families at Budget READ MORE :

To see more of the stories you love from The Mirror and to find them easily in Google then make us your preferred source. Free and easy-to-do, just click on the link here to find more from The Mirror at the top of your feed.

After receiving an eviction notice from his landlord earlier this year, Ritchie challenged the decision in court before being issued with a possession order earlier this month. Now Ritchie, who looks after his elderly parents living just six miles away, says he is awaiting the arrival of bailiffs following difficulties securing alternative accommodation.

‌



Ritchie, who believes his five remaining neighbours are preparing to sell up and relocate, said: "I've lived here for 11 years - this is my home and I have a life here. My parents are in their 80s and they live five minutes down the road. I want to stay close to them but I could end up anywhere.

View 8 Images Ritchie has rented his home for 11 years and has fought against leaving

‌



"It's been really hard to watch almost everyone move out of this street. It's heartbreaking. It's like living on borrowed time at the moment. Out of 70 million people in the country, I'm the only person facing homelessness out of this. I'm not being taken seriously and no one will speak to me.

"If you drive down Manor Road now, you would think it's private land owned by Universal Studios with the amount of traffic. I get looks from people driving down there, thinking 'who's that?'. I feel like an alien, intruding or trespassing."

Ritchie, who is staring down homelessness, was handed a Section 21 eviction notice on April 28 - mere days before the Renters' Rights Act 2025 took effect. He was given until July 1 to vacate, but Ritchie, who claimed Universal had been "bullying" his neighbours into selling their properties and moving out, sought legal counsel.

‌



View 8 Images Universal has started construction work right next to the properties

Ritchie, who previously worked in construction before ill health forced him to stop, also contacted his local authority, which he says told him to remain in the property to avoid being classified as intentionally homeless. He appeared in court earlier this month attempting to challenge the notice - however, a possession order was granted on September 19.

‌



Ritchie now says he's been told to stay put until bailiffs arrive to change the locks - as his appeals to the council for alternative accommodation have reached a brick wall. He claims his landlord has sold the property to Universal on the condition of his eviction, which he suspects was designed to circumvent the new Renters' Rights Act coming into effect.

Ritchie, who lives in a historic cottage that once housed brickworkers, said: "The Section 21 notice I was given was granted April 28th, just before new renter's rights came in. I sought legal advice to Legal Aid and I was told to sit tight until a court possession order. Last week, I went to Bedford Crown Court and the possession order was granted on the 19th of September.

View 8 Images Ritchie said he feels like a trespasser in his own home

‌



"I've been advised to wait until a bailiff warrant is approved by the court and then I get two weeks notice before they change the locks. And all this time, the council are telling me I'm at the bottom of the list for housing. It's not like I'm being paid to move by Universal. From a legal point of view, Universal haven't done anything wrong because they'll make sure everything is done to the letter. But from a moral perspective, their belligerence is unreal. They think we don't matter."

Demolition got underway this month as part of efforts to build the new 476-acre £50bn Universal theme park. Universal Destinations and Experiences runs theme parks and resorts across the globe, drawing on the catalogue of the entertainment conglomerate.

‌



View 8 Images Demolition to make space for the new park started this month

The company is perhaps best known for blockbuster film franchises such as Fast & Furious, Jurassic Park, and Despicable Me. The park could feature Europe's tallest rides, soaring to 377ft (115m), with completion scheduled for 2031.

‌



The development will encompass several themed lands, a 500-room hotel, plus retail, dining and entertainment, generating 20,000 jobs in the process. Plans involve demolishing 12 homes to clear space for the park and new dual carriageway - with Ritchie's current property sitting right in the middle.

Last year, residents revealed how they had been contacted by representatives with formal offers for their properties or enquiring whether they'd consider selling up. However, some refused to leave their cherished homes, which they said they'd purchased specifically for the village lifestyle and rural surroundings.

View 8 Images Ritchie's home, circled, is a historic cottage once used to house brickworkers

‌



Just five households now remain on Manor Road, and Ritchie said he feels like a "trespasser" along his country lane. He has also claimed he's sent roughly 70 emails to Universal begging for discussions - and even dispatched two letters via tracked delivery to their headquarters in Orlando.

Ritchie said: "In April last year, I was told the houses weren't part of the development and they were staying. But then different neighbours were contacted to say the houses were part of it and there was the view to demolish. I emailed Universal using on various addresses I found online or been told to contact but never heard back.

‌



"After pushing last summer, the contractor dealing with the houses said they would set up a meeting between me and Universal Studios as they acknowledged I'd lived there ten years. But at Christmas, I was told they were only going to deal with the landlord as Universal see it as the same as someone walking off street and buying the property outright.

View 8 Images Ritchie said he has already seen the impact of the works on local wildlife

‌



"I've emailed them between 50 to 70 times and I've never even had an acknowledgement of receipt. As last resort, I sent two letters recorded delivery to their headquarters in Orlando with full tracking for £32. They were signed for but, again, no response."

The developers had sought a 'Special Development Order' which could see them granted powers to compulsory purchase. Permission was granted in December 2025 which allowed the park to submit directly to the government and bypass local planning.

Part of Manor Road has been closed since July as part of 'site stabilisation and enabling works'. In a letter dispatched to residents in September concerning the roadworks, Universal stated they remained "committed to being a good neighbour".

Article continues below

Yet Ritchie said he felt completely overlooked. He added: "I think they've [my neighbours] accepted the inevitable that the houses will be demolished. It's sad.

"There's fields all around us and lakes round the back. I get lots of water voles in my garden now because animals are being forced out the land. We had a large grass snake in the road - all these animals have now got nowhere to go."

Universal Studios UK were contacted for comment.

News.title: Boy, 6, killed in Llanfairfechan crash as police arrest 39-year-old man
News.content:
Boy, 6, killed in Llanfairfechan crash as police arrest 39-year-old man

Emergency services rushed to an accident in Llanfairfechan, North Wales, where a six-year-old boy was tragically pronounced dead at the scene and a 39-year-old man was arrested

View 2 Images A boy has died following a collision in Llanfairfechan (Image: Google)

A six-year-old boy has tragically died after being hit by a vehicle in North Wales.

Emergency services rushed to the scene following reports of an accident involving a child in Llanfairfechan, shortly after 5pm on Thursday

Despite the best efforts of paramedics, he was pronounced dead at the scene. The family of the child are being supported by specially trained officers.

North Wales Police said a 39-year-old man has been arrested and is helping with police enquiries.

Detective Inspector Tim Evans from North Wales Police’s serious collision investigation unit said the thoughts of the force are with the family.

He appealed to anyone who saw the incident or may have dashcam footage to get in touch, reports WalesOnline.

View 2 Images A man has been arrested following the tragedy in Llanfairfechan (file) (Image: Ian Cooper/North Wales Live)

He stated: "Our thoughts are with the young boy's family and friends at this extremely difficult time.

"An investigation into the circumstances surrounding the collision is ongoing and we are appealing for anyone who witnessed the incident, or who may have dashcam footage from the area at the time, to contact us by calling 101, quoting reference O162122"

Hundreds of people have taken to social media to express their sadness at the tragedy.

"May this dear child rest in peace and we will pray for his family who must be devastated," wrote one person on Facebook, while another said: "My God! To everyone involved in this tragedy my thought are truely with you. I hope his parents will be able to see the outpouring of grief and the love. The people across North wales are currently thinking of you. X."

North Wales Police said: "North Wales Police were called shortly after 5pm this evening (Thursday 1 October) following reports of a collision involving a vehicle and a child in Llanfairfechan.

Article continues below

"Tragically, despite the best efforts of the emergency services, a six-year-old boy was pronounced dead at the scene.

"The family are being supported by specially trained Family Liaison Officers.

"A 39-year-old man has been arrested and is helping with Police enquiries."

News.title: Putin 'plotting huge attack on 3 nuclear plants' as terrifying Ukraine plan leaked
News.content:
Putin 'plotting huge attack on 3 nuclear plants' as terrifying Ukraine plan leaked

Leaked plans suggest Russia will strike Ukraine's power infrastructure and nuclear plants this winter in a dangerous bid to freeze its enemies into submission

View 3 Images The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Station has already been at the centre of heavy fighting (Image: AP)

Vladimir Putin is reportedly planning to freeze Ukrainians into submission this winter in a massive wave of strikes against several targets - including the country’s nuclear power infrastructure.

‌



‌



Officials in Kyiv are warning this could be the hardest winter of the war so far, with Russia using its increasingly powerful weapons to devastate Ukraine’s power grid ahead of the freezing months to come.

‌



Ukrainian authorities pointed to an attack on Wednesday as the start of Russia's winter campaign. A large thermal power plant and other energy facilities were struck in the capital Kyiv, leaving several neighbourhoods without power or water.

‌



But this is just the beginning, Ukrainian authorities have said, warning Russia plans a winter barrage using ballistic missiles and jet-powered drones that Ukrainian forces often struggle to intercept.

View 3 Images The warnings come after Ukrainian officials claimed to have intercepted Russian war plans (Image: POOL/AFP via Getty Images)

UK reveals 31 new Russia sanctions hitting Putin's war chest and child kidnap network READ MORE :

Ukrainian energy minister, Denys Shmyhal, reportedly showed an intercepted Russian war plan to European partners in Paris two weeks ago which included terrifying schemes to strike nuclear power plants.

‌



The plan, seen by the New York Times, is said to outline plans to collapse Ukraine’s power grid through sustained attacks. A campaign of strikes using up to 1,000 missiles, drones and bombs would target a wide range of facilities.

Electrical substations, hydroelectric and thermal power plants, and boiler houses would all be hit in an attempt to break morale and cripple the war effort.

Most worryingly of all, Russia would fire missiles with the aim of shutting down Ukraine’s three operating nuclear power stations, hitting electrical switchyards which connect the plants to the grid.

‌



View 3 Images The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant in Ukraine is Europe's largest (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

The switchyards are located less than a mile away from the reactors, meaning there is a serious risk of a disastrous meltdown in the event of a strike missing its target even slightly.

Moscow also has plans to fire dozens of ballistic missiles and glide bombs at Ukraine’s water system, Mr Shmyhal reportedly told European partners in Paris. This would represent the first such large-scale attack by Russia on Ukraine’s water network.

Article continues below

The Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant - Europe's largest - has been at the centre of heavy fighting throughout the war. The nuclear plant passed into Russian hands in March 2022 after repeated strikes on or near the facility.

Since then strikes on the area have also been carried out by Ukrainian Armed Forces, with a driver killed by a drone strike at the site in April. In May, the International Atomic Energy Agency was informed that a lab at the plant had been hit.

News.title: Your rights explained as PIP review changes to be shared by Andy Burnham government
News.content:
Your rights explained as PIP review changes to be shared by Andy Burnham government

Andy Burnham's government will be sharing the results of The Timms Review, which is set to overhaul the way people gain from the UK's main disability benefit

View 3 Images Andy Burnham's government are making changes to PIP (Image: Zeynep Demir Aslim/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

Andy Burnham's government is set to shared the results of a huge review the UK's main disability benefit, the Personal Independence Payment (PIP) - and people are looking into their rights when it comes to the benefit. A major review on the future of PIP is set to be handed to the government in November, with its content expected to explain how the non-means-tested system should be overhauled.

‌



‌



The government launched The Timms Review in October 2025 to ensure PIP is fair and fit for the future, and helps support disabled people to achieve better health, higher living standards and greater independence, including through employment.

‌



How much money people get through the scheme depends on how many points they get, based on how much their condition affects daily life.

‌



PIP supports many people with a disability or long-term health condition, and the government has said it is committed to ensuring it remains a non-means-tested cash benefit for people both in and out of work.

View 3 Images The Department for Work & Pensions sign outside Caxton House in Whitehall (Image: Andrew Aitchison, In Pictures via Getty Images)

However, people are worried that a possible overhaul could result in it becoming more difficult for people with certain conditions to claim, or cuts for some households.

‌



Applications and payments through PIP have ballooned over the years, which has largely been put down to younger adults claiming for conditions like anxiety, depression and ADHD. It's understood these claimants could be targeted in the disability benefits overhaul, expected in 2027.

This has led to people on PIP looking into their rights to see what could happen under a PIP overhaul.

What are your rights if you are already receiving PIP?

The Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) can currently stop or reduce your PIP payment over a handful of reasons. These include people railing to return review forms or missing a telephone assessment or face-to-face interview without a good reason.

‌



Another reason PIP could be removed is if the health condition a person is claiming for improves significantly at a scheduled reassessment and they no longer meet the points threshold.

View 3 Images There are currently a number of reasons PIP can be removed or reduced (Image: Getty Images )

The benefit can also be changed or removed if the person claiming the benefit moves abroad or goes into certain types of NHS-funded or residential care for a long period.

Article continues below

Benefits could also be reduced or stopped if somebody receiving PIP fails to report and change in circumstances, is accused of benefit fraud or the DWP takes back a benefit overpayment.

If a person claiming PIP is not sure why the DWP stopped or reduced their payment, they should check any letters the DWP have sent you or call the PIP enquiry line and ask them to explain.

News.title: Lloyds customers cut cost of heating by signing up to new offer by October 12
News.content:
Lloyds customers cut cost of heating by signing up to new offer by October 12

The offer, which is designed to help customers save money on their heating bills, is available now until October 12

View 2 Images Lloyds and E.ON Next launch 24 months exclusive fixed energy tariff (Image: Getty)

Lloyds is giving its customers access to an exclusive fixed energy tariff of £1,697 a year for 24-months from E.ON Next. The offer, available now via the Bill Switcher section in the Rewards Hub in the Lloyds app until October 12, is said to provide customers with certainty around the cost of household energy.

‌



‌



From October 1, the energy price cap rises, taking the average annual bill for a typical household with both gas and electricity, paying by Direct Debit, to £1,723, and forecasts suggest the January price cap could be £2,065. Actual bills will vary depending on how much energy a household uses.

‌



In addition, the first 1,000 eligible customers applying for the energy deal will receive an Amazon voucher. The voucher will be worth £25 for customers switching both gas and electricity, and £10 for those switching just one.

‌



Chris Butt, Head of Rewards Partnerships at Lloyds, said: "As colder weather approaches, many households will be looking for ways to keep their energy bills down. This exclusive tariff offers customers more certainty over what they will pay towards their bills.

View 2 Images The price cap went up at the start of this month

"Customers can also make their money go further with Lloyds Rewards, which offers a host of offers, cashback, and a range of activities to earn rewards. They can also use the Bill Switcher service, which makes it easy to compare household bills and find a better deal."

‌



What is Bill Switcher?

Together with ApTap, Lloyds created Bill Switcher, a free service in the Rewards hub in the Lloyds app, which helps customers check whether they could pay less for their broadband, mobile phone or energy. Since launching Bill Switcher, Lloyds says it has helped customers save more than £359,000 in energy and broadband deals.

Customers can use it to compare providers, see alternative deals and switch to a new supplier if they find an option that suits them. The service is found in the tools section of the Rewards Hub.

Article continues below

What is Lloyds Rewards?

Lloyds describes its Lloyds Rewards as a dedicated space in the Lloyds app where customers can browse cashback offers and perks available to them. This includes up to 15% cashback when shopping at selected retailers with an eligible Lloyds debit or credit card. Customers activate an offer in the app, then shop as normal in-store or online.

The Rewards space also offers prize draws and simple challenges. Lloyds is currently running a Super Prize Draw, giving away thousands of pounds in cash prizes, including a £1 million top prize in November.

Customers can see the prize draws available to them and, depending on the draw, enter with a tap or complete a simple action to earn an entry. Challenges can be taken on to unlock further rewards

News.title: Budget airline Ryanair cancels 1,000 flights and 'collapse' is blamed
News.content:
Budget airline Ryanair cancels 1,000 flights and 'collapse' is blamed

Ryanair gave an update on Friday morning

View 3 Images Ryanair has consistently railed against Nats (Image: Mrkit99 via Getty Images)

Budget carrier Ryanair has issued an update, confirming that it cancelled 1,000 flights.

‌



‌



It partly attributed the recent "collapse" of Britain's air traffic control system for the scrapping more than 1,000 flights in September. The Irish airline said the cancellations stemmed from two separate air traffic control (ATC) failures within a fortnight of one another last month, alongside ATC strikes in Belgium and widespread disruption across Europe caused by volcanic ash clouds from eruptions at Mount Etna.

‌



The head of Britain's National Air Traffic Services (Nats), Martin Rolfe, has faced mounting calls to quit following a string of air traffic failures that led to thousands of flight cancellations across the industry last month, leaving hundreds of thousands of passengers stranded.

‌



View 3 Images Budget airline Ryanair has partly blamed the recent ‘collapse’ in Britain’s air traffic control system for cancelling more than 1,000 flights in September (Image: Gareth Fuller/PA)

The most recent incident was triggered by a "connectivity issue" at its Prestwick centre in Scotland, which was unrelated to an ATC software fault on September 8 that sparked widespread travel chaos.

Ryanair has been among those demanding Mr Rolfe's resignation, while Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander has arranged a meeting with Nats chairman Sir Warren East, the former chief executive of Rolls-Royce, in the coming weeks to address the ongoing issues.

‌



Latest Ryanair figures

Ryanair's most recent traffic statistics revealed the airline operated over 111,700 flights last month, carrying 20.1 million passengers, a rise of 4% year on year. Wizz Air also released passenger data showing a 24% increase year on year in passengers flown last month, reaching 7.78 million, with capacity up 25.3%.

Yet Wizz announced recently it would slash its flight schedule by 5% over the second half of 2026 owing to broader Iran war pressures on the travel sector and spiralling fuel costs.

Following the latest disruption, easyJet said it “calls into question the resilience of Nats’ systems” and Jet2 said customers and airlines need “action, accountability and proper resilience”.

‌



View 3 Images Ryanair was hit by the Nats problems (Image: Will Meaking/PA)

Calls to resign

On September 21, chief operations officer for Ryanair Neal McMahon said: “Martin Rolfe has presided over repeated system failures, repeated passenger disruption and repeated failures to deliver an effective back-up system.

“Enough is enough. Martin Rolfe should resign today.”

Article continues below

Tim Alderslade, chief executive of industry body Airlines UK, said ATC was “critical national infrastructure” which “must be resilient enough to keep people moving”.

He added: “Yet another Nats failure is causing delays and disruption for passengers and airlines alike, and comes just days after its report into the most recent major outage. Passengers and airlines deserve better and the independent CAA (Civil Aviation Authority) report, together with the forthcoming Civil Aviation Bill, must address the underlying weaknesses in the system so that these failures stop happening."

News.title: Man City verdict has 'significant implications for integrity of the game', says FA
News.content:
The independent commission's verdict against Manchester City has "significant implications for the integrity of the game", according to the Football Association.

In a statement, English football's governing body added: "We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate."

The FA's statement comes after it was confirmed on Tuesday that City were found guilty of all charges relating to breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations between the 2009-10 and 2017-18 seasons.

City have repeatedly denied guilt, and have until Friday to lodge an appeal.

"As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage," the FA added.

"We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely."

Sources told BBC Sport that City were expected to claim that key sponsorship deals were funded by the Abu Dhabi government, rather than the club's owners, as part of an appeal.

Among the independent panel's findings were that City arranged "sham contracts" with a number of commercial partners as part of a scheme to disguise secret funding of more than Â£830m.

The Premier League says City "systematically broke Premier League Rules for nearly a decade".
