Sports.title: The Premier League played their part in Man City mess and still have questions to answer
Sports.content:
The Premier League played their part in Man City mess and still have questions to answer

The Premier League are getting plenty of credit for their devastating Manchester City statement - but why were they allowed to get away with it for so long?

View 3 Images Premier League CEO Richard Masters is earning plenty of plaudits - but huge questions remain (Image: Getty Images)

The Premier League is getting plenty of plaudits for the brutal takedown of Manchester City. Understandably so.

‌



‌



But the Premier League is always at pains to stress the independent commission is exactly that. Independent.

‌



If I were allowed, I would give the three members of the commission the public accolades they deserve. It was obviously a monumentally difficult case but there has clearly been no compromise.

‌



The commission laid bare cheating on a quite remarkable scale. Across the nine seasons from 2009/10 to 2017/18, City claimed commercial income of £949.94 million when only £119.25 million had come from sponsors.

It really is staggering. Just because the rules were lousy, it does not mean a club had a licence to treat them with impunity.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

There are 7,000 pages to the verdict but the sins are quite simple. City created sham commercial agreements to falsify their revenue so they could spend more on players without breaching the Premier League’s financial regulations.

In fact, the sins are so basic and of such magnitude that they beg some simple questions.

‌



How did City get away with it for so long? How come the Premier League did not smell a rat? Did the Premier League - and other executives - simply turn a blind eye?

In 2009/10, City’s recorded sponsorship income was £27million. In 2012/13, City claimed their sponsorship income was £121.75million.

View 3 Images Man City's achievements and Premier League dominance are now tainted

‌



It is hard to believe no-one in the Premier League’s headquarters - where there is supposedly a compliance unit - considered this jump in sponsorship income to be odd.

And it kept rising, until in 2017/18 it stood at £145.73million, only £11million of which was actually paid by sponsors. The rest was owners’ money.

Yet there was no sign of any Premier League investigation. As we all know, the investigation was only prompted by the Portuguese hacker Rui Pinto and his Football Leaks website, which published internal emails from City detailing schemes by the club to cover up true sources of income in a bid to comply with financial fair play regulations.

‌



Look, City are the culprits in the worst example of systemic cheating in the history of British sport. The punishment has to be draconian. But the Premier League has played its part in a mess so damaging that it is hard to know where to start.

Somehow, City’s cheating on an industrial scale went unnoticed for those nine seasons. The abnormal length of the investigation meant another eight full seasons passed.

View 3 Images Man City have won eight league titles since 2012 (Image: (Photo by Michael Regan/Getty Images))

‌



And now this. So, essentially, almost two decades of the Premier League has been - to use the stand-out word of the organisation’s statement on the City verdict - a sham.

You cannot separate the nine seasons that were investigated from the eight seasons that followed.

As much as the players will protest, the team that will run out at Anfield on Sunday week cannot be separated from the ones that have won titles over the past two decades.

Article continues below

It is some mess. And it is, of course, City’s fault. Spectacularly and grimly so. But the Premier League has little to be proud of either.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Andy Burnham's new statement and 'evidence' to appeal guilty verdict
Sports.content:
Manchester City's appeal deadline is today after the club were found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog covering the fallout from the Premier League's guilty verdict on Manchester City for Friday, October 2.

The pressure is being cranked up on the Premier League club with their deadline for an appeal today. The Treasury Committee, which is responsible for overseeing policies and administration of His Majesty's Revenue and Customs, have asked whether the government department has requested the redacted documents contained within the commission's report.

The Premier League announced earlier this week that City had been found guilty of 114 charges brought against them for financial breaches.

City responded by maintaining their innocence and have until the end of today to launch an appeal, with the club expected to do so before the deadline.

Their top-flight rivals are said to be readying legal action against them to the tune of £800million, while a cross-party group of MPs have urged HMRC to investigate the tax implications of the Premier League's charges.

It now remains to be seen what punishment is given to City, with reports claiming that chiefs at other football clubs want a sanction to be imposed before the end of the season.

Etihad, the main shirt sponsor for City, meanwhile, have also issued a statement in response saying they are "deeply concerned" by the Premier League's announcement. There are also concerns that City's Abu Dhabi owners could be stripped from the club, something Prime Minister Andy Burnham doesn't want to happen.

City are now set to argue that the government of Abu Dhabi - not the club's owners - part-funded the "sham" sponsorship deals that contributed to them breaching Premier League financial rules.

Stay tuned for the latest news and updates in our live blog below as the saga continues to unfold...

Sports.title: Liverpool news: Jurgen Klopp comments on Man City's 115 charges as Alexander Isak gets message
Sports.content:
Liverpool news: Jurgen Klopp comments on Man City's 115 charges as Alexander Isak gets message

The latest Liverpool news sees Alexander Isak subject to discussion from a former Reds hero

View 3 Images Alexander Isak has been back in form this season (Image: Getty)

There's little over a week until Liverpool return to Premier League duty against Manchester City. Andoni Iraola's side will become the first team to play the league leaders since they were found guilty of breaching the top-flight's financial rules.

‌



‌



Such a matchup seems fitting given the Reds finished twice in two of the seasons that City captured the title during the nine-year period between 2009 and 2018. On top of the dramatic narrative that comes with the clash, both sides are unbeaten in the league, with Liverpool on two wins compared to City's five.

‌



The international break is heading into its third and final week as Alexander Isak has been handed an eye-opening verdict over his start to the season. Meanwhile, Jurgen Klopp has revealed his stance on the biggest story in football right now.

‌



Mirror Football takes a look at the latest stories coming out of Anfield...

Isak paying back

View 3 Images Alexander Isak has been on fire this season (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

It's been a return to form for Alexander Isak this season after an injury-hit debut season at Anfield. The Swede became Liverpool's most expensive player ever when they signed him for £125million last season but was struck by fitness issues and managed just four goals in 22 games across all competitions.

‌



The 27-year-old has already matched that record this season solely in the Premier League, with four goals in five games. Isak's potency in front of goal and his improved performances has former Reds striker Emile Heskey believing he's finally showing the form that made Liverpool fork out a nine-figure fee for his services.

Ian Wright demands 'unprecedented' Man City punishment after Premier League statement READ MORE :

"I'm not sure about what to add to his game because he is what he is," Heskey told Rekatochklart.com. "I like his movement. He's getting chances, and creating chances. You're going to miss some anyway. I love the runs that he's making. He looks sharper now, like he was when he was at Newcastle.

"That comes with games, the more and more you play. I like his movement, I like his runs. I think he's coming back to his best now because people are seeing him making the runs now. The second goal against Ipswich where he made the run in behind for Cody Gakpo who passed it with the outside of his boot.

‌



"If you go back a little bit, just before he makes that run for Gakpo, he's made a run for Virgil (van Dijk) who doesn't play it. He turns around and he's like throwing his hands around and then he realises Gakpo's got it, and he comes back onside and makes the second run."

Klopp's Guardiola verdict

View 3 Images Jurgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola enjoyed countless battles in the Premier League (Image: Getty Images)

Jurgen Klopp admitted his reluctance to comment on Manchester City being found guilty of serious financial breaches stems from the respect he has for Pep Guardiola. Despite being found guilty of 114 of the 115 charges by an independent commission, the club insist they are innocent.

‌



The two legendary managers enjoyed a healthy rivalry for years, with their former clubs having gone head-to-head in numerous thrilling title races. Despite previously joking he'd attend a parade if the Reds were retrospectively awarded titles, Klopp admitted he no longer holds this view.

FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

The Germany boss said: "I haven't given it much thought, even though I've seen it of course. I also know what I said about it in the past and how if there's ever a parade I'll be there, but it doesn't feel like that anymore.

Article continues below

"My respect for Pep Guardiola and the football played at City during the time we played against each other... plus what an opponent they proved to be for us at the very highest level is far too great for me to be able to say anything now."

Sports.title: Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford 'issue' raised as fresh transfer instruction sent
Sports.content:
Man Utd news: Marcus Rashford 'issue' raised as fresh transfer instruction sent

Manchester United star Marcus Rashford's form has been discussed and a club legend has sent the club a transfer instruction

View 2 Images Marcus Rashford has been a regular for Manchester United since returning to the club this summer (Image: Marc Atkins/Getty Images)

Manchester United continue to capture attention during the international break. Michael Carrick has just over a week until his side returns to action against Tottenham Hotspur on October 10.

‌



‌



United signed off for the extended break with a disappointing draw to Fulham and the club have since suffered injury blows. Noussair Mazraoui recently became the third member of Carrick’s team to sustain a fitness issue while on international duty, joining Bruno Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu.

‌



Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford were both initially included in Thomas Tuchel’s England squad but the duo opted to withdraw due to injury concerns. Rashford has regularly featured for United this term since returning from his Barcelona spell but club legend Wayne Rooney has outlined why he believes the forward is yet to hit top form.

‌



Meanwhile, United icon Rio Ferdinand has called upon the Red Devils to sign a free agent to help bolster Carrick’s squad. Here, Mirror Football looks at some of the biggest stories surrounding United.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Marcus Rashford 'issue' highlighted

Rooney has refused to pin Rashford’s lack of goals this season on the 28-year-old managing a hip issue. Instead, the club’s all-time top scorer has argued that the issue impacting Rashford’s output is his role in the team, with the England international yet to record a goal or assist in six appearances.

‌



“No, because I actually think he has done OK in games and he has looked lively and in some games he hasn’t,” Rooney said on the Stick to United podcast. “But I think in some of the games, he has actually looked quite lively and sharp.

“I think the issue is he’s too far away from goal. That’s the issue why he’s not scoring or creating.

“He’s playing too wide. He’s playing too deep at times. With Marcus Rashford, with good attacking players who can score goals, you want to get them as close to the goal as possible, and I don’t think he’s close enough to the goal.”

‌



View 2 Images Veteran striker Karim Benzema is a free agent after leaving Al Hilal (Image: Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images)

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Man Utd transfer instruction issued

United legend Rio Ferdinand has suggested the club should sign former Real Madrid icon Karim Benzema as a free agent, given the club’s lack of recognised strikers. Benjamin Sesko is yet to start a league game this season and missed the Fulham draw with a shin issue, which prompted him to withdraw from the Slovenia squad.

‌



Matheus Cunha has been deployed as a centre forward and Carrick also has Joshua Zirkzee at his disposal but Ferdinand feels that United could benefit from adding Benzema’s experience to the squad. The 38-year-old has been available on a free transfer since leaving Al Hilal this summer, having scored 10 goals in 16 games for the club.

“If you knew you had to manage his [Sesko] minutes, I totally agree with you. Without him, there isn’t really a focal point,” Ferdinand said on his YouTube channel when discussing United’s need for another striker. “We’ve got players that want to come deep to the ball more often than not and get involved in the build-up, and then you lose that focal point out there.

“But if you had somebody up there who could share the minutes, share the load, help in terms of experience, lend that experience to Sesko for him to learn as well, you’d have been getting so much more out of just a signing to go and play the 90 minutes.

Article continues below

“Welbeck springs to mind, obviously, so does Benzema. Two players I feel would have added huge value to the forward line that we have.”

Sports.title: Arsenal news: Haaland transfer stance becomes clear as cheap £9m bargain eyed
Sports.content:
Arsenal news: Haaland transfer stance becomes clear as cheap £9m bargain eyed

Another week of international duty remains for Arsenal players before they return to north London to continue their Premier League campaign

View 3 Images Arsenal are reportedly keen on a shock swoop for Erling Haaland (Image: Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta has another week to wait before Arsenal host Leeds United in the Premier League. The extended international break continues with 16 players away representing their countries.

‌



‌



Five Arsenal stars were initially called up to Thomas Tuchel's England squad before Declan Rice withdrew as he prioritises recovering from a congested fixture list.

‌



Arteta is currently sweating over the fitness of Martin Odegaard, Ezri Konsa and Kai Havertz, with the latter forced off against the Netherlands with a hamstring issue. It is thought that the club are optimistic there are no long-term injury concerns for the German.

‌



Here, Mirror Football has the latest headlines coming out of the Emirates Stadium.

Haaland transfer stance becomes clear

Erling Haaland has been tentatively linked with a move to Arsenal should Manchester City be removed from the Premier League. TEAMtalk claim the Gunners will assess the situation should the Norwegian forward become available.

However, the same publication claims that the player has not given thought to leaving the Etihad Stadium and he is fully focused on challenging for the Premier League title this year.

‌



Haaland's Norway team-mate Kristoffer Ajer claims the prolific striker has not been affected by the verdict and is not considering a transfer. The Brentford defender said: "He’s been exactly the way he’s always the same with the national team. He’s truly focused on the upcoming games. I think he’s trying to do the same as everyone else, wait and see what the outcome is...that’s clearly been his way of doing it."

View 3 Images Haaland's current transfer situation has been made clear regarding Arsenal's potential pursuit (Image: Grzegorz Wajda/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images)

When asked about Haaland's demeanour changing, Ajer added: "No not at all. Ever since I met him brings lot of energy and joy to the group. The biggest compliment I always give is that he hasn’t changed a bit from the moment I met him even though he’s the biggest star on the planet right now.

‌



"He’s been exactly the same the last few days as well which is not a surprise for me."

£9m bargain eyed

View 3 Images Breno Sales has caught the eye of the Gunners (Image: Martín Fonseca/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images)

Arsenal have reportedly joined Chelsea and City in monitoring Vasco da Gama youngster Breno Sales. The 16-year-old has attracted attention from across Europe, with a bid of almost £9million recently rejected, according to reports in Brazil.

Article continues below

The defender began his career as a striker before switching to left-back and later moving into a more central position. This year, Sales has made 17 appearances and scored once.

He won the U17 Copa do Brazil last year and has become a regular in the Brazilian national team's youth set-up. The teenager is expected to be involved in the upcoming U17 World Cup in Qatar next month, giving Premier League sides another opportunity to weigh up a potential move.

Sports.title: Alejandro Garnacho decision slammed after £43m Chelsea transfer details come to light
Sports.content:
Alejandro Garnacho decision slammed after £43m Chelsea transfer details come to light

Manchester United and Chelsea outcast Alejandro Garnacho has had a tough start to life at Aston Villa with criticism continuing to be issued to the winger

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho has been handed another harsh verdict after Aston Villa struggles (Image: (Photo by Stewart Kendall/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images))

Alejandro Garnacho has been brutally slammed yet again for his attitude after another challenging start to a new part of his career. The Argentine joined Aston Villa on a season-long loan from Chelsea, which includes a £43million obligation-to-buy under certain conditions, despite only arriving at Stamford Bridge from Manchester United in the summer of 2025.

‌



‌



Unai Emery is believed to have been an admirer of Garnacho for some time but is yet to hand him a Premier League start despite Villa's injury problems with fellow new arrival Johan Manzambi only making his first start against Tottenham.

‌



Garnacho has only played 31 minutes in the Premier League having remained an unused substitute in both Champions League and Carabao Cup action.

‌



For the buy-option included in his loan to become permanent, he has to make a certain number of appearances and that is already in jeopardy. It has also come to light there is also no break clause in his temporary switch which would allow Chelsea to bring him back in January.

England confirm injury blow as star becomes sixth player to withdraw from squad READ MORE :

Even if that was a possibility, it would seem unlikely given his performances last season for the Blues. Garnacho was often criticised for his work ethic and those complaints have not dissipated since his exit, with former Villa striker Dean Saunders making his feelings clear.

He said, via Svea Casino: “If I’m being honest, I’m not a fan of Alejandro Garnarcho and his attitude. Look at what happened with him and Manchester United.

‌



“When you look at his talent and ability, when I was playing football and we had talented players come in to train with us or sign for us, talent alone didn’t impress me. I wasn't impressed by people who can do tricks, juggle a ball and beat three men.

“I was more impressed with people who were hard to play against, like Jamie Lawrence, who I played with at Bradford. No one liked playing against Jamie. He'd run through a brick wall, tackle someone, chase back, and defend.

View 2 Images Alejandro Garnacho has only made three substitute appearances for Aston Villa

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

“Some players have nowhere near the talent of Garnacho, but I’d be more impressed with someone who turns up every week, gives a seven-out-of-10 performance, works hard defensively, and provides quality in the final third.

“We can all do tricks and skills, but that consistent work rate is what you’re getting paid for. To be honest, I was surprised Villa signed him.”

Article continues below

There is still plenty of time for Garnacho to be a success at Villa Park and it may have helped that he scored in a behind-closed-doors friendly against Southampton last week.

Emery's side return to Premier League action against Brentford later this month before facing Fenerbahce and Viking in the Champions League. They will also face Newcastle and Aston Villa in the league and Bournemouth in the Carabao Cup.

Sports.title: Bristol Rovers coach Paul Raynor reveals cancer diagnosis and sends powerful message
Sports.content:
Bristol Rovers coach Paul Raynor reveals cancer diagnosis and sends powerful message

Paul Raynor, who is assistant to Steve Evans at League Two club Bristol Rovers, was diagnosed with bowel cancer after doctors discovered a tumour following tests

View 2 Images Paul Raynor (Image: Rachel Le Poidevin/PPAUK/Shutterstock)

Bristol Rovers assistant manager Paul Raynor has revealed that he has sadly been diagnosed with bowel cancer. Raynor, 60, will start undergoing chemotherapy and radiotherapy this month, vowing to 'try and beat this' in an inspiring response.

‌



‌



The ex-Swansea City midfielder was told by doctors that the cancer had not spread to any major organs and that the chances of success were high. Raynor, who also played for Nottingham Forest, Preston North End and Cambridge United in his 25-year playing career, submitted a sample after being convinced to by his wife, Karen.

‌



"I was a typical man and left it, with my wife badgering me into doing it," he explained. "So I did it and a week later I was told there was an abnormal reading, and I had to go in for a full check. Within an hour, I was sat with a consultant and being told they had found a tumour."

‌



Raynor plans to tackle the disease with all his strength and vowed: "We're going to try and beat this. We will beat this and then be back on the grass helping the guys later in the season with a bit of luck.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



"The plan is I'm going to be here as much as possible. I'm going to be there on matchdays, and I aim to be and I want to be. If I'm well enough, I certainly will be."

The Nottingham-born coach joined Bristol Rovers in December 2025 when Steve Evans was appointed manager. Rovers avoided relegation to the National League last season and have started well this term, sitting third in the League Two table and level on points with leaders Barnet.

The pair have worked together at nine clubs including Rotherham United, Leeds United and Stevenage, and Raynor says that Evans' support has been 'immense'. "I've known and worked with the gaffer for 25 years and he's a massive friend and these last few weeks he's been absolutely immense but everyone has," Raynor added.

‌



View 2 Images Paul Raynor has praised Steve Evans for his support (Image: Jacques Feeney/Getty Images)

The 60-year-old also paid tribute to his wife and urged anyone who is concerned about a cancer diagnosis to get tested. "If it wasn't for my good lady, Karen, I wouldn't have sent the sample off and it could've been too late and the ramifications could be anything," Raynor continued.

"They're telling me there's a good chance it's curable but if I hadn't done that sample it could've been a lot, lot worse. The message is: get your samples done, whatever tests you need go and get it done because it's massively important."

Sports.title: No.10 issues statement after Andy Burnham slammed for 'backing' Man City owners
Sports.content:
No.10 issues statement after Andy Burnham slammed for 'backing' Man City owners

Andy Burnham has been criticised for saying that he'd be 'really concerned' if Manchester City's owners sold the club after they were found guilty of breaching Premier League rules

View 2 Images Andy Burnham received backlash for his comments (Image: Ian Forsyth/Getty Images)

Downing Street has issued a statement after Prime Minister Andy Burnham was accused of 'backing' Manchester City's under-fire owners. City were found guilty of 114 breaches of the Premier League's financial rules between 2009 and 2018, with an independent commission finding them to have inflated revenue and reduced costs by £900million, handed out 'sham' contracts and misstated accounts over the nine-year period.

‌



‌



The club strongly deny the charges and say that there is a 'comprehensive body of irrefutable evidence' that proves their innocence. Should City fail to win in their appeal, it's been speculated that their Abu Dhabi owners, including Sheikh Mansour, could be forced to sell the club.

‌



Asked if he was worried about such an outcome, Burnham - formerly the Mayor of Greater Manchester - told the BBC on Wednesday: "I would be really concerned to lose them.

‌



"They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester. Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is."

FOLLOW OUR MAN CITY FB PAGE! Follow our Manchester City Mirror Football Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Everton fan Burnham was hit with widespread backlash for his comments, prompting Downing Street to issue a statement on Thursday night. A No.10 spokesperson said: "The Prime Minister made clear the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules.

"He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected. If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences."

The statement was later tweaked to say: "Whenever wrongdoing is established." Burnham added in his interview that he expects his dealings with City while he was Mayor to stand up to potential scrutiny.

‌



"Oh indeed," the PM affirmed. "I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn't just put into the Etihad and the campus around it but also into the city, but yes of course."

Did Andy Burnham get it wrong? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Andy Burnham dealt with Manchester City's owners as Mayor of Greater Manchester (Image: PAUL ELLIS/AFP via Getty Images)

‌



After making it clear that he won't be 'getting directly involved in the process', Burnham went on to say: "I have to keep my distance from it. It would be wrong for me to do anything else.

"It's an independent legal process that has to play its course through ... There's a lot at stake. Let's be honest about that, for the football club, for city supporters, for the city of Manchester."

Among those to criticise Burnham were members of the Conservative Party. Shadow minister for sport Louie French commented: "Burnham is publicly backing the owners even as the investigation continues.

Article continues below

"Fans will rightly ask whether political pressure is being applied here and how it relates to the owners' well-reported investments in Manchester. Football must be governed independently, with the rules applying equally to everyone."

Sports.title: 'They'll be hating each other!' - Nelson: Don’t let AJ and Fury smiles fool you!
Sports.content:
Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury's smiles and respect will be replaced by a boiling rivalry when their fight gets closer, says Sky Sports Boxing's Johnny Nelson.

The British heavyweight rivals traded a few taunts but also shared words of mutual respect at their long-awaited first press conference in London on Wednesday evening.

But Sky Sports expert Nelson believes their first media meeting was just a "soft launch" and expects real animosity to appear ahead of their blockbuster battle in Cardiff on December 11, penning his thoughts below...

"I think after all these years of all the back-and-forth and Tyson calling him every name under the sun and AJ being super cool and Eddie Hearn saying what he's saying, I thought when they sat in front of each other on Wednesday, if I'm honest - maybe I got taken away with all the hype - but I thought there was really going to be a real ruckus.

"But they were like a couple of businessmen that went there to say: 'Right, we're going to tick all the boxes.'

"I'm quite sure, as the weeks roll on, you can compare it to a 100-metre sprint.

"It's 10 weeks to go, so this first week, it's niceties. I think as we get to 20 metres down the line, it will get a bit tighter and tighter, and then by the time we're at 50 metres, these guys will be champing at the bit, hating on each other. That's probably what they have to do.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the best bits from the Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua press conference

"I think the public might have been a little subdued Wednesday because of all the back-and-forth they've seen previously. So they thought: 'Let's see if this is for real.'

"The build-up to this fight as the weeks roll on, the words will get worse. Tyson's potty mouth will get in the way and things will be said, litigation and threats and everything.

"Even up until the first bell goes, it is going to be drama. This is what this fight's got written all over it.

"So that was a soft launch of what to expect.

"I think the smiling shocked everybody. Only because, as I said, of what we've seen in the build-up and everything.

"It's like a kettle boiling and thinking: 'Right, they're finally in the room together.' For the first time we've seen them head-to-head, these guys were just grown up.

"They were boys, now they're men. They've got children, they've got responsibilities. So now they probably conduct themselves a little better, but they'll turn back into boys again as it gets closer to the fight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fury and Joshua come together in a face-off ahead of their fight on December 11

"I do expect Fury to come out and have a tear-up. The last person he said that about was Deontay Wilder, and he did.

"I know Tyson Fury thinks Anthony Joshua isn't good going backwards.

"I don't think Joshua wants this fight to go the distance where it depends on Fury's boxing skills, because boxing Fury is like trying to hit with a bag of rice, so I'd be very surprised if the fight went past five rounds.

"But for five rounds, it will be drama.

"There'll be rocks, people will be hitting the canvas; it's going to be absolute drama.

'Both are past their prime - fight should have happened five years ago'

"I do think they're both past their prime.

"I've always been an AJ fan. I've always thought AJ would do him, but looking at the last fight of both fighters, the one that's got a little more left is Fury. AJ looked vulnerable.

"He looked susceptible. He looked like he could be hurt. And Tyson may not look as sharp and on point as he did 10 years ago, as he did when he boxed Wilder the first time.

"These guys are a lot older but it's whose style suits an older age. Fury's style suits the older age, whereas Joshua's style, if you don't hit him, he's going to hit you and take you out. So I have to say, it leans towards Fury at this stage in their careers.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Joshua makes his predictions to Sky Sports for his fight against Fury on December 11

"But they're getting paid handsomely. They're going to put their lives, their reputations, their bragging rights on the line.

"It's going to be so hard for these two to walk the streets and everybody and their dog will be talking about the fight, putting it on them, saying good luck.

"I can imagine at the Principality Stadium on fight night, the noise, two o'clock in the morning, it's going to be such an atmosphere. It's going to be a great story.

"I would say at least five years ago is when this fight should have happened.

"Five years ago, they were both mature, in their prime and good and ready to go.

"Now we've seen the decline of these fighters and it's not unfair to say that. We've seen better performances from both fighters.

"Five years ago, these two getting in the ring together, you would have had two young, hungry warriors that wanted more.

"Now I think it's more of a business transaction that will turn personal as it goes on. This is more business than pleasure.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Barry Hearn says he was pleased with the 'respect' shown between Fury and Joshua at their press conference

"The fight will go on and it's a shame, but at least we're getting it. At least the fans are going to see it. At least the place is going to be packed out. Everybody will be watching this fight because there's been a 10-year build-up to it.

"In terms of who wins, I'm leaning more towards Fury.

"I'm going to get some calls from my friends. I know I'm an AJ fan but you've got to say what you see.

"And I think this time suits Fury all the way through."

Sports.title: Infraad looks to bring up a hat-trick at Ascot
Sports.content:
We have a busy day’s racing on Friday with action from Ascot, Hexham, Newcastle and Wolverhampton, live on Sky Sports Racing...

3.35 Ascot - Rapid Improver Infraad takes on Galiyan

An excellent field of six has assembled for this Listed Noel Murless Stakes where Infraad bids to continue the winning thread.

William Haggas' three-year-old has improved through the season winning a useful handicap at Goodwood before taking the Melrose at York with aplomb. He steps up into Listed grade but will be expected to go close under Tom Marquand.

Galiyan brings in some solid credentials and matches Infraad with an official rating of 106. He has been highly tried since winning a Chester maiden and wasn't disgraced when fifth in the St Leger last month.

Melrose and Haydock second Galilean Quality rates the pick of the remainder.

5.25 Wolverhampton - Handicap newcomer Enchanted Queen faces four rivals

George Boughey and Billy Loughnane team up with handicap debutant Enchanted Queen for a trappy renewal of the bet365 Fillies' Handicap at Wolverhampton.

An easy winner of a Kempton novice on his first start for the yard, he steps up in distance as he tackles handicaps off a mark of 84.

The Roger Varian-trained Bintaziza looks the chief threat under Ray Dawson. Having scored on her first couple of outings on the all-weather, she suffered defeat at Thirsk. Sent off only 9-1 for the Sandringham in June, she has not been seen since and should have more to give.

2.48 Hexham - Moveit Like Minnie and Banderas contest feature

The main event on a quality Friday afternoon at Hexham sees Moveit Like Minnie top a field of seven for this Jewson Hexham Handicap Hurdle.

The Nigel and Willy Twiston-Davies-trained mare landed an eighth career victory at Wincanton in March before ending the campaign down the field in a quality Plumpton heat. She returns from a break in a lesser heat and could defy topweight for a team who have been among the winners.

Banderas was successful over two miles here back in May and he must be feared if handling the dip in distance under this six-pound higher mark.

Winds Of Winter and Double Digits complete the shortlist.

William Buick, James Doyle, Colin Keane, Tom Marquand and Kieran Shoemark all in action.

Sports.title: Browns overcome Steelers' comeback for dramatic win in final seconds
Sports.content:
Deshaun Watson passed for 268 yards and moved the Browns into position for Andre Szmyt's career-long 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds remaining that gave Cleveland a 27-24 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday night.

Watson, who completed 24 of 33 passes with a touchdown and an interception, was four of five for 46 yards as he led a go-ahead drive in the fourth quarter for the third straight week.

The Browns - who are 3-1 for the first time since 2021 - had a 21-7 lead late in the first half before the Steelers rallied to tie it at 24-all. Aaron Rodgers threw a three-yard touchdown pass to Pat Freiermuth with 1-44 remaining and Rodgers sneaked it in for the two-point conversion.

Rodgers, who was 22 of 40 for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions, had one final chance to get the Steelers in field goal range, but he was picked off by Grant Delpit at the Browns' 18 with one second left.

Pittsburgh's Jaylen Warren rushed for 93 yards on 17 carries and DK Metcalf had five catches for 115 yards.

Image: Watson completed 24 of 33 passes with a touchdown and interception. (AP Photo/Sue Ogrocki)

Cleveland's defence sacked Rodgers five times.

Cleveland has won eight straight Thursday night games, the longest active streak and fourth longest in NFL history. Four have come against the Steelers.

Pittsburgh (2-2) is 0-10 on the road against AFC North rivals on Thursdays.

After Cleveland went three-and-out on the opening possession, Pittsburgh went 78 yards in 17 plays, capped by Wilson taking a shovel pass 12 yards around left end on a jet sweep. It was the second straight game in which Steelers have reached the end zone on their first drive.

Watson had 181 yards passing by halftime, his most in the first 30 minutes since joining the Browns in 2022.

Jaleel McLaughlin tied it at 7-7 with 12-14 remaining in the first half on a 28-yard run around right end. The fourth-year running back broke a pair of tackles at the 22 and went through a narrow opening at the 15 before scoring.

Image: Cleveland Browns players celebrate. (AP Photo/David Richard)

The drive was set up after Denzel Ward picked off Rodgers' pass intended for Michael Pittman Jr. at the Browns' 44 on the second play of the second quarter.

Cleveland took a 14-7 lead midway through the second quarter on Quinshon Judkins' two-yard run off right guard. The touchdown came three plays after Watson found Denzel Boston for a 60-yard completion to the Steelers 14 on the first play of the drive.

Harold Fannin Jr. then hauled in his third touchdown in two games on a two-yard pass from Watson on third-and-goal with 1-22 remaining.

It was the first time since Week 13 of the 2020 season against Tennessee that the Browns scored at least 21 points in the second quarter.

The Steelers got within 21-10 on Boswell's 31-yard field goal with eight seconds left before halftime.

Rodgers rolled right and connected with Washington for a 21-yard touchdown early in the fourth quarter to bring Pittsburgh within 21-16. The two-point conversion attempt failed. The Steelers fought their way back to level the game but the Browns emerged victorious with a dramatic finish.

Sports.title: Verstappen makes fast start in Malaysia to outpace Russell
Sports.content:
​Max Verstappen made an impressively fast start to Formula 1's return to the Sepang International Circuit to set the pace from George Russell in the first practice session of the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia.

With F1 cars back on the popular track on the outskirts of Kuala Lumpur for the first time since 2017, Verstappen - the winner of that last race at Sepang - was quickly back in the groove in his Red Bull and set the pace on a 1:37.520 by three tenths of a second.

Russell, who pipped Verstappen to victory in Baku last week, was second quickest in a Mercedes car that features a major aerodynamic upgrade this weekend.

The package represents Mercedes' first car update of significance since the Canadian Grand Prix at the end of May and includes a new floor, rear suspension and rear corner.

While it will inevitably take a little time for the Silver Arrows to fully assess the revised W17's performance and to get the most out of it, Kimi Antonelli will hope to close up to Russell after the title leader lapped 0.6s slower than his team-mate alone in the first session.

Antonelli was fifth but a full second off Verstappen's pace a week on from a Baku weekend when he was comprehensively outperformed by Russell, who cut the Italian's championship lead to 66 points.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Anthony Davidson takes us through Lewis Hamilton's 2017 pole lap around the Sepang International Circuit.

Only Russell finished within half a second of Verstappen. Isack Hadjar, who has a five-place grid penalty to serve for engine changes in Sunday's race, was third fastest in the second Red Bull but 0.7s slower than his team-mate.

Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies told Sky Sports F1: "It's early to get excited because it's only FP1 but Max and Isack did a good job in very difficult conditions - they got into a rhythm pretty quickly.

"Everyone is fighting with the car because of the extreme heat so it doesn't feel good for anyone. It's fair to say, relative to the others, we were not too far from the ballpark."

Ferrari were a long way off the pace in first practice with Charles Leclerc in fourth and Lewis Hamilton in sixth lapping over 0.8s slower than Verstappen.

McLaren were even further off the pace and finished outside the top 10 completely, with Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris 11th and 12th respectively. The Woking team ran a back-to-back comparison of their version of 'Macarena' rotating rear wing - which they call the H-wing - with Piastri running the design while Norris had the standard specification.

Amid typically hot and humid Malaysian weather, and on a noticeably dusty track, tyre degradation was quickly a factor on a circuit that features an older tarmac and numerous long, fast corners.

Image: Max Verstappen in Malaysia (Red Bull Content Pool)

Indeed, the Mercedes pit wall told Russell during his long run on the soft tyres late in the session that they appeared to be the "outlier" compared to rivals in terms of higher wear.

But Red Bull's Mekies cautioned: "It's early days. We saw the high deg of the Mercedes but everyone is out of the [set-up] window now."

Pierre Gasly was the lead midfield runner in seventh for Alpine, while Racing Bulls were eighth and ninth with Liam Lawson and Arvid Lindblad - who will take a grid penalty for engine changes on Sunday - respectively.

Audi's Nico Hulkenberg rounded out the top 10 ahead of second practice at 9am, live on Sky Sports F1 and Sky Sports Main Event.

Sports.title: Pride of Wales up for grabs as Price battles Clayton at World Grand Prix
Sports.content:
Welsh bragging rights and a place in the World Grand Prix semi-finals will be up for grabs when Gerwyn Price and Jonny Clayton meet in Leicester on Friday night.

World No 4 Price is one spot ahead of Clayton in the PDC Order of Merit and will extend his lead over his compatriot - and World Cup of Darts partner - if he wins their game.

However, if Clayton, battling to qualify for the Grand Slam of Darts in November, is victorious, and then goes on to lift the title on Sunday, he will usurp the Iceman as Wales' top-ranked player.

World Grand Prix quarter-finals Live on Sky Sports+ and Sky Sports Main Event from 7pm on Friday Nathan Aspinall vs Ryan Joyce Gerwyn Price vs Jonny Clayton Luke Humphries vs Niels Zonneveld Gian van Veen vs James Wade

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Price hit two 120 checkouts in his dominant victory over Sebastian Bialecki on the opening night at Mattioli Arena

Price leads the pair's head-to-head 30-15 and won their last meeting earlier this month - an 11-7 success in the semi-finals of the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam.

But the 41-year-old was "smashed up", to use his words, by The Ferret in the World Grand Prix final in 2021, with Clayton romping to a 5-1 success.

Price, who picked up the World Cup title with Clayton in 2020 and 2023, said: "I know how good Jonny can play, I know how bad he can play. I know how good and how bad I can play.

It would be nice to have another [major] under my belt. I am always chasing, I never give up. I always say, ‘if I don’t win today, I will try again tomorrow’. “When I’m up on that stage, I love every second of it, and that’s all that counts. I think when the day comes that I don’t enjoy it, then I’m in trouble.

"I just need to take my opportunities. If I can start well, score in between and put Jonny under pressure, I think I will come through but it's going to be a real tough one.

"It's special for Wales regardless of who wins the game. We're going to have a Welshman in the semi-final of another massive major."

Clayton added: "There's banter between me and Gezzy. Every time he gets to Welsh No 1, he sends me a flag with a No 1 on. We're good friends, world number 4 and 5. You can't fault that from Wales!"

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Clayton landed four ton-plus finishes in his second-round victory over Wessel Nijman

Clayton scrapped through his first-round match against Krzysztof Ratajski 2-1 - Price joking that his countryman got "lucky" - but then slammed in four-ton plus finishes, including three in the first set, as he saw off the improving Wessel Nijman 3-1.

Price is yet to drop a set in the tournament, first sweeping past Sebastian Bialecki 2-0 and then thumping Ross Smith 3-0 as he gained revenge for his defeat to 'Smudger' in the recent World Series of Darts final in the Netherlands.

The all-Cymru clash between Price and Clayton is joined on Friday's schedule by Luke Humphries versus Niels Zonneveld, James Wade vs Gian van Veen and Nathan Aspinall vs Ryan Joyce.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Mark Webster previews Clayton vs Price, saying there is more on the the line for The Ferret

'If I think I am going to win easy, I will fail'

Zonneveld, who has dumped out Josh Rock and Gary Anderson, is the lowest-ranked player left in the event at world No 35 but second seed Humphries will not be overlooking the Dutchman, especially after being upset by the unseeded Mike De Decker in the 2024 final.

Humphries, eyeing a second Grand Prix title after victory in 2023 said: "One thing this tournament teaches you is not to take anyone for granted. If I think because Niels is whatever ranking he is that I'm going to win the game easy, I will fail.

"He's playing good darts and could be the Mike De Decker story. I will treat him with the respect I would every player, the respect he deserves.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Luke Humphries fired in a 10-dart finish as he swept Jermaine Wattimena aside at the World Grand Prix

On what winning his first major since the 2025 Premier League - and eighth overall - would mean to him, Humphries added: "When you have experienced that achievement of winning a lot and then it all goes away for 12 months, when you get that experience of winning again it feels even sweeter.

"I have worked really hard over the last 12 months and not got the rewards so winning would do me good, boost my confidence.

"Because I'm not picking up one or two majors a year, people think you are not as good as you used to be but I feel I am playing better than ever. I still feel there is another level in me. I'm just trying to find where that comes from."

Image: Humphries will take on Niels Zonneveld in Friday's quarter-finals

'ChatGPT tells Joyce he is on the right track'

The unassuming Joyce is, along with Zonneveld, an outsider to lift the trophy, particularly with the way his last-eight opponent Aspinall hammered in eight 180s on Wednesday night in his rout of Luke Littler's conqueror Luke Woodhouse.

Joyce, though, is a master on double 16 and realises this double-in, double-out tournament likely represents his best chance of winning a major - the Geordie made the semi-finals in 2024 before being brushed aside by Humphries.

'Relentless', who has seen off six-time Grand Prix champion Michael van Gerwen and Danny Noppert so far, has also been buoyed by AI telling him he is on the right track.

Image: Ryan Joyce says a discussion with ChatGPT shows he is on the right path

He said: "I think I was just bored one night, and I thought, 'I'll put ChatGPT on and say I've got a big game coming up. Have you got any tips on how I can handle it better?'

"The AI programme gave me a list of lots of different things to do, and I thought to myself, 'well, actually, I already do most of that, I already think like that, I've actually taught myself that from my own experience of being a professional for so many years'.

"That gave me a little boost, so I'll just continue with what I'm doing. I don't need anybody's help. I'm just going to do it myself."

Image: Nathan Aspinall is Joyce's opponent on Friday

Aspinall, however, says Joyce's hopes will come crashing down if he replicates his display against Woodhouse.

"Joyce is unreal on his double 16 but he can't score like me - and he knows that. If I score like I did [in round two], he's not going to beat me, simple as that."

Sports.title: Manchester City face appeal deadline after Burnham stirs tensions; Nations League news: football – live
Sports.content:
2m ago 04.42 EDT FA confirms it has powers to take disciplinary action against City Matt Hughes The FA has confirmed it has powers to take disciplinary action against Manchester City and key individuals at the club in the governing body’s first comments since City were found guilty of more than 100 breaches related to financial regulations. The FA statement reads: “The Independent Commission’s decision has significant implications for the integrity of the game. We are carefully considering the decision and its implications and will take action where appropriate. “As proceedings between the Premier League and Manchester City Football Club remain ongoing, we do not intend to comment further at this stage. We will, however, continue to monitor developments closely.” Share Updated at 04.43 EDT

8m ago 04.35 EDT “Everyone at Liverpool should be happy today” – Jürgen Klopp was full of praise for Florian Wirtz after his goal in Germany’s 2-0 win over Serbia last night. double quotation mark That was exceptional; he played a fantastic game. Our style of play suits Flo Wirtz. I don’t even know what Flo has to do right to make everyone happy. Everyone in Liverpool should be happy today. Wirtz didn’t feature in Klopp’s first game in charge, a 1-1 draw with the Netherlands last week, and came off the bench in the 1-0 defeat to Greece that followed. He played the full 90 last night, operating off the frontman Nick Woltemade and scoring on the hour mark to double Germany’s lead. View image in fullscreen Jürgen and Flo. Photograph: Kai Pfaffenbach/Reuters Share

18m ago 04.26 EDT Manchester City: Ed Aarons and Porto-based Miguel Dantas have taken a deep dive into the situation surrounding Rui Pinto, the former history student whose leaks of private documents in 2018 prompted the investigation into City. After Pinto turned his attention to Gianni Infantino on Wednesday, Portuguese authorities confirmed that he is no longer a protected witness: double quotation mark That is understood to have come as a surprise to the 37-year-old, who finds himself without a job, a home or an income. He has been living in a safe house under protection and has never disclosed his location, and it is understood he has received no visitors. The Guardian understands talks had been initiated to begin the process of reintegrating Pinto back into social and professional life. That initiative will be halted, leaving Pinto to fend for himself. He has been advised not to return home, contact family members or visit crowded places socially or for work. Criminal or saviour? Rui Pinto abandoned by Portuguese authorities after Manchester City leaks Read more Share

31m ago 04.13 EDT Women’s Champions League: “Of course there is a lot of noise but the players are very calm – I haven’t seen or noticed anything that will take any percentage out of the players’ performance” – the words of Andrée Jeglertz last night after his Manchester City team were held to a 1-1 draw by Real Madrid. Linda Caicedo’s opener was cancelled out by Khadija Shaw in City’s first game since the Premier League’s guilty verdict. Tom Garry was at Joie Stadium to gauge the mood … double quotation mark Speaking to supporters on the bridge that connects this venue with the neighbouring Etihad Stadium, some appeared relaxed about the situation and unsure what it had to do with the women’s team, while others were clearly troubled and looking forward to watching some football as a form of escapism. An elderly City fan, who did not wish to be named, said pre-match: “We’ve been through rough times before, we’ll come through rough times again,” in a matter-of-fact manner. Another simply demonstrated what appears to be a growing dislike for reporters asking about the 115 charges when they said angrily “you’re from the media?” before using an expletive and promptly walking away. Shaw secures WCL draw against Real Madrid as Manchester City show spirit after week of turmoil Read more Share

41m ago 04.02 EDT Nations League: Jorge Jesus guided Portugal to an impressive 4-2 win in Denmark in the first game since Cristiano Ronaldo had walked away from the squad over concerns about his playing time. Ronaldo left camp after an apparent rift with Jesus having been left on the bench for last Sunday’s win in Norway. João Félix was again on the scoresheet for Portugal as his late strike sealed the points. Jürgen Klopp won his first match in charge of Germany at the third attempt as Florian Wirtz’s second-half goal helped secure a 2-0 win over Serbia in Munich. After losing to Greece on Sunday, Klopp had to field frankly ridiculous questions about the diversity of Germany’s national team. Greece almost pulled off another shock win last night but surrendered a two-goal lead to draw with the Netherlands in Thessaloniki. Virgil van Dijk and Tijjani Reijnders rescued things for Xavi, who admitted he was at fault after a poor first half. “Maybe I made things unclear for the players by making too many changes,” said the Netherlands boss. Nations League: Ronaldo-less Portugal prosper while Klopp gets first win as Germany coach Read more Share

55m ago 03.49 EDT Nations League: Let’s have a look back at last night’s action, eh? Wales notched their first win of the campaign by coming from behind to beat Norway in Cardiff. With the score level at 1-1 at the break, Torbjørn Heggem was sent off 17 seconds into the second half and Neco Williams scored the winner from the resulting free-kick. A lot of eyes were on Manchester City’s Erling Haaland, who was kept at arm’s length by Wales and serenaded by chants of “You’re just a shit Kieffer Moore” from home supporters. Martin Ødegaard, who captained Norway to the World Cup quarters in the summer, described the result as the “first punch in the face for a long time” while Wales manager Craig Bellamy was happy to respond to the criticism he has received of late: double quotation mark Look, I am a strong person, I think we all are, but it’s the people around me I’m conscious of. It’s just society. What are we? Eight prime ministers in the space of 11 years? It’s nuts ... We’re such a small country, why can’t we have each other’s backs? Why don’t we look after each other more? The others can go at us. We’re too quick [to criticise]. The Ireland squad were under pressure to boycott last Sunday’s game against Israel in Hungary, which they won 3-0, and face them again in Dublin this Sunday. With Ireland 1-0 up after Troy Parrott’s fine solo goal, tennis balls with Palestine flags were thrown on to the pitch in the 20th minute before a man appearing to be carrying a Palestine flag invaded the pitch in the 35th minute. Sports.title: Neco Williams fires revitalised Wales to fightback win against 10-man Norway
Sports.content:
On a night when Erling Haaland moped around the pitch, dragging his hulking frame across the Cardiff turf, Wales registered a welcome victory over 10-man Norway and their first this year. Was this just one of those games where the game’s deadliest finisher was stuck on the fringes or was it a case of 115 things occupying his mind? Either way, this defeat proved a humbling experience. “You’re just a shit Kieffer Moore,” was the chant aimed at Haaland from the locals.

Daniel James cancelled out Oscar Bobb’s well-worked opener in the first half and 17 seconds after the restart Torbjørn Heggem was sent off for fouling James as the Leeds winger streamed towards goal, resulting in a free-kick from which Neco Williams earned Craig Bellamy a timely win with an unerring strike.

“It feels a bit like the first punch in the face in a long, long time,” said the Norway and Arsenal captain Martin Ødegaard after his country lost successive games for the first time in four years. “Now we have to respond, stick together and fight back.”

For Bellamy, a first win since last November eased the mounting negativity after a bruising run of results, chiefly their World Cup playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March and a listless display in Denmark last Sunday. “I felt my own disappointment since Bosnia and I’ve felt the stick as well,” the Wales head coach said. “The summer wasn’t easy. These games weren’t easy. But I’ve seen it … I’ve seen managers before me get it. I’ve seen the abuse the previous manager [Rob Page] got. It’s been a really difficult couple of months but it’s ‘welcome to this’ if you want to step into this … this is it. I do think we could be kinder to each other.”

It was plain to see Bellamy had been hurting and he cited his daughter receiving abuse on social media. “I chose to live back down here because I wanted to be on the ground, I wanted to be called a wanker to my face,” he added.

View image in fullscreen Torbjørn Heggem sees red straight after half-time. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

“The World Cup [playoff defeat] moved, I just felt the shift … Look, I am a strong person, I think we all are, but it’s the people around me I’m conscious of. It’s just society. What are we? Eight prime ministers in the space of 11 years? It’s nuts ... We’re such a small country, why can’t we have each other’s backs? Why don’t we look after each other more? The others can go at us. We’re too quick [to criticise].”

View image in fullscreen Dan James brings Wales level in the first half. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Wales bounced off the canvas after Ødegaard’s cute ball released Bobb on goal to open the scoring on 11 minutes. Liam Cullen, now of third-tier Leicester, pinched the ball from Sander Berge after the Fulham ­midfielder was sluggish to claim Fredrik Aursnes’s pass and Wales raced away from the scene.

Cullen and Lewis Koumas burst forward and Sorba Thomas zipped a low cross into the box, where James beat David Møller Wolfe to the punch. Thomas, who by his own admission loves staying wide to get chalk on his boots, was a constant threat.

Norway were punished for being slow out of the blocks in the second half, Heggem hauling James down after the restart. James does everything at speed and Heggem knew he was in trouble. The Spanish referee Alejandro Hernández awarded a free-kick on the edge of the box and ­Williams dispatched a wonderful right-foot strike to Ørjan Nyland’s right, to the surprise of the former Aston Villa and Reading goalkeeper.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bobb played draught excluder behind a white wall of Norway shirts and Nyland stepped to his left. Nyland was out of position when he had to shuttle across his goalline when Williams thrashed the ball into the bottom corner.

Haaland had one of those games; he was on the periphery and recorded just 11 first-half touches, the fewest of any player, including the Borussia Dortmund full-back Julian Ryerson who was forced off through injury after 16 minutes. Ethan Ampadu easily won what, technically, will go down as a duel on halfway but in truth Haaland just stuck out a leg in the hope of claiming the ball. His first whiff of goal came a couple of minutes before the interval but Ryerson’s replacement, Marcus Pedersen, misread Haaland’s movement and the move collapsed.

The substitute Josh Sheehan spurned a golden chance to extend Wales’s advantage, sending a weak shot at Nyland after more fine craftsmanship from Thomas to release the Bolton midfielder on goal. Up the other end, Haaland ambled across the box in preparation for another Pedersen cross. When it arrived Haaland soared high but unmarked sent a header straight at Danny Ward. Then came a puff of the cheeks, a look to the turf. It has been that kind of week.

Sports.title: Nations League: Ronaldo-less Portugal prosper while Klopp gets first win as Germany coach
Sports.content:
Portugal maintained their perfect start to Nations League Group A4 as Jorge Jesus’s squad showed little signs of missing Cristiano Ronaldo with a 4-2 victory over Denmark in Copenhagen.

The 41-year-old Al-Nassr forward and five-time Ballon d’Or winner left the camp before the match amid reports of a falling out with Jesus, his former club manager, having been left on the bench throughout a victory in Norway.

João Cancelo gave Portugal a 13th-minute lead before Brentford midfielder Mikkel Damsgaard equalised.

Gonçalo Ramos swiftly put Portugal back in front after 25 minutes, with Napoli forward Rasmus Højlund levelling things up at 2-2 early in the second half following a swift counter.

Vitinha’s header, his first Portugal goal, and a late strike by João Félix made it three straight wins.

“A victory of the highest quality,” said Jesus. “This Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard – and that cannot be overlooked. Of course, this is more important than anything else that has happened.”

New Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp got his first win with a 2-0 Group A2 victory over Serbia in Munich. Bayern Munich midfielder Tom Bischof fired in his first senior international goal and Liverpool forward Florian Wirtz then added a second in the 61st minute.

Germany produced a disciplined and intensive game, illustrating the high-pressure soccer Klopp wants to instill in the team. “That’s going in my archive. We’ll make a video out of it now,” Klopp said. “That’s how we want to play.”

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp (right) applauds fans alongside Tom Bischof, who scored his first international goal in the victory over Serbia. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

Speaking to public broadcaster ZDF, he added: “The mix of football and attitude was top level today. I told the boys that this has to be our benchmark.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wirtz said: “It was important to win again, just for the spirit in the team, and to send a signal out that we’re good football players and also a good football nation. Definitely a step in the right direction.”

In the same group, Tijjani Reijnders scored a late equaliser as the Netherlands fought back to draw 2-2 with Greece, who remain top. Fotis Ioannidis and Giorgos Masouras had the home side 2-0 up at the break.

Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk powered in a header from a corner on the hour. After Denzel Dumfries had seen his goal ruled out by VAR for offside, Reijnders lashed home a rebound in the 89th minute to secure a point.

In Group B3, Israel and Kosovo played out a goalless draw in Debrecen, Hungary. In Group D1, Malta and Gibraltar drew 1-1 while in Group D2, Azerbaijan were held to a goalless draw by Liechtenstein in Baku.

Sports.title: Shaw secures WCL draw against Real Madrid as Manchester City show spirit after week of turmoil
Sports.content:
Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City head coach, said the noise surrounding the guilty verdict dished out by the Premier League had zero impact on his women’s team’s performance after they played out a high-quality draw with Real Madrid in the Women’s Champions League.

Khadija ‘Bunny’ Shaw’s ruthless finish earned City a point against an impressive Real Madrid side on a night when the hosts were surely glad for attentions to turn – however briefly – towards on-pitch matters after a week when the wider football club has dominated the headlines for the wrong reasons.

“Of course there is a lot of noise but the players are very calm – I haven’t seen or noticed anything that will take any percentage out of the players’ performance,” Jeglertz said.

The result – which was a fair reflection of an even but entertaining game – left both sides with two points from their opening two fixtures but City will know their league phase opponents should theoretically become less challenging from hereon after their opening draw at Bayern Munich. The Swedish coach added: “It is OK, it’s an OK start in the Champions League. It’s not ideal but it’s a good start and we know what is needed from us in the rest of the tournament.”

Quick Guide WCL roundup: PSG pummel Leuven Show The day after Paris FC played their first Women’s Champions League home game at Stade Jean-Bouin, across the road from Paris Saint-Germain’s Parc des Princes, PSG’s women’s team entertained Leuven 20km away at the club’s suburban training centre. Rasheedat Ajibade put the hosts ahead from close range after nine minutes against the Belgian side. Naomie Feller (pictured) then scored a quick-fire double, before Sakina Karchaoui and Vitória Yaya completed PSG's 5-0 rout. In the early games, Modesta Uka scored Austria Vienna’s first goal in the WCL but Inter's captain, Ivana Andrés, levelled in the fourth minute of added time to earn a 1-1 draw. Inter dropping points left Barcelona, who thrashed Roma on Wednesday, as the only WCL team with six points after two games. In a match between two teams that had lost in the opening round, HB Køge crushed visiting Swiss team Servette 5-1 in Denmark. PA Photograph: Benoît Tessier/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Jeglertz had been at pains to insist that it has been “business as usual” for his team despite the damning guilty verdict released by the Premier League towards the men’s side. There was a strange mood around this stadium in the buildup to kick-off with opinions mixed.

Speaking to supporters on the bridge that connects this venue with the neighbouring Etihad Stadium, some appeared relaxed about the situation and unsure what it had to do with the women’s team, while others were clearly troubled and looking forward to watching some football as a form of escapism.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw fires home Manchester City’s equaliser early in the second half. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

An elderly City fan, who did not wish to be named, said pre-match: “We’ve been through rough times before, we’ll come through rough times again,” in a matter-of-fact manner. Another simply demonstrated what appears to be a growing dislike for reporters asking about the 115 charges when they said angrily “you’re from the media?” before using an expletive and promptly walking away.

A much politer, younger woman simply expressed her sadness and her hopes that it wouldn’t cause the players stress.

Once the match started, there were occasional references to the news from the stands; midway through the first half one home fan sang ‘Sheikh Mansour, my lord, Sheikh Mansour, oh lord, Sheikh Mansour’, to the tune of Kumbaya, although nobody else appeared to join in. There was also a small group of men carrying an inflatable banana in one corner defiantly chanting about ‘City going down with a billion in the bank’.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In general, though, the regular Women’s Super League match-going fans who are members of the supporters club seemed focused on their usual repertoire of fan chants to encourage the players, whether singing about the brilliance of Aoba Fujino and later chanting the name of Mary Fowler, who hit the crossbar with a header before the break.

By then Real Madrid were already ahead courtesy of Linda Caicedo’s clinical, low finish into the bottom corner after a lethal burst of pace. The visitors could have scored as early as the first minute, when a sloppy mistake by Carlotta Wamser allowed Felicia Schröder to shoot but her effort flew narrowly wide and bounced off the stanchion, rippling the net but from the wrong side. It was a sign of the Spanish team’s intent and they looked sharp throughout.

City’s play was significantly more urgent and incisive after the break and – after Yui Hasegawa spurned a volleyed chance when she was in space inside the box – it did not take long for the hosts to equalise. Shaw turned and clinically fired into the corner of the net with great technique after good pressing from City led to Hasegawa winning the ball in midfield and feeding Shaw in the area. It was the Jamaica striker’s fifth goal of the season in all competitions and her first of this Champions League campaign.

Suddenly the WSL champions were dominating the territory, although Caicedo did go close at the other end with a diagonal shot that bounced wide. The introductions of Beth Mead, Sam Coffey and Grace Clinton from City’s bench only seemed to further strengthen the hosts.

Hasegawa volleyed just wide again, this time from the second phase after a half-clear corner, in another let-off for Real Madrid, who had gone close themselves at the other end when Ayaka Yamashita did well to save from Caicedo. The home fans were on their feet to applaud Yamashita and chant her name when she later produced a quick reaction save to keep out Irune Dorado’s close-range effort and keep the score level.

Sports.title: Pro-Palestine protests interrupt game as Ireland pass up 2-0 lead in draw against Austria
Sports.content:
Protests halted events in Dublin twice before the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium.

Despite a significant security presence, the contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a “limited tennis ball protest”, when – around the 20th minute – tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text “#StopTheGame” were launched on the pitch.

Then around the 35th minute a man ran on to the field of play from the opposite side carrying what appeared to be a Palestinian flag and was immediately tackled by security and carried off.

It has been a tumultuous week for the Republic. Their two Nations League fixtures against Israel have divided opinion in the country, sparking protests, including one which took place pre-match outside the stadium. The Republic’s behind-closed-doors “home” game against Israel in Backa Topola, Serbia, is scheduled for Sunday, and the manager Heimir Hallgrímsson on Wednesday confirmed it was their intention to play.

Troy Parrott got the hosts under way with a sensational 12th-minute opener and added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved the Republic’s undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

View image in fullscreen Michael Gregoritsch (left) points to the sky after scoring Austria’s second goal. Photograph: Brian Lawless/PA

Hallgrímsson’s men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrímsson made three changes, including the re-introduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

The goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, who had made himself unavailable for the Israel meetings, was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhín Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before the Republic enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors’ half.

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah’s glanced-on header from a goal kick.

View image in fullscreen Troy Parrott slots home the Republic of Ireland’s opening goal in the 12th minute. Photograph: Evan Treacy/EPA

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts before nutmegging Philipp Lienhart and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Play was briefly paused just before the 20th minute to clear up the tennis balls, a pause both teams used for a hydration break. The second stoppage of play took place around the 35th minute.

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead. Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a video assistant referee check and blasted it past the Austria keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed by VAR.

The Brentford keeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch, guessing the wrong way as the Augsburg forward fired into the corner.

The Republic captain, Dara O’Shea, was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar, and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: US lined up instead of Qatar to host inaugural Women’s Club World Cup
Sports.content:
The US is poised to host the first Women’s Club World Cup in January 2028, becoming the latest in a series of major Fifa tournaments staged in North America. Discussions to take the competition to the US are at an advanced stage, with Los Angeles and San Diego among the favoured host cities.

It will follow the men’s tournament, whose expanded version debuted last year, in being staged by a country that also hosted the men’s World Cup this summer.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the path has cleared for the US to hold the 19-team event without going through a formal bidding process, even though Qatar was in talks with Fifa about hosting.

The winter scheduling will avoid a clash with the men’s Copa América, which the US is the frontrunner to host in June and July 2028, but raises the prospect of a hectic year-round calendar for the world’s top players. The Club World Cup is placed squarely between the 2027 Women’s World Cup and the 2028 Olympics, which will demand full-strength squads. A number of top clubs are in favour of a rule change limiting players to one international tournament per year, whether for club or country.

Fifa is keen to use the Club World Cup as a dry run for the 2031 Women’s World Cup, which the US will host in conjunction with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica in a decision to be formally approved at an Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November.

Football’s global body is eager to assess the stadium venues, pricing and demand for tickets at the smaller 19-team Club World Cup before the 48-team World Cup three years later. Time to organise and market the Club World Cup is tight, given it will start on 5 January 2028.

Sources have cited the chaos engulfing Fifa’s leadership since the emergence of Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated FFE scheme as a significant reason for the backlog of hosting decisions still to be taken. In July, Europe’s top clubs threatened not to participate in future Club World Cups unless the FFE project was shelved. They also warned the threat would hold unless a joint venture between European Football Clubs and Fifa, agreed in outline form, but yet to be signed off, was completed before television rights could be sold for the women’s Club World Cup.

Another tournament awaiting a venue is the 2029 men’s Club World Cup. The US has expressed interest in hosting that competition, but should the women’s event be confirmed it appears more likely to be co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal before they jointly host the men’s World Cup the following year.
