Sports.title: Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar is quietly REMOVED from Michigan sex offender registry
Sports.content:
Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar is quietly REMOVED from Michigan sex offender registry

Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar has been quietly removed from the Michigan Sex Offender Registry list.

Nassar, who served as team doctor for the national gymnastics team from 1996 to 2014, used his position to exploit hundreds of young athletes, including medal-winning Olympic gymnasts Simone Biles and Aly Raisman.

He is currently serving multiple prison sentences lasting decades after being convicted on multiple counts of sexual abuse and child pornography in both federal and state court.

According to the Eaton County (Michigan) Prosecutor's Office, the 63-year-old is among more than 20,000 people whose names have been removed from the sex offender list after the Michigan State Police recently purged thousands of individuals from the database whose crimes happened before July 1, 2011.

A Michigan Supreme Court ruling on September 9 said that amendments to the Sex offender Registration Act issued in 2021 cannot be used to retroactively require registration due to older incidents, leading to the purge of the database.

The prosecutor's office wrote on social media that: 'The Michigan Supreme Court's decision to eliminate SORA requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning. Our community, along with the victims of these crimes, expected the registry to provide a measure of protection and awareness—assurances that have now been removed by the Court's ruling.'

Larry Nasser has been quietly removed from the Michigan Sex Offenders Registry List

Nasser is serving decades in prison after being convicted of multiple crimes

The registry is intended to 'assist the public' with preventing future criminal sexual acts by convicted sex offenders, according to Michigan State Police, and typically lists a legal name, photo, primary address, work address, age, physical description and court with records relevant to the criminal conviction.

'His conduct occurred before 2011 despite his convictions coming after,' said The Eaton County Prosecutor's Office, confirming Nasser's removal, per CBS News.

The prosecutor's office claimed the Supreme Court could have applied for a different interpretation and allowed for certain sex offenders to stay on the list.

More than 150 gymnasts were abused by Nassar during his 30-year career. Nassar admitted to sexually assaulting the athletes when he worked at Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics.

The doctor also admitted to possessing child pornography, and more than 100 women sought over $1billion from the federal government for the FBI's failure to stop him.

He was sentenced in federal court in 2017 to 60 years in prison on charges of possessing child sex abuse material. The following year, Nassar was sentenced to up to 175 years and up to 125 years, respectively, in two separate Michigan courts for molesting female gymnasts under his care.

Following the federal sentencing, U.S. Attorney Birge said: 'Today was a day of reckoning for Larry Nassar. He more than deserves this punishment for what he did.

'He consumed child pornography on a massive scale. We found 37,000 images of child pornography on his computers. Insatiable hunger of that nature simply encourages those who produce such images to continue to sexually exploit children. Compounding his danger to the public,

'Nassar was an insidious hands-on child predator in his own right. He took advantage of family friendships. And he treated his license to practice medicine as a license to sexually molest children. Thanks to the brave victims who came forward, we learned the full scope of his depravity. The breadth and dark depth of his heinous acts are extraordinary.'

Larry Nassar is pictured in court during his sentencing hearing in Michigan in January 2018

Olympic icon Simone Biles was among Nasser's long list of hundreds of victims

In April 2024, the US Justice Department announced a $138.7 million settlement with more than 100 people who accused the FBI of grossly mishandling allegations of sexual assault against Nassar in 2015 and 2016, a critical time gap that allowed the sports doctor to continue to prey on victims before his arrest.

When combined with other settlements, $1billion now has been set aside by various organizations to compensate hundreds of women who said Nassar assaulted them under the guise of treatment for sports injuries.

Simone Biles publicly broke her silence in January 2018, revealing in a powerful tweet that she was one of Nassar's victims.

'It took me a long time to write that, probably a couple of days, because every time I would go to write, I would start balling, and I couldn't get through it,' she said.

Biles also noted that she was heartbroken over having to continue to train at the ranch, the former USA Gymnastics national training center where she and her teammates were abused by the disgraced doctor.

Sports.title: Bungling Andy Burnham is criticised for ANOTHER error in attempting to clarify his statement on Man City case after being called out for 'tone-deaf' response following 'concern' over losing Abu Dhabi owners
Sports.content:
Bungling Andy Burnham is criticised for ANOTHER error in attempting to clarify his statement on Man City case after being called out for 'tone-deaf' response following 'concern' over losing Abu Dhabi owners

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has received further backlash after Number 10 attempted to clarify his comments around the financial case surrounding Manchester City.

Burnham's claim that he would be 'really concerned' if Manchester City's owners were to sell the club after it was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations has been hit by widespread criticism.

The Prime Minister made the comments following confirmation from the league that Man City had been found to have created a slew of 'sham' deals and contracts which misled the Premier League over £900million-plus in sponsorship deals over a nine-year period.

'As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules,' a spokesperson said on Thursday. 'He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

'If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.'

Football fans, though, haven't taken kindly to the latest message.

'Wrongdoing has already been established,' one fan posted on X. 'Get them gone.'

Another shared: 'This is an equally bad statement. Wrongdoing has already been established.'

A third posted: 'Burnham is a joke. We all heard what he said. He's backtracking, not clarifying.'

The end of the statement was later changed to: 'Wherever wrongdoing is established...'

Andy Burnham (with Man City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak in 2019) has been criticised for comments made on his 'concern' that the club's ownership might sell

The Premier League's chief executive Richard Masters stated that the club had 'systematically broken' the rules for nearly a decade and called the decision by the Independent Commission who heard the case 'the most significant in Premier League history'.

Since confirmation of the decision broke on Tuesday evening, there have been calls for Man City to face relegation, fines, and even expulsion from the top flight, as well as arguments that the Abu Dhabi ownership group should move on – but former mayor of Greater Manchester Burnham took a more hesitant tone and lingered on the investment they had made into both the club and the city.

Those on social media were quick to suggest that Burnham's comments could likely interfere with the process of both Man City's appeal and potential future sanctions if the charges are upheld.

One fan posted: 'It was a confusing and, at best, tone-deaf intervention. Coming from a skilled operator, it was quite jarring.'

Stan Collymore suggested that Burnham's 'concern' was 'tone deaf', highlighting the 'clunky' comments as an example of the power of sports-washing.

'For a PM, the day after a judgement by a respected panel to say 'we can't afford to lose City Group, they've put a lot into Manchester' is missing the point so widely that he's now going to be tagged as taking a side or grossly naïve,' he wrote in a lengthy post on X. 'Neither things people will readily vote for.'

Rio Ferdinand added that he thought Burnham was 'on the back foot referencing Manchester City', but other commenters on the site were more critical.

'This is political interference,' one wrote. 'Already stating that he sees them as a positive influence and not wanting them gone. Unacceptable interference by influencing the (government's Football) Regulator.'

Another added: 'Absolutely disgusting statement from the PM. He's basically saying you can cheat the system all you want if you pay enough. Just shows what sort of morals he really has'.

Green Party deputy leader Mothin Ali also weighed in, saying: 'Andy Burnham's comments are staggering, just one day after saying people should come before profit, he sides with big money over the integrity of a sport that belongs to the people.

'It's a shame the prime minister appears to agree there should be one rule for the rich and one for everyone else.'

Conservative MP Louie French, who serves as shadow minister for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport warned: 'Burnham's clumsy comments haven't just undermined the ongoing legal process and Premier League. He's left the IFR Chief, who is a Labour donor and will determine the fit and proper owner test, exposed to future legal challenges, as we warned would happen.'

Burnham has received backlash for his comments as a statement trying to clarify what he said was released

Burnham's comments did attract praise from one corner of social media, with Man City supporter and Oasis frontman Liam Gallagher writing: 'There's only 1 ANDY BURNHAM.'

Burnham, whose mayoral tenure in Greater Manchester began three years after the 2014 deal struck between Manchester Council and the Abu Dhabi United Group worth £1billion promising a regeneration of city centre districts New Islington and Ancoats, had stressed in his remarks that he was unable to 'intervene' in the ongoing case.

Speaking at the home of his side Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he said: 'I would be really concerned to lose (Man City's Abu Dhabi owners).

'They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.

'I can't intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it's ongoing, and because it's still contested by Manchester City, then I think it's right that I don't say much more.'

'I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn't just put into the Etihad (Stadium) and the campus around it but also into the city.'

In 2023, when charges were first brought against Man City, Abu Dhabi warned the United Kingdom that a negative outcome might damage relations with the country.

Man City have until October 2 to appeal the verdict, and Evertonian Burnham added that he did not want to assume guilt, as some had done in the wake of the Toffees' own sanctions in 2023.

'Everton was in this position a few years ago and you might remember that I fought for Everton in that situation because I still hold the view very firmly that they weren't fairly treated in that process,' he continued.

'I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time and with hindsight I think more people would say that wasn't fair, the way that was handled.

'So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I'd had before becoming prime minister.'

Everton had fallen foul of the Premier League's financial regulations and were charged and deducted ten points, later reduced to six on appeal. But this was the scenario Man City seem to have been looking to avoid during the 2009-18 period scrutinised by the Independent Commission.

David Kogan, chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), stated that he had the powers to 'assess the suitability of owners, directors and executive' and that the body would look to use their powers to protect 'the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football'.

The IFR and the FA will assess the findings once the sanctioning and appeals process has been completed.

Man City continue to deny any wrongdoing, with chief executive Ferran Soriano stating in a video shared with the club's staff that they were in possession of 'irrefutable evidence' of their innocence that could dispel the Premier League's 'conspiracy theory' on appeal.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland is SUING a Norwegian airline after they launched a World Cup advert with a plane sporting his ponytail haircut
Sports.content:
Manchester City forward Erling Haaland is suing a Norwegian airline for using a plane with his signature hairstyle in an advert.

Haaland, who cut his hair at the start of the season, became synonymous with his ponytail hair that he donned while scoring plenty of goals for both club and country.

Airline Norwegian Air Shuttle ASA used an image during the World Cup of a plane with Haaland's hair edited onto it, and the forward has failed to see the funny side of things.

The caption read: 'We've never felt more Norwegian.'

The post has since been deleted from the company's social media channels.

Haaland is now taking the company to court with allegations of a violation of the Marketing Act, and, on October 9, a meeting between the judge and lawyers before the main hearing will take place, according to Norwegian publication VG.

Erling Haaland is suing a Norwegian airline after they used his haircut for an 

Company spokesperson Catharina Solli said: 'We struggle to understand why we have been taken to court. Just like almost everyone else in Norway, we encouraged the national team during the summer.

'We did this by publishing a few things spontaneously, inspired by social media trends.

'It is unfortunate that this encouragement has been greeted by a lawsuit. But we hope to have a reasonable dialogue, in order that we can continue in the future to support our sporting heroes together.'

Haaland's lawyer Thomas Hagen, meanwhile, said: 'This case is about the illegal use by Norwegian of Haaland's distinguishing features to sell air tickets during the World Cup finals.'

Haaland scored seven goals as Norway made it to the quarter-finals in their first World Cup this century before losing to England.

Sports.title: Man City charges LIVE: Appeal deadline, HMRC investigation, £800m bill
Sports.content:
Manchester City's appeal deadline is today after the club were found guilty of 114 breaches of Premier League financial rules

Hello and welcome to Mirror Football's live blog covering the fallout from the Premier League's guilty verdict on Manchester City for Friday, October 2.

The pressure is being cranked up on the Premier League club with their deadline for an appeal today. The Treasury Committee, which is responsible for overseeing policies and administration of His Majesty's Revenue and Customs, have asked whether the government department has requested the redacted documents contained within the commission's report.

The Premier League announced earlier this week that City had been found guilty of 114 charges brought against them for financial breaches.

City responded by maintaining their innocence and have until the end of today to launch an appeal, with the club expected to do so before the deadline.

Their top-flight rivals are said to be readying legal action against them to the tune of £800million, while a cross-party group of MPs have urged HMRC to investigate the tax implications of the Premier League's charges.

It now remains to be seen what punishment is given to City, with reports claiming that chiefs at other football clubs want a sanction to be imposed before the end of the season.

Etihad, the main shirt sponsor for City, meanwhile, have also issued a statement in response saying they are "deeply concerned" by the Premier League's announcement. There are also concerns that City's Abu Dhabi owners could be stripped from the club, something Prime Minister Andy Burnham doesn't want to happen.

City are now set to argue that the government of Abu Dhabi - not the club's owners - part-funded the "sham" sponsorship deals that contributed to them breaching Premier League financial rules.

Stay tuned for the latest news and updates in our live blog below as the saga continues to unfold...

Sports.title: Portuguese media deliver damning Cristiano Ronaldo verdict as players refuse to discuss him
Sports.content:
Portuguese media deliver damning Cristiano Ronaldo verdict as players refuse to discuss him

Cristiano Ronaldo's international future has taken centre stage after his behaviour during the latest round of UEFA Nations League fixtures

View 3 Images Cristiano Ronaldo played no part for Portugal against Denmark (Image: Ritzau Scanpix/AFP via Getty Images)

It was another successful evening for Portugal on Thursday but Cristiano Ronaldo was nowhere to be seen. The veteran was left out of Jorge Jesus' side to face Denmark but the Euro 2016 winners ran out 4-2 winners without him.

‌



‌



Ronaldo was left furious after being kept on the bench for Portugal's previous game, a narrow victory over Norway. He then opted to leave the camp, just halfway through a four-match break.

‌



"In time, I will tell all the Portuguese the truth about the reasons that motivated me to leave the national team, to which I always devoted myself," Ronaldo wrote on Instagram. "Now is the time to wish Portugal and all my teammates good luck, without exception."

‌



Rafael Leao was handed the Al Nassr star's No.7 shirt in Copenhagen, where Portugal led 2-1 at the break and added two more second-half goals after Rasmus Hojlund had briefly brought Denmark level. Here's what the Portuguese media have said, not just about the match but also about Ronaldo's absence and what might come next.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Cristiano Ronaldo's sister hints star has QUIT Portugal in explosive social media rant READ MORE :

Record

In Ronaldo's absence, Joao Felix has stepped up. The former Chelsea forward scored for the third game running - this time after arriving as a late sub - to earn plaudits from Record.

‌



"He seems to have ushered in a new era for the National Team yesterday," the verdict read. "In the first match following the Cristiano Ronaldo saga, the Portuguese ship remains steady even without the captain.

"It was the 66th time Portugal took the field without the star player since his debut in August 2003, and the positive trend continued."

TSF

TSF carries comments from manager Jorge Jesus, who described the win in Denmark as the best of his team's three performances during the current break. He suggested he will address the Ronaldo situation after Sunday's game at home to Norway, rather than in between two games.

‌



View 3 Images Joao Felix was among the goals in Ronaldo's absence (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/ZUMA Press Wire/Shutterstock)

"Because they have so much individual quality, things come more easily," the boss said of his squad. "If you think this means having the group under control, then I have the group under control. They're all going hand in hand with me on my ideas."

Mais Futebol

It's not just Jorge Jesus who wasn't discussing Ronaldo. Mais Futebol has some post-match reaction from Renato Veiga, who indicated players on the Portugal team are not allowed to speak about the 41-year-old.

‌



"I'm very close to Cris and he knows I have a great affection for him, but I've been told I can't talk about the matter. I can't, I'm sorry," Veiga said.

O Jogo

View 3 Images Portugal have impressed under new boss Jorge Jesus (Image: Ulrik Pedersen/NurPhoto/Shutterstock)

There was praise in O Jogo for the togetherness shown by Portugal amid the headlines. The Selecao became the first team to reach nine points in any UEFA Nations League group in the current edition, as they aim to retain the title they won in 2025.

Article continues below

"The triumph in Denmark strengthened Jorge Jesus at a sensitive moment and opened up a new path," they wrote. "Light bodies, harmonious music, a slender synchronisation of movements, one-two passes, and a daring attitude were evident.

"With a phlegmatic response to the Ronaldo hurricane, a sudden storm that swept across the world, Portugal responded with unity, without any sign of a divided spirit, displaying more certainties than doubts, seemingly pacing an easy win in this phase of the Nations League."

Sports.title: Newcastle United fans inspire a new £115,000 stadium deep in the heart of Africa
Sports.content:
Newcastle United fans inspire a new £115,000 stadium deep in the heart of Africa

EXCLUSIVE: FIFA made its first-ever grant to Zambia after fundraising by an intrepid Tyneside couple - we first told the story of Crispin Mason-Jones and his wife, Dr Ellie Bond, in 2022

View 4 Images Members of the Mfuwe Mags U15s try out their new kit - and it resembles Newcasle's famous trim (Image: Andy Commins / Daily Mirror)

A new stadium inspired by Newcastle United fans will soon be built deep in the heart of Africa.

‌



‌



FIFA made its first-ever grant to Zambia after years of fundraising and campaigning by an intrepid Tyneside couple - backed by the Daily Mirror.

‌



We first told the story of Crispin Mason-Jones, 64, and his wife, Dr Ellie Bond, 60, in 2022.

‌



We travelled with them to the rural community of Mfuwe to see the first kit delivered to a team known as the 'Mfuwe Mags,' inspired by the couple's love of Newcastle United.

Now Crispin's plans for a new pitch at the 'JK Stadium' in the bush are taking shape with a £115,000 ($150,000) grant from FIFA, the first ever awarded to the African country.

The exciting development will be built alongside a multi-sport facility and an educational outreach project.

‌



Crispin, 64, of Jesmond, Newcastle, said: "The grant is to go towards the cost of the main football pitch and the all-weather multi-sport facility.

View 4 Images The plans for the new pitch in Mfuwe, Zambia

"The Zambian currency may have dropped in value since last year but it will still go a long way toward achieving our goals."

‌



He added: "It is for the region's people.

"The educational buildings on the site were through our joint venture with the Project Luangwa Foundation.

"They are now completed and were instrumental in us receiving the grant from FIFA.

‌



"We would not have received the grant without the new buildings.

The exciting plans and the transformation of the land are show in the designs for the new stadium - and the work that has already been done on the ground.

Aerial shots show the bare land transformed with areas marked out for the new football pitch and a vital all-weather facility.

‌



Crispin is now looking at options to ship both strips and Astroturf out to Africa from the UK, and fundraising for the transport costs.

View 4 Images Plans for the new football development in Zambia are shown by these aerial photographs

"We are now focusing on providing kit to schools rather than local teams to foster sport within them.

‌



"I did the original drawings and the early work with Project Luangwa, and I am now looking for Astroturf for the pitch."

Apart from the Mags, The Valley Queens, who play in the Zambian National League, will also benefit from the work done by Project Luangwa at the JK Stadium.

The Mirror joined Crispin as he brought £1,000 worth of black-and-white strips and 21 pairs of junior football boots to the Mags under-15 side.

‌



View 4 Images The children of Zambia in their new kit

They have provided thousands more kits since then, taking them over 5,000 miles from Tyneside to Africa.

Project Luangwa has another Toon supporter in CEO Ian Macallan. Originally from Durham, he provided education at remote bush schools alongside health and sporting programmes.

‌



Toon fan Ian, chief operating officer of Project Luangwa, works with communities in the area on tourism, education and gender programmes.

In July, it was awarded a $150,000 grant from Fifa's Global Citizen Education Fund to develop sporting opportunities in Mfuwe.

It is the first time Zambia has received a Fifa grant of this kind. The money is intended to provide facilities including a football pitch and facilities for tennis, basketball and netball.

Sports.title: 7 future England stars aiming to prove Thomas Tuchel wrong and become the next Harry Kane
Sports.content:
Harry Kane is the last in a long line of classic English centre forwards. England captain Kane follows on from the likes of Alan Shearer, Wayne Rooney, Gary Lineker, Michael Owen and Co.

Some are goalscorers rather than classic No. 9s but either way they are out-and-out strikers and sadly they are becoming a dying breed. It is so serious that Arsene Wenger, FIFA’s head of global football development, even held a coaches seminar in May 2023 to discuss the “Number 9” crisis throughout the whole game.

Incredibly, Liam Delap is the only English striker under the age of 27 to have scored a Champions League goal. It is no wonder that England boss Thomas Tuchel fears England have got a tough job in replacing Kane when one day the 33-year-old hangs up his boots.

Kane is irreplaceable and stepping into his shoes is a daunting task because he is just 13 short of a century of goals for England in just 123 caps. Dominic Calvert-Lewin is in this squad and Danny Welbeck was knocking on the door last season while Ivan Toney went to the World Cup.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Ollie Watkins was also in the World Cup squad but has now departed to the Saudi Pro League. They are three excellent No. 9s but they almost highlight the problem further because there is a huge gap underneath Kane when it comes to strikers.

Tuchel said England might not be able to find a direct replacement for another ten years but, realistically, we are just guessing. Kane had loan spells at Leyton Orient, Millwall, Norwich and Leicester before eventually getting a far chance at Tottenham - and the rest is history.

‌



Kane scored 73 goals for Bayern Munich and England and if he does not win the Ballon d’Or then, quite frankly, they should scrap the trophy. He has been the best striker by far.

So, there may be a striker coming through who blindsides us all. But this is a far cry from the 90s when, for example, Shearer, Les Ferdinand, Robbie Fowler and Teddy Sheringham were all in the Euro '96 squad and there was no room for Ian Wright or Andy Cole.

Is Harry Kane England's greatest ever striker? Have your say in the comments section.

View 6 Images England will have to find a new No.9 one day (Image: Michael Regan - The FA/The FA via Getty Images)

‌



The next wave had Rooney and Owen plus Peter Crouch and Jermain Defoe. Daniel Sturridge, Welbeck and even Rickie Lambert went to the 2014 World Cup. Wenger raised it in the FIFA seminar and it is a popular theme with academy scouts and coaches.

When in charge at Arsenal, Wenger loved centre forwards. He bought Olivier Giroud and he was used to illustrate the No. 9 discussion at the FIFA seminar. At the 2018 World Cup, Giroud had 15 attempts at goal, with 11 of them coming from inside the penalty area, but scored no goals and had no attempts on target.

Four years later, Giroud had 15 attempts, all were inside the area, six on target and he scored four. It highlighted that Giroud had more crosses and passed the ball to create chances for team-mates less in Qatar.

Wenger tried to argue that a good centre forward is worth his weight in gold. Wenger puts part of the issue down to a lack of hunger in the game.

‌



View 6 Images Thomas Tuchel has sent England a warning (Image: Gabriel Kuchta - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images)

That is why, he says, so many forwards come from South America where they do not have the wealth and luxuries of European academies and clubs. Youth football - from very young age groups - and into academy teams are simply not playing with a centre forward.

As one of the best youth scouts in the country said, every ball is into feet, they are being coached to play with false nines, No. 10s and formations have moved away from a target man. It is the same in defence, he argues, in that centre halves are being coached to play and the profile of youngsters has also changed towards technique over physicality.

You can watch any academy game and it is a rarity now to see a classic centre forward whereas every team used to play with a No9 Training drills used to feature getting the ball wide, centre forwards timing their runs and movement. Now it is all about ball into feet.

‌



The other key difference is opportunities for homegrown players. Last season, the promotion of minutes played by English players in the Premier League hit an all-time low of 25.8 percent. It has risen slightly to 27.1 percent this season but that is a stark and worrying trend. It has been around the 30 mark for several years previously.

It even hit a high of 36.1 percent in 21/22. It almost went unrecognised but England really played 4-4-2 at the World Cup with Jude Bellingham pushing up to join Kane in attack.

Tuchel has referenced Bellingham being an option for England in the future because of his intelligence, physique and bringing other players into the game. But England, like other nations, have a real problem when it comes to finding a classic centre forward.

Ones to watch

Brian Madjo - Aston Villa

‌



The 17-year-old was born in London, had a journey which took him to Metz and then Aston Villa and a drawn out transfer. He is strong, 6ft 4in and scored in the European Super Cup against Paris Saint-Germain which underlines his potential. Has scored four goals in nine games for England under-17s.

View 6 Images Brian Madjo is a hot prospect for Aston Villa (Image: Aston Villa/Aston Villa FC via Getty Images)

Liam Delap - Nottingham Forest

He is the quiz question about which player under 27 has scored in the Champions League. He is big, strong and has potential. He definitely made the wrong move to Chelsea, did not play enough and now should get a fresh start at Nottingham Forest.

‌



Will Lankshear - Middlesbrough

The 21-year-old has to get a mention because of the Harry Kane similarities. He was at Spurs, went out on loan and scored goals at Oxford. He has gone to Middlesbrough permanently with a big sell-on clause and his inclusion in the England under-21s means he must get a mention.

View 6 Images Tottenham sold Will Lankshear for a fee rising to £20million (Image: Richard Sellers/Sportsphoto/Allstar via Getty Images)

Vincent Joseph - Arsenal

‌



His move from Liverpool to Arsenal - an increasing trend among academy players and graduates - caught the eye. He has been prolific for England under-18s and, while it is always hard to predict, Arsenal have seen something.

Chizaram Ezenwata - Chelsea

The 18-year-old Chelsea starlet has been prolific for various England age groups and is with the under-19s now. He is big, strong - he is 6ft 2in tall - and the London-born forward is gaining a growing reputation.

View 6 Images Chizaram Ezenwata is highly regarded at Chelsea (Image: Cameron Howard/Getty Images)

‌



Shimi Mueka - Chelsea

The Chelsea prospect is currently on loan at Celtic and was the Premier League’s under-21 player of the season last year. Mheuka became Chelsea’s youngest-ever starter in a European competition against Copenhagen in the Europa Conference League, aged 17 years and 173 days.

Ale Rodriguez - Lyon

The 18-year-old was born in Venezuela and is currently on loan at Annecy from Lyon. But has represented England from under-15s to under-20s and is highly thought of. Keep an eye.

‌

Sports.title: Ireland held by Austria despite Parrott double as protests interrupt game
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott scored twice but the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin.

The contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a "limited tennis ball protest", when - around the 20th minute - tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text '#StopTheGame' were launched onto the pitch.

The match paused a second time when an invader carrying what appeared to be a Palestine flag entered the pitch and was promptly tackled and carried off by security.

The protests came after Ireland's decision not to boycott their game against Israel last week - although goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu did make himself unavailable.

Ireland are due to face Israel again on Sunday.

Image: Tennis balls with Palestine flags were throw onto the pitch

Before the protests, Parrott scored a sensational 12th-minute opener, and then added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved Ireland's undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrimsson made three changes, including the reintroduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

Bazunu was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was a significant security and police presence outside the stadium, where a small group of protesters also gathered before kick-off.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhin Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before Ireland enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors' half.

Image: Parrott is congratulated after scoring his second goal against Austria

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah's glanced-on header from a goal kick.

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts, before nutmegging Philipp Lienhardt and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Image: A protestor was carried off the pitch during the game

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead.

Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a VAR check and blasted it past the Austria 'keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed after a VAR check.

The Brentford goalkeeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch's free-kick as Ralf Rangnick's side fought back for a point.

Ireland captain Dara O'Shea was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Hallgrimsson admits 'toughest days' of career after Ireland beat Israel
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their controversial Nations League fixture at a neutral venue in Hungary.

Players did not shake hands with each other before their meeting at the Nagyerdei Stadion in Debrecen and there was no exchange between Ireland captain Dara O'Shea and Israel's Manor Solomon.

Ireland players also appeared to bow their heads while Israel's national anthem was played out before kick-off.

Black armbands were worn by Ireland players, which Football Association of Ireland (FAI) chief executive David Courell said was a gesture to recognise "all lives lost" in the Israel-Gaza conflict.

Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu was the only player who chose not to play after the squad voted to proceed with the match on Saturday amid calls for the game not to go ahead.

Goals from Troy Parrott, Adam Idah and Jack Moylan sealed the victory for Heimir Hallgrimsson's side.

Moylan celebrated his goal by kissing and raising his black armband before kissing his badge.

Hallgrimsson: I couldn't be more proud of the players

Republic of Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"It has been some of the toughest days of my coaching career, but its not about me.

"The game, the desire the players showed to make a statement on the pitch - they are football players, they wanted to show on the pitch, make that talking with their feet.

"What they did was impressive. In tough times that's when you find your leaders, there were so many players that stepped up in these tough times. The energy levels they showed was impressive.

"The performance was good given all the preparation, the lack of training, all of our meetings were about something other than football.

"I couldn't be more proud of the players.

"By playing I know we are making some people unhappy. By playing we are making others happy. Winning probably pleases everyone, but there will still be people angry that we played the game.

"I hope we can settle that slowly down and stay together as a team. I wish people in Ireland continue supporting these boys, because they certainly deserve it."

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland slip to deserved defeat in Kosovo
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland slipped to a 1-0 defeat away to Kosovo in their Nations League opener in Pristina.

The build-up to the League B3 encounter had been overshadowed by the controversy around upcoming fixtures against Israel, which Republic boss Heimir Hallgrimsson had admitted many of his squad members were uncomfortable about playing.

Chiedozie Ogbene had fired an early chance over before Kosovo responded to finish the first half strongly at the Fadil Vokrri Stadium.

The home side saw two shots cleared off the line and Ireland goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher then clawed away a header from Vedat Muriqi as Hallgrimsson's side got to the break on level terms.

Ireland - who are scheduled to play Israel in Hungary on Sunday and then again in a 'home' tie at another neutral venue in Serbia seven days later - dug in for the second half but were eventually undone with seven minutes left when Kosovo captain Muriqi bundled the ball in from close range.

Udinese defender James Abankwah was handed a first competitive start as part of a back five, with in-form Real Betis striker Troy Parrott the lone forward and Dara O'Shea taking the captain's armband.

Image: The Republic of Ireland have won two of their six games in 2026 so far

Ireland created what ended up being their only real clear chance in the 22nd minute. Abankwah got away down the right and ran into the Kosovo penalty area before cutting the ball back to Ogbene, who sent a curling effort over the crossbar.

Kosovo, who are in League B for the first time, went close on the half-hour mark when a cross from the left found its way through to Muriqi, whose angled shot was cleared off the line by Jayson Molumby.

Veldin Hodza then saw his 10-yard strike blocked in front of goal by O'Shea before Kelleher got up to claw away a looping header from Muriqi, which was set for the top corner.

Ireland made a positive start to the second half, with a deep cross from the right by Abankwah finding Parrott at the far post and his header was gathered by Kosovo goalkeeper Arijanet Muric.

Image: Vedat Muriqi scored the winner for Kosovo

Kosovo, though, continued to carry a threat themselves. Baton Zabergja sent a 20-yard effort just wide of the top corner, which again got the home supporters into full voice.

Muriqi forced Kelleher into another smart reaction save from an angled shot at the near post before Kosovo eventually made the breakthrough in the 83rd minute.

Ermal Krasniqi's shot was deflected onto the crossbar and Muriqi reacted quickest in a crowded six-yard box to nod the ball over the line.

Kosovo should have got a second late on when substitute Krasniqi dragged his shot wide after being set up by Muriqi following a break onto a long ball.

Ireland pay price for 'off day'

Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson told RTE:

"[Kosovo are] a good team, momentum with them, crowd with them, and to be honest they deserve the win.

"There was nothing that we didn't know about how they would play, where their threats would be, but [it was] an off day for a lot of our players and [it is] a tough place to come to if you have an off day, so a deserved win for Kosovo."

Hallgrimsson added: "We were the team that needed to defend today and didn't connect in possession or passes, not as sharp as we have done.

"We have to quickly find out the reason that we had an off day. We can all do better than we did today.

"It is a two-day turnaround for the next one, so we better be quick…and do better than this versus Israel. They are probably in the same position as us [having lost to Austria]."

Asked if the controversy from playing the fixtures against Israel had impacted on his team's performance against Kosovo, Hallgrimsson said: "I couldn't say now. It is difficult to measure that one."

He added: "This is the situation, we have to cope with it. And like I said before the game, this camp is a test of character.

"We need to do better in that area than we did here today. We knew that we needed to win the duels, win the one-vs-ones, but sadly they had the upper hand on all the basics."

What it means and next fixtures

Sports.title: Why have the Republic of Ireland's two games against Israel become so controversial?
Sports.content:
The Republic of Ireland will face Israel in a men’s football fixture for the first time since 2005 in this international break, but there have been calls for the two UEFA Nations League games not to be played at all.

Both meetings - the first played in Debrecen, Hungary on Sunday and the second scheduled for the Serbian town of Backa Topola on October 4 - have been overshadowed by politics, with the Football Association of Ireland (FAI) urged to boycott the internationals amid ongoing conflict in the Israel-Gaza War.

Uncertainty over the games going ahead might have subsided, but the tensions between the two nations have not.

Heimir Hallgrimsson, the Republic of Ireland head coach, has been accused of "stupidity and hypocrisy" by the Israel Football Association after last week suggesting his team would be "playing against genocide" when facing Israel, while his players are not ruling out their own protests ahead of the games.

The Athletic examines the key issues ahead of the first meeting this weekend.

Why have these games caused controversy?

This has been a contentious issue rolling down the tracks ever since the 2026-27 Nations League draw was made in February. Group B3 saw the Republic of Ireland pitted against Kosovo, their opening opponents this evening, and Austria, but it was the prospect of facing Israel which created immediate unease.

The Football Association of Ireland (FAI) had overwhelmingly approved a motion that called on UEFA to ban Israel from its competitions just four months earlier due to violations of the governing body's statutes, including "the organisation of clubs in illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank without the consent of the Palestinian Football Association".

The Nations League draw duly reignited the row. Irish politicians, including the FAI member Joanna Byrne, were quick to call for a boycott of the Israel games in the following days and protests ensued when Qatar visited Dublin's Aviva Stadium for a friendly in May. Tennis balls featuring the Palestine flag were thrown on the pitch by supporters, twice causing brief interruptions.

Image: Tennis balls with a Palestinian flag on were thrown onto the pitch in Dublin during protests in May 2026

The FAI had already confirmed its plans to go ahead with the Israel games by then, and that decision was formally approved at an EGM in July.

That saw only 32 votes in favour of a boycott, with 75 members voting for the games to be played. The FAI had argued that boycotting games would cause "significant and lasting harm to Irish football" due to the likely disciplinary sanctions from UEFA.

A measure of the opposition to the Republic of Ireland facing Israel also came with the acceptance that the "home" fixture would not be played in Dublin. The FAI cited "operational challenges (that) could impact the delivery of the game on home soil" and the decision was eventually made in late June, with the support of UEFA, to move the game to Backa Topola, a small town in northern Serbia, on Sunday week.

No tickets for the game will be made available to Ireland fans.

The FAI has subsequently revealed that a request to see the two nations kept apart in future competition draws has been rejected by UEFA.

"The answer I got was very clear," FAI chief executive David Courell told reporters on September 18. "That would not be possible because Ireland and Israel have never been in direct conflict."

What is the political backdrop?

The Republic of Ireland has consistently outlined its backing for the Palestinian people since the conflict with Israel began almost three years ago, joining Norway and Spain when officially recognising a Palestinian state in 2024. Taoiseach Micheal Martin has also made his stance clear, accusing Israel of committing "genocide" last year in comments reported by the Irish Mirror.

The conflict in Gaza began after Israel responded to attacks by Hamas militants on October 7, 2023, which saw around 1,200 people, mostly civilians, killed in Israel and 250 taken hostage. The war has subsequently seen 73,000 people killed, according to figures from the Gaza Health Ministry and used by the UN.

Strained relations between the Republic of Ireland and Israel have continued this year. Two Israeli government ministers were the subject of travel bans in June, while foreign minister Helen McEntee also confirmed Ireland's intent to limit goods trading with settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank this summer.

Image: Taoiseach Micheal Martin

A meeting between the Republic of Ireland and Israel on a football field this weekend has subsequently taken on enormous significance against such a backdrop.

There are similarities in Ireland's political stance with those of Norway, who faced similar calls for a boycott when Israel travelled to Oslo last October. The Norwegian Football Federation (NFF) had aligned itself with its government and said in a statement leading up to Israel's visit that the "tragic humanitarian suffering in Gaza" had made the fixture challenging.

That World Cup qualifier, won 5-0 by Norway, saw thousands take part in a protest march to the stadium.

Who has opposed the games taking place?

Moving a home game 1,500 miles away has not stopped the objections building ahead of the two teams meeting on Sunday. More than 160 Irish sportspeople signed an open letter asking their national team to boycott the Israel games under the banner of the Irish Sport for Palestine Group, who have also run the "Stop the Game" campaign that protested outside of the Irish team hotel in Dublin on Monday.

"This is a significant moment and with this moment you have an opportunity to do the right thing," the letter said.

Kevin Kilbane, the former Republic of Ireland international who holds 110 caps, has also been unequivocal in his views. "The Republic of Ireland should not be playing Israel… not while Israeli forces are committing genocide," he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.">he wrote in a column for the Irish Times.

Amnesty International also issued a fresh statement on Tuesday that said UEFA risked letting football "rubber-stamp apartheid" by allowing Israel's continued participation in its club and international competitions. A spokesperson for the Israeli FA responded to that by saying: "Their obsession with the idea of Israel as a state is incurable, as is their need of attention."

The Irish media, meanwhile, has faced its own dilemmas in the coverage of the Israel games. RTE, the public broadcaster behind Ireland's boycott of the Eurovision Song Contest in the last two years due to Israel's continued involvement, has stripped back its coverage. Contractual obligations will be met, RTE confirmed in a statement, but there would be no studio coverage or commentators sent to either fixture.

Image: Kevin Kilbane, former Ireland international, has spoken out

What have the key stakeholders said ahead of this weekend?

Relations between the two nations have grown increasingly hostile in the last week. Hallgrimsson appeared in front of the media to announce his squad for the upcoming friendlies and made pointed remarks when asked how his players would focus on football.

"We're not playing with genocide, we're playing against genocide," the former Iceland head coach told reporters. "We're playing against Israel, we're not playing with Israel."

The reaction to those words, in a social media post from the Israel FA account, raised temperatures further still. "We have contributed to the world and humanity in countless fields, earning an impressive number of Nobel Prizes along the way," it read. "Unfortunately, we have not yet found a cure for stupidity, ignorance and hypocrisy displayed by @IrelandFootball team coach. We're not playing with ignorance, hypocrisy and stupidity, we're playing against the coach who embodies them."

Martin, who was among the world leaders attending the UN General Assembly in New York, was then drawn back into debate on Tuesday. "I think those are unacceptable remarks. They should be withdrawn. Israel can't keep denying what the world knows and what the world understands."

The FAI has not addressed Hallgrimsson's comments publicly, but the Republic of Ireland's head coach said on Wednesday that he had been "grateful for the support" he had received.

"Maybe from a leadership point of view, it was not clever from me to take the attention (away) like this. It's a tricky time for us," Hallgrimsson said in his pre-match press conference ahead of facing Kosovo.

The same extends to his players, too. Dara O'Shea, the Ipswich Town defender, said, according to the BBC, that he and the rest of the players would come together on Friday to "openly discuss" the prospect of a protest ahead of the first Israel game in Debrecen on Sunday.

Image: Dara O’Shea, left, and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson during Wednesday’s press conference

Why are the games being played in Hungary and Serbia?

Hungary has acted as an adopted home for Israel since the start of the conflict. They first played there in November 2023, when resuming their attempts to qualify for Euro 2024 when hosting Switzerland at the Pancho Arena in Felcsut, a small village 26 miles west of Budapest.

Victor Orban, who lost his position as Hungary's prime minister this year, had been a long-standing ally of Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and claimed Hungary to be the "safest country in Europe" for Jews.

The World Cup 2026 qualifiers against Estonia, Norway and Italy were all held in Debrecen, which has also previously hosted European games for Israeli sides Maccabi Haifa and Maccabi Tel Aviv.

The Republic of Ireland's choice of Backa Topola, Serbia, is less clear. Dublin ceased to become an option, even behind closed doors, as the opposition to Israel visiting became clear, which left limited options for relocation.

It needed to be a nation sympathetic to Israel to avoid further protests and Serbia, neighbouring Hungary to the south, has forged strong diplomatic relations. According to the Associated Press, Serbia's president Aleksandar Vucic inaugurated an assembly factory for Israel-made drones last week, with plans for three more production sites.

A switch to Serbia was reliant on UEFA approval and it will be Backa Topola's home of the TSC Arena where this story ends on October 4.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"
