World.title: Ukraine, South Korea clash over transfer of 2 North Korean prisoners
World.content:
A diplomatic scandal has erupted over two North Korean prisoners of war, with South Korea demanding an apology from Ukraine. What's been the reaction in Kyiv?

Speaking at the UN General Assembly on September 23, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy sparked a diplomatic dust-up with South Korea.

In his speech, Zelenskyy mentioned that Ukraine had recently "sent two North Korean prisoners of war to the Republic of Korea" — men who had been captured by Ukrainian forces during fighting in Russia's Kursk region in January 2025. Both had expressed a wish to resettle in South Korea, he said.

The reaction from Seoul was swift: South Korea's Foreign Ministry summoned Ukraine's ambassador to Seoul, Andrii Vieshkin, and demanded an explanation for what it described as Kyiv's "unilateral disclosure" of the prisoners' transfer, despite a prior agreement to keep the matter confidential, along with an official apology.

Russia's war in Ukraine has given North Korea the opportunity to strengthen ties with Moscow, in part by sending soldiers to the battlefield Image: KCNA/KNS/AFP

Responding to Zelenskyy's speech, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war was a sensitive topic with wide-ranging consequences for diplomacy and national security on the Korean Peninsula.

Did Kyiv and Seoul have a secret agreement?

Dmytro Lytvyn, Zelenskyy's spokesperson, wrote on Facebook that no such confidentiality agreement existed between the two countries, adding that it was wrong to keep secret where such prisoners were being transferred.

Soon after, South Korean presidential spokesperson Kim Sung-wan called Lytvyn's denials false, according to news agency Reuters. Kim said Ukraine had asked for confidentiality — allegedly over concerns there might be criticism at home if the North Korean prisoners weren't swapped for Ukrainian prisoners being held in Russia.

Seoul had agreed to the secrecy for diplomatic reasons, he added, but also to protect the prisoners and their families who were still living in North Korea.

Missed opportunity to 'improve bilateral relations'

Nataliya Butyrska, an Asia-Pacific expert at the New Europe Center in Kyiv, told DW that Ukraine and South Korea lacked a continuous, trust-based dialogue, especially under the current government in Seoul.

"We should actually be natural partners — we should be standing shoulder to shoulder, with North Korea fighting against Ukraine," she said. "But that's not the case, due to a lack of trust."

Why Kyiv and Seoul are clashing over North Korean POWs To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

The prisoner transfer has been a hotly debated topic in South Korean media in the last week — not least because, according to South Korea's constitution, North Koreans are considered citizens of South Korea. It's also been instrumentalized by opposition lawmakers, while President Lee, aiming to ease tensions with the North, has taken a more measured approach.

"The prisoners could have been used by Ukraine to improve bilateral relations between Kyiv and Seoul," said Butyrska, adding that no one in South Korea was now thinking of thanking Ukraine for transferring the prisoners.

Butyrska pointed out that Russia, which usually doesn't express any interest in foreign prisoners, had actually demanded the return of these two North Koreans. "There was even a period of six months when the Russians refused to release any Ukrainian prisoners of war," she said. "They were not prepared to undertake any swap, because they wanted the North Koreans."

Is Ukraine being held hostage by South Korea's domestic politics?

For some observers, the diplomatic crisis can be linked back to domestic conflicts in South Korea. The opposition wants to know why the president agreed to keep the prisoner transfer secret, and have accused Lee of trying to gain favor with the North.

"President Lee Jae Myung was surprised by the incident, and now wants to shift the blame in part on Ukraine," said Mykola Polishchuk, a Korea expert based in Ukraine. He believes the transfer would have become public knowledge sooner or later, and that Seoul knew that Kyiv was going to comment on it. Reports that Ukraine had asked for secrecy were, he added, a way for a frantic politicians in Seoul to come up with an explanation.

"Ukraine has ended up mired in a scandal which it neither wanted nor planned for," said Polishchuk.

North Korea expands role in Russia's war with Ukraine To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

"South Korea has been pursuing the transfer of the prisoners for a long time. And now everybody seems to be happy that those Korean prisoners are in custody," said Shim Sangmin from the Asan Institute for Policy Studies in Seoul. "But what really complicates the matter is the fact that the South Korean government is trying to make new ways to reconcile with the North Korean regime." He said Seoul was now worried that this transfer of North Korean prisoners could hamper efforts to reestablish communication between the North and the South.

In his view, the Lee government is "more open to the idea of reestablishing ties" with Russia, rather than continuing to cooperate with Ukraine. "That's possibly one of the reasons why this government is skeptical about containing military cooperation with Ukrainian military forces, even though there would be a definite military advantage for South Korean military forces," he added.

Ukraine shouldn't expect military support from South Korea

Butyrska said the latest developments indicate a likely further cooling of ties between Kyiv and Seoul.

"The South Korean government wasn't particularly friendly toward us to begin with, and will now likely keep its distance," she said, adding that it would have been better for Kyiv to have stayed quiet.

In return for a gesture of goodwill and "quiet diplomacy," she added, Ukraine might have seen support from South Korea in another form — technology, for example, especially via third countries. While South Korea isn't directly selling weapons to Ukraine, it does deliver to Poland, Finland, the Czech Republic and Romania, and it's pursuing further integration with the European military equipment supply chain.

For Polishchuk, any cooperation on military technology between Ukraine and South Korea is out of the question, now and in the future. He believes trade and humanitarian help would continue, however. South Korea, he said, is highly unlikely to side with Russia, especially given Seoul's many obligations toward the United States.

This article was originally written in Ukrainian.

World.title: Turkey's stock market scandal affects nearly half a million investors. Police have made several arrests and an AKP politician has resigned.
World.content:
Nearly half a million investors are affected, arrests have been made, and a female politician from the ruling party has resigned. What is behind the stock market manipulation scandal in Turkey?

Investors in Turkey want one thing above all else: for their money to retain its value. Given inflation of around 30%, that is not exactly easy. As a result, many people are buying gold, foreign currency or stocks and increasingly, mutual fund shares that promise high returns.

But the stock market has become a trap for around half a million Turkish investors. In mid-September, the benchmark BIST 100 index plummeted by 6% in a single day and lost about 12% within just a few trading days.

This sharp drop in stock prices was triggered by a major market manipulation scandal. Approximately 455,000 investors have been affected, more than 45 people have been arrested and a high-ranking politician from the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP) has resigned.

What happened?

Everything started when some investment fund providers had trouble making timely repayments to investors. Among those affected were funds managed by the companies Pusula Portfoy and Tera. Two Tera funds alone held assets totaling around €6.5 billion ($6.37 billion).

In response, the Capital Markets Board (SPK) intervened and shut down the funds of seven asset managers, including Tera, Pusula and Atlas. According to the state-run news agency Anadolu, a total of 131 funds are set to be liquidated.

The Istanbul Public Prosecutor's Office is now investigating charges of fraud, violations of the capital markets law and the formation of a criminal organization, Justice Minister Akin Gurlek announced.



The suspicion: The fund companies are alleged to have artificially inflated the value of their funds, while in reality their funds contained worthless "junk stocks."

Among the 45 people arrested so far are executives from investment firms. In addition, the assets of 42 individuals and 46 legal entities have been frozen, according to Gurlek on X.

The Istanbul Stock Exchange has also taken action: it excluded 27 stocks from the BIST 100 benchmark index as of October 1.

Will investors get their money back?

The funds are being liquidated: Their assets will be sold and the proceeds distributed to investors in proportion to their fund shares. The deadline for this has been extended from three to six months. According to Aysel Gundogdu, an independent financial advisor in Istanbul, this is intended to reduce selling pressure so that stocks are not sold at fire-sale prices. However, this does not mean that the liquidation of each fund will take six months. Depending on market conditions, it may be completed more quickly.

Only, there is no guarantee. An investment fund is not a savings account and any loss in value affects the investor. Gundogdu expects that money market funds will largely be redeemed. With hedge funds and equity funds holding "junk stocks" that are virtually untradeable, however, the situation could prove more difficult.

It is important to distinguish between market losses and damages resulting from potential irregularities.

Economist and columnist Guldem Atabay emphasized that a distinction must be made between price losses and manipulation: Investors bear the market risk, but they do not have to accept false information, artificially inflated prices, or a lack of oversight.

Are the fund company and managers liable for the damages?

If funds are closed or liquidated, the shares and other securities in the portfolio can be sold. The question is how much they are worth and how easily they can be sold.

Financial expert Gundogdu believes that the fund's assets will not cover investors' claims. Furthermore, she says there have been structural failures. "The crisis is far greater than a simple liquidity crisis. There are flaws in management and oversight."

She therefore considers it possible that the assets of the fund founders and managers could also be tapped to make up for the shortfall.

Economist Atabay calls for those responsible to be identified and for the damages to be recovered from them. Following the liquidation of the funds, it must be clarified who is responsible for any legal violations. "Liquidation is no substitute for accountability," Atabay said.

Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya of the ruling AKP asked Turkish President Erdogan to resign Image: AP Photo/picture alliance

What are the political costs of the crisis?

The crisis has already led to the resignation of a high-ranking female politician in the ruling AKP party. Fatma Betul Sayan Kaya, deputy party chair and former minister of family affairs, asked Turkish President and AKP leader Recep Tayyip Erdogan to "relieve her of all her posts." This has been a phrase frequently used within the AKP for years when someone is forced to resign.

She was facing allegations regarding stock transactions by her and her husband, Ilyas Kaya, in connection with the fund crisis. Political responsibility, she wrote on social media, goes beyond legal responsibility. She said her position should not hinder the investigation.

The opposition now intends to bring the issue before Parliament. Selcuk Ozdag, deputy leader of the Yeni Yol parliamentary group, announced that as soon as Parliament reconvenes, he will submit a motion for a parliamentary investigation. The investigation is intended to determine whether politicians are involved in the manipulation scandal.

This article was originally published in German.

World.title: US pressures EU allies to release diesel stockpiles
World.content:
The Trump administration has called on its European allies, particularly Germany and France, to release strategic diesel reserves in an effort to ease fuel prices. The EU will hold an emergency meeting on Friday.

The United States on Thursday told its European allies, particularly Germany and France, to "immediately" release their strategic reserves of diesel to help lower the soaring price of the refined fuel.

It comes after President Donald Trump on Wednesday floated the possibility of banning US diesel exports to stem the rise in prices.

Average US diesel prices have surged over 70% to $6.39 per US gallon (€1.50 per liter) since the start of the Iran war, according to AAA motor club data.

The surging cost of fuel has stoked public anger and intensified anxiety within Trump's Republican Party that it could lose control of Congress in November's midterm elections.

Germany's ADAC motoring club on Thursday reported an average diesel price of €2.409 per liter ($10.25 per US gallon).

Donald Trump blames Ukraine for record US diesel prices To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video

What did US officials say?

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright told Fox News on Thursday that he was "highly confident" Europe could ease fuel prices by drawing down emergency diesel inventories.

"This is a time for a coordinated release of diesel stores as we ⁠go into ​to harvest season and we go into winter heating oil season," Wright told the US broadcaster. "Now's the time to bring ​more diesel to the market, and that diesel is available. I think we have some positive news coming."

US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said Washington had done its share of an agreement struck in March among International Energy Agency (IEA) ​members in releasing 172 million barrels of US diesel. "America is doing its part," Bessent said on social media. "We look to our allies to match their commitments with action."

"Our European partners should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions," he added.

US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, meanwhile, said there was an "eagerness on both sides to work together" on the diesel issue.

"We know that France, Germany and Italy are sitting on reserves ... ‌I won't ​put words in their mouth, of course, but ​I think they would love to have ⁠a ​cooperative path ​forward with the United ​States on how ‌we get more diesel ​to ⁠market," Greer told a news conference ⁠at a two-day G20 trade ministers' gathering in Milwaukee, USA.

How did the EU respond to the US demand?

The European Union's energy task force will hold an emergency meeting on Friday morning to discuss the situation, a spokeswoman for the European Commission said.

"The diesel market is currently very tight, leading to high prices for consumers across the world," said Anna Kaisa Itkonen, adding that discussions will also involve the IEA, the West's energy watchdog.

"The Commission ... is closely coordinating with EU member states to take stock of the situation and examine appropriate measures to tackle these high prices."

The EU's top energy official Dan Jorgensen was on Thursday in contact with French, German, Italian, Irish and also British authorities to coordinate their positions.

EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic, who was also attending the gathering in Milwaukee, met with his US counterpart Greer but told reporters that they did not go into detail on energy exports.

The EU official said any move by the US to ban diesel exports would be "unexpected for Europeans."

He added that such a ban would have "very dramatic consequences for our economic performance."

Sefcovic said both sides "decided to stay in close touch to avoid any surprises here."

France's minister delegate for international trade, Nicolas Forissier, told the AFP news agency: "I can't imagine that there will be a ban." He stressed that both sides will "try to find solutions."

Germany's Economy Ministry, meanwhile, said the IEA has not yet asked Berlin to release diesel stocks.

World.title: New crew makes the quickest US flight to ISS
World.content:
The SpaceX spacecraft carrying the Crew-13 team docked with the International Space Station in 7 hours and 55 minutes, setting a new record.

Four astronauts docked at the International Space Station (ISS) port on Thursday after completing the fastest flight by a US spacecraft to the outpost, NASA officials said.

The SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket, with the Crew-13 aboard, lifted off at 11:10 a.m. local time (1510 GMT) from Cape Canaveral, Florida, and within 7 hours and 55 minutes, its capsule, SpaceX Dragon "Grace," docked at the ISS — setting a record for a US trip to the ISS.

The flight by the spacecraft was the quickest so far, not only for Elon Musk's company, but for any American entity, including NASA.

The time taken for a trip to the ISS mainly depends on the distance between the ISS and the spacecraft at the time of launch.

The space station's convenient location allowed the spacecraft to reach it faster.

The last crew, which took off from the United States, took more than 30 hours to reach the station.

A Russian Soyuz spacecraft set the overall record for a flight to the ISS in October 2020, reaching the station in just over three hours.

What do we know about the crew?

The new ISS crew was set to arrive in mid-September, however, its flight was delayed due to a leak aboard the Dragon.

It includes Americans Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canadian Joshua Kutryk, and Russian Sergey Teteryatnikov

Watkins, the Crew-13's commander, became the first Black woman to lead a crew to orbit. The crew is slated to stay at the ISS for six months and will be replacing Crew-12, which is set to return to Earth on Monday.

Despite many international cooperation agreements collapsing after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, the United States and other ISS partners still work with Russia on the space station.

The ISS has been continuously in use for the last 25 years. NASA has committed to operating it through 2030.

World.title: Acampadas en España por la vivienda, en directo | El Congreso comienza el debate decisivo de los decretos sobre vivienda
World.content:
Indignación y decepción ante posible caída de los decretos en la sexta noche en Sol

La posible caída de los dos reales decretos de vivienda aprobados este martes en el Consejo de Ministros ha llenado de indignación, rabia y decepción la madrileña plaza de la Puerta del Sol y parte de la calle Arenal, donde la madrugada de este jueves se vive la sexta noche de acampada, con más de 1.300 tiendas y alrededor de 2.000 personas. El no de Junts a los dos reales decretos ha llenado la plaza de gritos de rabia como: “PSOE y PP la misma mierda es”, “No nos vamos, nos quedamos”, “Aquí están los antifascistas”, “Ser policía vergüenza me daría” o “Ayuso dimite, el pueblo no te admite”.

De hecho, se ha producido un momento de tensión cuando un grupo de manifestantes se ha aproximado a las vallas que rodean la Real Casa de Correos, sede del Gobierno de la Comunidad de Madrid. Este conato ha sido disuelto por otros manifestantes que han hecho retroceder a sus compañeros para evitar altercados.

A última hora de este jueves se ha conocido la decisión de Junts de votar en contra de los dos reales decretos si no eran retirados antes de la votación de este viernes por la mañana y se redactaba uno nuevo acorde a sus condiciones. Una decisión que no ha sentado bien entre los manifestantes, pero que, por otra parte, era esperada. “Creo que buena parte de nosotros ya estaba preparada para que no se aprobaran ninguno de los dos decretos”, ha indicado Malena, quien ha añadido que “ya era mala señal que se dividieran en dos”. No obstante, ha indicado que, aunque no se aprueben, van a seguir manifestándose, ya que “esta acampada no es solo por un decreto, sino para cambiar las cosas”.

Además, ha indicado que el siguiente paso, tras la manifestación de este sábado, “debería ser una huelga general”. Para Pol, otro manifestante, la “decepción era previsible”, ya que el Gobierno se encuentra “entre la espada y la pared por un lado u otro” e intentar sacar adelante es “prácticamente imposible porque hay que poner de acuerdo a casi todos los grupos parlamentarios”. “Al final, todo lo que estamos haciendo es para que las cosas cambien y si no cambian, tendremos que seguir manifestándonos”, ha comentado Naya, otra manifestante que ha tenido que situar su tienda en la calle Arenal, puesto que la Puerta del Sol ya no admite más. (Efe)

World.title: La estafa del falso empleado de banca
World.content:
Recibir un SMS que alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en nuestra cuenta bancaria puede evitar que seamos víctima de un robo, excepto si no ha sido el banco quien realmente lo ha emitido

En la estafa del falso empleado de banca el delincuente primero envía un mensaje con una alerta sobre un movimiento sospechoso en la cuenta y facilita un enlace o un número de teléfono al que llamar. Ya en la conversación, intenta convencer a la víctima de que su dinero está en peligro para que autorice operaciones que resultarán fraudulentas

En 2025, Instituto Nacional de Ciberseguridad (INCIBE) registró 25.133 casos de phishing. Durante los dos últimos años, tanto la Policía Nacional como la Guardia Civil y el Banco de España han emitido alertas sobre el aumento de las llamadas de falsos empleados bancarios.

TÉCNICAS DE MANIPULACIÓN

Autoridad Suplantan a profesionales pertenecientes a bancos a los que la víctima concede poder y confianza Urgencia Crean la sensación de que hay poco tiempo para actuar, lo que evita que la víctima reflexione o consulte con alguien Sobrecarga de información técnica Emplean jerga bancaria para intimidar y hacer creer que dominan una situación compleja Aumento gradual de las peticiones Incluye a la víctima en grupos de aplicaciones de mensajería para hacerle creer que mucha gente ya está ganando dinero

CIBEREXPERTO NOMBRE Jordi Sánchez CARGO Experto en fraude de CaixaBank “Durante la llamada, el estafador te hace creer que te está guiando para solucionar tu problema, pero en realidad, está intentando que tu hagas exactamente lo que necesita, emitir operaciones bancarias, descargar aplicaciones o facilitar información, como códigos o datos de tarjetas” Play / Pause CÓMO EVITAR LA ESTAFA DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA 1 Sospechar de mensajes inesperados. No clicar en ningún enlace que aparezca en el mensaje ni llamar al número que ofrecen. Ante la duda, siempre se debe llamar a los números oficiales del banco 2 Desconfiar de la urgencia y de las amenazas.Mensajes como “Su cuenta será bloqueada” buscan que se actúe sin pensar 3 No compartir claves ni códigos de verificación. El banco nunca solicitará contraseñas u otros códigos de seguridad 4 No descargar archivos ni instalar aplicaciones. Los estafadores pueden pedir que se descarguen programas que en realidad les están dando acceso al teléfono de la víctima

Una estafa que ha evolucionado. Este fraude comenzó como un SMS y una llamada, pero hoy se dan variantes como la que busca robar información de las tarjetas bancarias mediante el uso de la tecnología NFC del teléfono móvil. Este sistema de comunicación inalámbrica permite compartir información entre otros, tarjetas y móviles, y realizar pagos sin contacto. Los estafadores solicitan a la víctima que se descargue una aplicación maliciosa y que acerque la tarjeta al smartphone. Así, sus datos son enviados a otro teléfono de los atacantes, donde crearán una tarjeta de forma virtual con la que intentar sacar dinero o comprar en comercios.

El teléfono puede parecer auténtico. Los estafadores pueden hacer que en la pantalla del móvil de la víctima figure el mismo número que utiliza el banco para atender a sus clientes o que el SMS aparezca en el mismo hilo que las comunicaciones legítimas mediante una técnica que se conoce como spoofing (que significa suplantación).

Conocen datos personales de su víctima. En muchos casos, disponen de información de su objetivo, como el banco del que es cliente, parte del DNI o la dirección de correo electrónico.

Si ya se ha caído en la estafa. Se debe poner en conocimiento del banco de inmediato para que se puedan adoptar las medidas operativas oportunas. También es muy importante guardar las evidencias, como capturas de pantalla, SMS, correos y registro de llamadas. Presentar una denuncia ante la Policía Nacional o la Guardia Civil.

OTROS CASOS DEL FALSO EMPLEADO DE BANCA

Cada semana aparecen noticias con nuevas maneras de embaucar a ciudadanos con una estafa de este tipo:

World.title: Vetusta Morla vuelve y el Teatre Lliure cumple 50 años: planes para este fin de semana en Barcelona
World.content:
Octubre empieza con regresos y celebraciones. Vetusta Morla rompe dos años de parón y escoge el Palau Sant Jordi para iniciar una nueva gira, justo un día antes de que Hombres G ocupe el mismo escenario. En Montjuïc, el Teatre Lliure celebra sus 50 años con una gran fiesta y actividades gratuitas, mientras 14 restaurantes compiten por servir las mejores bravas en el Poble Espanyol.

Barcelona es la ciudad escogida para inaugurar la vuelta de la banda de Tres Cantos. Tras dos años de parón que anunciaron para descansar, llega Gira de vuelta. Canciones de ida, una serie de conciertos que empezaron a preparar a principios de año mientras componían un nuevo álbum, todavía sin fecha de publicación, del que de momento solo hay un avance, Si vuelves. La última vez que llenaron el Sant Jordi fue en 2022, cuando presentaron Cable a tierra y, ahora, vuelven a Montjuïc (este viernes a las 21.00) para comprobar cuánto les han echado de menos sus fans. Y el sábado, a la misma hora, será el turno de otra generación: 24 horas después, Hombres G ocuparán el mismo escenario con Los mejores años de nuestra vida, una gira que celebra más de cuatro décadas de carrera.

50 aniversario del Teatre Lliure

Una imagen exterior del Teatre Lliure de Montjuïc. Jordi Borràs / ACN

La plaza Margarida Xirgu será el escenario de la gran fiesta que se ha preparado para celebrar que, hace medio siglo y tras la muerte de Franco, en Montjuïc empezó a abrirse camino una programación de teatro independiente y en catalán. A partir de las 21.00 y con acceso libre y gratuito, habrá sesiones como la de Nao & Marcel DJ Set, conciertos e invitados especiales. Además, para conocer la importancia de este teatro público en la historia de Barcelona, recomendamos reservar plaza en alguna de las visitas guiadas de (Re)Viure el teatre, una experiencia ideada por el dramaturgo Didier Ruiz en la que se pueden visitar los talleres, almacenes o la sastrería del teatro a través de las historias de sus trabajadores y artistas. Hay pases cada 20 minutos de 10.00 a 16.00 Es un fin de semana perfecto para quedarse en Montjuïc, porque el domingo (de 11.00 a 17.00) los jardines de Laribal celebran una comida popular de arroz para recuperar las antiguas fontades. Además, todos los museos de la montaña, como el Pabellón Mies van der Rohe, el Museu Olímpic o el Jardín Botánico, abren sus puertas de forma gratuita.

Las mejores bravas en el Poble Espanyol

Imagen de la ultima edición del Bravas Fest. ARIADNA CREUS

14 restaurantes de Barcelona y alrededores competirán, este fin de semana, para que sus bravas sean las más aclamadas. Desde este viernes hasta el domingo (de 18.00 a 0.00), restaurantes como La Esquinica de Nou Barris, el Tomás de Sarrià, el Xinvic de l’Eixample o el Collonut de Sant Andreu se reúnen en el Mahou Bravas Fest en el Poble Espanyol. Se pueden probar los diferentes menús ideados por cada local con bravas, caña y una tapa especial. Todo, en una cita gastronómica que celebra su quinto aniversario y, por ello, ha invitado a figuras clave de la noche barcelonesa como DJ Amable, Miqui Puig o Axel Pi para ponerse a los platos, además de programar conciertos como el de Hotel Cochambre. La entrada es gratuita hasta completar aforo, así que recomendamos hacer una reserva previa en la web del festival.

World.title: Soy presidente de mi comunidad y el administrador se niega a entregarme el acta de la última junta. ¿Qué puedo hacer?
World.content:
Pregunta. Somos una comunidad de cuatro portales y cuatro presidentes. Yo soy uno de ellos. El 12 de mayo tuvimos reunión general donde se acordó el cambio de presidentes y otras cuestiones, como los arreglos de los tejados. Pedí a la administradora cuatro veces el acta de la reunión general, tanto por WhatsApp como por email y no hay manera de que lo mande. ¿Qué puedo hacer? R. Calzada Gútiez

Respuesta. La Ley de Propiedad Horizontal (LPH) establece en su artículo 19 que el acta debe quedar cerrada con las firmas del presidente y del secretario al finalizar la reunión o dentro de los diez días naturales siguientes. Asimismo, dispone que el acta debe remitirse a los propietarios conforme al procedimiento previsto en la ley. Además, el secretario está obligado a custodiar los libros de actas y a conservar durante cinco años las convocatorias, comunicaciones, apoderamientos y demás documentación relevante de las reuniones.

Estas disposiciones implican que, una vez celebrada la junta, los acuerdos deben formalizarse mediante la correspondiente acta, firmada por el presidente y el secretario dentro del plazo legal, y comunicarse a los propietarios en el domicilio designado a efectos de notificaciones. Por tanto, el secretario-administrador tiene la obligación de remitir a todos los propietarios, incluidos los miembros de la junta, copia del acta con los acuerdos adoptados.

Además, el artículo 20 de la LPH establece entre las funciones del administrador actuar como secretario de la junta y custodiar, a disposición de los propietarios, la documentación de la comunidad. Entre esta documentación se encuentran las actas de las reuniones de los últimos cinco años, que el administrador debe conservar y poner a disposición de los propietarios, junto con cualquier otra documentación comunitaria que pueda solicitarse.

Por ello, si el administrador no ha remitido el acta con los acuerdos aprobados o no facilita el acceso a documentación de interés comunitario, puede exigírsele su entrega mediante un requerimiento fehaciente, como un burofax con certificación de texto y acuse de recibo, fijando un plazo para su cumplimiento.

Si, pese a ello, no atiende el requerimiento, su conducta podría considerarse contraria a sus obligaciones legales y profesionales. En ese caso, podría presentarse una queja ante el Colegio de Administradores al que pertenezca, reclamar los daños y perjuicios que, en su caso, se hayan ocasionado o acordar en junta de propietarios la resolución del contrato de prestación de servicios y el nombramiento de un nuevo administrador.

Si tiene dudas, sugerencias o simplemente quiere contarnos su caso, puede enviarnos un email a vivienda@elpais.es .

World.title: Por el estuario del Tajo, el jardín secreto de Lisboa
World.content:
A solo media hora de la capital de Portugal, en la otra orilla del mar de la Paja, se descubre un paisaje inaudito de arrozales, salinas y marismas rebosantes de aves donde navegan centenarios barcos de madera pintados de alegres colores

Hay estuarios grandes, estuarios muy grandes y luego está el estuario del Tajo, en cuyas riberas viven 2,8 millones de personas, la cuarta parte de la población portuguesa, incluida la de Lisboa. Es un auténtico mar, el Mar da Palha, de la Paja. Dicen que se llama así por los rastrojos que el viento y las corrientes arrastran desde las lezírias ribatejanas, las fértiles llanuras aluviales que el Tajo inunda periódicamente. Miguel Ferrera, patrón que recorre todos los días el último tramo desde el muelle lisboeta de Belém con los veleros de Palmayatchs, les cuenta a los pasajeros otra versión: antiguamente, las naos se desprendían al llegar a Lisboa de la paja que habían usado durante sus navegaciones oceánicas para proteger la porcelana china y otros objetos delicados, para controlar la humedad, para evitar que rodaran los barriles y para alimentar al ganado que iba a bordo. Si esto no es verdad, está bien contado.

Enorme, como el propio estuario del Tajo, es el contraste que hay entre sus dos orillas. La norte es una pura aglomeración urbana. La sur, en cambio, alberga la Reserva Natural do Estuário do Tejo, el mayor humedal de Portugal y de toda Europa occidental. La orilla de Lisboa es como un imán para los viajeros. La otra no suele aparecer en los mapas turísticos. En las guías de Portugal más vendidas en España ni siquiera se menciona. Mejor para nosotros. Viajar es descubrir.

Más información Odemira, una ruta por el concejo del Alentejo más salvaje

El patrón Miguel Ferrera, de Palmayatchs, en el Tajo a su paso por Lisboa. Andrés Campos

Vila Franca de Xira y el ‘Liberdade’

Este viaje comienza en Vila Franca de Xira, una población situada a 30 kilómetros de Lisboa, en la parte más angosta del estuario, justo donde el dulce Tajo desagua en el salobre mar de la Paja. Allí, en el puerto fluvial, a la vista del puente Marechal Carmona —el más antiguo de los que atraviesan el estuario, inaugurado en diciembre de 1951—, nos está esperando el Liberdade, un colorido barco de madera de 18 metros, 40 toneladas, dos velas, proa alta y fondo chato, idóneo para navegar por estos baixos. Botado en 1945, es una reliquia de los días en que aún no se habían construido los gigantescos puentes sobre el estuario y todo el transporte de mercancías y pasajeros se hacía en fragatas, falúas, cangueiros, botes, canoas, catraios y varinos como este. Durante los años sesenta, el río iba cargado con basura de Lisboa a la ribera sur, dejando un rastro de hojas de col, cabezas de sardinas y borra de café en la melena rubia del mar de la Paja. En ningún otro lugar de Europa había tantos y tan variados barcos tradicionales. Eran miles y hoy apenas quedan 70.

Con el Liberdade se puede ir en tres horas hasta el Parque das Nações de Lisboa. Aproar con un varino hacia esta futurista arquitectura de cristal y acero es como arrimarse a la Estación Espacial Internacional en un dirigible de lona. Otra posibilidad es recorrer los mouchões (islas) y riberas de la reserva natural, hoy un paisaje de ensueño, pero antaño una pesadilla para los campesinos que se consumían de hambre, cansancio y paludismo trabajando en los arrozales, tal como denunció Alves Redol en su novela Gaibéus (1939): “Les anda en las muñecas un cansancio que pide descanso, pero el trabajo no puede parar. No puede parar, porque allá abajo, en el aposento, el patrón está haciendo cuentas de la cosecha... Parece que de los brazos se hubieran caído las carnes y solo quedaran los huesos, como tomados por el reuma, y los tendones tensos, como correas de trilladoras en movimiento. Los pechos jadean, las piernas se doblan”.

Exterior de la biblioteca nacional la Fábrica das Palavras. en Vila Franca de Xira (Portugal). Andrés Campos

Por cierto, que en Vila Franca de Xira, de donde era Redol, hay un excelente museo del Neo-Realismo, el movimiento que él encabezó en Portugal. Y también, ya que hablamos de libros, hay una biblioteca deslumbrante, en un modernísimo edificio con vistas al Tajo, obra de Miguel Arruda. Antes era una fábrica de arroz. Ahora es (así le dicen) la Fábrica das Palavras.

EVOA: la torre de control de 120.000 aves

Nos despedimos del Liberdade y, ya en coche, cruzamos el Tajo por el puente Marechal Carmona y cogemos el primer desvío a la derecha para dirigirnos al centro de visitantes EVOA, un hermoso edificio bioclimático de madera que es algo así como la torre de control de las 120.000 aves que se concentran en la reserva: flamencos, gansos, cercetas y, sobre todo, avocetas, el 25% de todas las que invernan en Europa. No menos espectacular que el centro y las lagunas que lo rodean es el camino de 12 kilómetros que lleva hasta allí, entre arrozales tan inmensos que no hay manos suficientes para sembrarlos y es necesario hacerlo con avionetas. Al ser de tierra apisonada, el camino obliga a conducir despacio, observando a la desavisada avifauna como desde un hide. Así alucinamos viendo cómo las garzas reales se quedan inmóviles delante de nuestro vehículo, muy estiradas y con las alas semiabiertas, aprovechando al máximo el calor del sol otoñal. Es eso o lo que los ornitólogos llaman la postura del exhibicionista, la del cortejo, y nos hemos interpuesto sin querer entre la garza y el garzo.

El centro de visitantes EVOA, cerca de Vila Franca de Xira, en el estuario del Tajo. Andrés Campos

En el centro de visitantes EVOA se ofrecen recorridos guiados a pie o en minibús eléctrico alrededor de las tres lagunas del espacio, la Principal, la Rasa y la Grande, que suman 70 hectáreas. Rodeándolas, se descubren un montón de aves y otro aún más numeroso y colorido de libélulas: alguaciles comunes, vigilantes escarlatas, gallardetes listados norteños, azulillos de Graells… A los visitantes se les explica que esta última especie, la Ischnura graellsii, fue bautizada así en honor de Mariano de la Paz Graells, el naturalista riojano que descubrió la mariposa Graellsia, la reina alada de España. En el EVOA hay también una exposición inmersiva para sobrevolar y sentir la reserva como un pájaro, actividades para niños y rutas para ver cómo ha evolucionado el trabajo en los arrozales o cómo siguen descorchando a mano los alcornoques que asombran las dehesas ribereñas.

Un azulillo de graells, junto al centro de visitantes EVOA. Andrés Campos

Atardecer en la playa dos Moinhos

Entre dehesas de alcornoques discurre la carretera por la que nos acercamos a Alcochete. Los bichos que pacen en ellas nos recuerdan que estamos en el corazón taurino de Portugal. En Alcochete también hay un barco tradicional para pasear por el estuario, el Leão. Aunque el mejor paseo que puede darse aquí es a pie, caminando al atardecer desde el barrio de Barrocas —humilde pero encantador, con sus casitas de colores apiñadas en la ribera— hasta el final de la playa dos Moinhos, un arenal de 2,5 kilómetros donde el viento movía antaño tres molinos —ahí siguen en pie, uno de ellos rehabilitado como vivienda— y hoy las cometas de los kitesurfers. En Alcochete presumen mucho de ser la cuna del rey Manuel I. Pero presumen aún más de sus puestas de sol.

El eclipse solar del 12 de agosto, que en muchos lugares de la península lo vieron apiñados en los cerros, aquí se disfrutó después de una larga siesta en las tumbonas del Kimoa Beach Bar. El paisaje es de salvapantallas, con las barcas varadas en la orilla, las cometas en segundo término y, al fondo, el gigantesco puente Vasco da Gama. El eclipse aquí no era total, pero molaba más.

Unas salinas y un molino de mareas

Vista de las salinas de Samouco, junto a la localidad portuguesa de Alcochete. Andrés Campos

Al lado mismo de Alcochete, detrás de la playa, se encuentran las salinas de Samouco, que en su día fueron las más importantes del país y hoy son las únicas del estuario que mantienen alguna actividad, bien es verdad que de forma testimonial. Dos senderos circulares de 4,5 y 7,8 kilómetros permiten recorrer este laberinto acuático, observando flamencos, garzas, cigüeñuelas y otras 167 especies de aves. También se ve una manada de burros mirandeses —una raza en peligro de extinción, introducida aquí para su crianza y preservación que campa a sus anchas por este espacio natural, mordisqueando con fruición las plantas saladas, como si fueran snacks—. Hablando de snacks, en la tienda que hay en la entrada de las salinas se puede comprar la sal que se produce de forma artesanal en la Marinha do Canto. La más interesante gastronómicamente es la flor de sal, la que se forma en la superficie de las balsas los días de sol y viento seco. También se puede adquirir salicornia, una planta salada que se usa para decorar platos de pescado o como guarnición, cruda, cocida o salteada.

Burros mirandeses en las salinas de Samouco, en Alcochete. Andrés Campos

Para ir de Alcochete a Montijo, siguiente destino, hay que pasar por debajo de la autopista A-12, que aquí mismo comienza a elevarse para cruzar el estuario por el puente Vasco da Gama, el más largo de la Unión Europea: ¡17 kilómetros! Gracias al puente —o por su culpa, según se mire—, Montijo se ha convertido en una ciudad-dormitorio, un arrabal más de la cercana capital lusa que, sin embargo, aún conserva un insólito testimonio de su rústico pasado: el Moinho de Maré do Cais das Faluas, un molino de mareas que fue propiedad de la Orden de Santiago y que ahora, impecablemente restaurado, nos devuelve a los tiempos en que el estuario del Tajo era una fuente de vida y no un mero obstáculo. A Lisboa podemos regresar en media hora, cruzando el estuario por el puente Vasco de Gama. O volver por donde hemos venido a Montijo, tardando el doble. Si no se tiene prisa, es mejor esto último. Y más barato.

Comer y dormir con vistas al Tajo

Para comer y/o cenar a lo largo de esta ruta, existen varias opciones interesantes. En Vila Franca de Xira, hay un restaurante de ambiente taurino a más no poder, Cabeça de Toiro, y otro donde se come moderno y mejor que bien, 150 Gramas. En Alcochete, sería una lástima no probar la cataplana de Don Peixe y los pescados a la brasa de Cantinho do Ti Tonho. De postre, nada como las típicas e hipercalóricas fogaças que hacen en Padaria Piqueira.

Una de las empleadas de la panadería Padaira Piqueira, en Alcochete. Andrés Campos

Para dormir, no está nada mal el Lezíria Parque Hotel, en Vila Franca de Xira, con amplias habitaciones, buena cocina y un precio muy razonable para hallarse en las vecindades de Lisboa. En Alcochete, en una finca ajardinada con piscina y vistas al estuario, se encuentra la Quinta Praia das Fontes, del siglo XVI. Dispone de habitaciones dobles, apartamentos y villas. Y si preferimos pernoctar en Lisboa, podemos hacerlo sin apartar la mirada del Tajo en el Hotel Dom Pedro, un alojamiento de la cadena Radisson situado en el alto y elegante barrio de Amoreiras, que domina a vista de gaviota la ciudad y el estuario. No se abarca todo el estuario, porque es enorme —¡340 kilómetros cuadrados!, más que el delta del Ebro—, pero sí se llega a ver desde el puente 25 de Abril hasta el Vasco da Gama, que distan 14 kilómetros.

World.title: Inflation rate rose slightly in August
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

New numbers from the Dutch statistics agency CBS show the inflation rate rose slightly in August.

The preliminary estimate from the Central Agency for Statistics shows a 0.1% rise from August, putting September’s inflation rate at 3.4%.

The final numbers will be released on October 13.

Fuel and energy prices account for most of the increase. The cost of petrol and gas for heating is was up 13.9% in September over the same month the year before.

Grocery prices, however, have dropped slightly for the second month in a row. Food staples were down 1.3% over the year before, after dropping 0.5% in August.

World.title: The Netherlands had its first TV broadcast 75 years ago
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Seventy-five years ago today, the Dutch had their first opportunity to watch a television broadcast: a performance of the play De Toverspiegel, live from a studio in Bussum.

The Royal Family watched the 90-minute production from the Soestdijk Palace.

Concerns about television’s corrupting influence on society and a focus on post-war reconstruction meant that the Netherlands entered the television era only in 1951, later than the United Kingdom or the United States.

The BBC had begun broadcasting in 1936.

The country had around 500 television sets at the time. Radio was the much more widely consumed medium, with around 250,000 devices in homes across the Netherlands.

A television set cost 785 guilders, about a third of the average annual salary, putting the luxury good far out of reach for most of the country.

Media historian Huub Wijfjes told the NOS that initial television broadcasts simply copied whatever was on the radio. “TV took a dominant position and reached its peak in the 60s, 70s, and 80s. The medium displaced radio,” he said.

By 1956, there were 75,000 television sets in the country.

On the website for the Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision, you can watch the early broadcasts.

World.title: Israeli group disrupts Delft screening of Gaza documentary Naza
World.content:
A premiere screening of the documentary Naza, which investigates the killing of civilians by the Israeli military in Gaza, was interrupted in a Delft cinema on Thursday afternoon by a woman taking a microphone and addressing the audience about the October 7 massacres.

She stood in front of the screen midway through the film and began describing how her family members were murdered during the Hamas attacks that sparked the Gaza war in 2023.

The crowd booed her off stage, the microphone was disabled, some shouted “shame on you”, though some applauded her. The woman’s name is Sabine Taasa, a French-Israeli citizen from a town near the Gaza strip and who lost her husband and a son during the attacks.

An Israeli activist group Ad Kan accompanied Taasa to the screening. The group describes itself as former army and intelligence officers who infiltrate and obstruct what they say are anti-Israeli and anti-Semitic activities in foreign countries.

Another member tried to project footage from the October 7 attacks in the cinema while Taasa spoke, according to broadcaster NOS.

Naza, which has been lauded by critics, consists of anonymous interviews with 24 members of Israeli intelligence and military services. They describe how they attacked Gaza, how AI systems were used to select targets, and the policies toward collateral damage and loss of innocent life.

Some describe killing hundreds of civilians at a time to target single military figures; others describe using surveillance techniques to wait for militants to be at home with their families before striking – a tactic known as “where’s daddy”.

Israeli officials have condemned the film, with prime minister Netanyahu pledging to strip the film makers of their citizenship. Other military figures have disputed the claims made in the film and branded it propaganda.

Dutch-Israeli relations have been strained recently over the decision to ban imports of goods from illegal settlements in occupied Palestinian territories. Dutch diplomats have had their status stripped in response.

World.title: Late goal earns Oranje 2-2 draw with Greece
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Netherlands avoided a first defeat under head coach Xavi Hernandez on Thursday night, coming back from 2-0 down to draw 2-2 with Greece in the Nations League.

Substitute Tijjani Reijnders scored the equaliser from close range in the 89th minute in Thessaloniki.

Greece, who had already won away against Serbia and Germany, made it 2-0 on the stroke of half-time.

Xavi brought on Noa Lang, Ryan Gravenberch and Reijnders at the break for Van Bommel, Guus Til and Quinten Timber.

Captain Virgil van Dijk headed in a goal from the corner at 59 minutes in.

Denzel Dumfries twice had the ball in the net, but both goals were ruled out for offside.

Reijnders then scored the equaliser in the 89th minute. The Netherlands has now conceded in 11 consecutive matches, their longest run since a 16-game streak between 1956 and 1958.

“The way it went in the first half was unacceptable,” Van Dijk told broadcaster NOS. “We were outplayed before the break and that simply can’t happen. We showed a lot of good things in the second half, but that has to be there from the start.”

Oranje opened the campaign with a 1-1 draw against Germany in Amsterdam before beating Serbia in Belgrade. The draw leaves them on 5 points from 3 games, 2 behind Greece.

World.title: Real estate agents to face mandatory register as self-regulation
World.content:
The government plans to introduce a register of real estate agents as well as a complaints desk for buyers and sellers after an investigation revealed widespread dissatisfaction with the industry.

In a letter to parliament on Thursday, housing minister Elanor Boekholt-O’Sullivan said the moves come after attempts to get the sector to regulate itself had failed.

“Unfortunately, I must conclude that the professional associations are unable to take the necessary further steps,” the D66 minister wrote.

Until 2001, real estate agents had to be licensed, like lawyers and architects. Currently, anyone can call themselves a real estate agent and while there are two trade organisations in the Netherlands, both say they don’t have the ability to stand up to unscrupulous agents.

“We have consistently said over the past few years that a voluntary approach does not work here. The minister is now drawing the same conclusion,” Tristan Bons, deputy director of real estate association Vastgoed Nederland said in a statement.

According to Bons, the association doesn’t have the power to punish anyone as membership is voluntary and problem agents can simply leave the group.

Nearly a third of the respondents to the government-commissioned survey had at least one negative experience with a real estate agent. Almost 90% of those complaints involved an agent affiliated with a trade association.

Just 2% of people made an official complaint. Complaints vary from passing along confidential information to driving up the price of housing.

In August, homeowners association Vereniging Eigen Huis said it had received 900 reports between February and July on a special hotline for issues with real estate agents. Issues ranged from buyers feeling pressure to bid beyond their budgets to agents favouring certain clients over others.

More than 30 million people visited a museum in the Netherlands in 2025, a 2.5% increase over the year prior, according to trade association Museumvereniging.

Dutch museums welcomed 31.6 million visitors in 2025, almost back to pre-pandemic levels. In 2019, museums saw 32.6 million guests.

Nearly 90% of Dutch people go to a museum at least once a year, the Museumcijfers 2025 report found.

In 2025 the Netherlands had 492 registered museums. Most institutions are history museums, making up 62%, followed by art museums, which account for 24%.

The use of the yearly Museum Card hit a record high of 9.7 million visits in 2025. Visits using the subscription service is up 5% over the 2019 peak.

A recent survey by Ipsos I&O found that trust in museums is high and most adults consider them to be an important part of society.

World.title: Golf to a Japanese garden: 13 great things to do in October
World.content:
It’s October and the cultural season is off to a good start. There are lots of restful established names in this month’s cultural offerings, with some modern challenges mixed in.

Experience Butoh

It’s the 10th edition of the Butoh Festival at the Teatro Munganga in Amsterdam this month. Fourteen dancers from Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, Mexico, Taiwan and the UK will be performing their interpretation of the avant-garde “dance of darkness”, which originated in Japan after the devastation of the atomic bombs. October 2 and 3. Website

Get your skates on for some colf

It is touted as the earliest depiction of golf: Hendrick Avercamp’s Colf Players on the Ice dating from around 1625. Then as now, the players in the foreground look like well-to-do-gentlemen while in the back two others seem to be playing a game of ice hockey.

The Rijksmuseum and the Mauritshuis have just bought the painting for an eyewatering €11.4 million from a private owner in the United States. It will go on show in Avercamp’s home town of Kampen as part of the exhibition Averkamp back in Kampen: the 17th century through the eyes of Hendrick and Barent. (Barent, Hendrick’s nephew, also specialised in winter landscapes) From October 3. Website

Believe it (or not)

In a time when scientific fact is regarded as just another opinion, the Teylers Museum in Haarlem is mounting Zeker Weten? (Are we sure?), an exhibition around the five tenets of scientific research: prove, repeat, modify, check and build.

That is exactly what the scientists of yore did, for instance when sightings of black swans overturned the assumption that only white ones existed, and the discovery in 1938 of a coelacanth, which proved it was not extinct. Historical books, models and instruments illustrate the search for “exact” science. From October 2. Website

Meet Matisse at the H’ART

The H’ART Museum in Amsterdam has unselfishly offered to relieve the soon-to-be refurbished Centre Pompidou of its Matisse collection, along with other paintings by the likes of Mark Rothko, Pablo Picasso, and Barnett Newman that also needed a new temporary home.

Chez Matisse – Masterpieces from the Centre Pompidou, comprises some 80 works, including La Blouse roumaine, which is hardly ever allowed off the Pompidou premises. The collection follows Matisse as he experimented with colour and shapes, culminating in his work at the Chapelle du Rosaire in Vence. From October 3. Website

Catch a De Kooning

The Rijksmuseum blockbuster this autumn is a retrospective of Dutch abstract expressionist painter Willem de Kooning (1904-1997) which puts his drawings centre stage. De Kooning left his native Rotterdam at age 24 and entered the United States as a stowaway. Willem de Kooning at work shows over 120 drawings, and some of his sculptures and paintings, mapping out De Kooning’s journey from house painter to important innovator of modern art. From October 6. Website

Get a taste of Japan in The Hague

The Japanese Garden at the Clingendael Estate in The Hague, which opens for a few weeks every year, is more popular than ever. Make sure you get your ticket for a slot to see its autumnal splendour. From October 10. Website

Cock a snoot at speculators

Plus ça change…Cherry Town is a jolly musical romp about housing shortage, corruption and the healing power of love, based on the operetta by Russian composer Dmitri Shostakovich written in 1959. Performed by the Dutch National Opera and supported by the Netherlands Philharmonic, the comical shenanigans of speculators and indignant tenants are a treat for young (from 10) and old. Sung in English. October 8-20. Website

Remember Marisol

The Boijmans van Beuningen museum in Rotterdam has dusted off the largely forgotten work of Marisol (1930-2016), a Venezuelan artist whose playful wooden sculptures about serious subjects, such as women’s rights and the environment, became popular in the 1960s. The museum organised her first solo show and The Car became one of its most celebrated exhibits. From October 9. Website

Say hello to Whistler’s mum

Van Gogh liked and wrote about many of his contemporaries, including James Whistler, which spurred the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam to organise the major retrospective Whistler, Dandy and Disruptor. The dandy bit refers to his dashing looks while his l’art pour l’art attitude upset the critics of the time.

His most famous painting Arrangement in Gray and Black, No. 1, better known, to his annoyance, as Whistler’s Mother, moved Van Gogh, who said it reminded him of his own mother. From October 16. Website

..and see his take on Amsterdam

At the same time as the main exhibition in Amsterdam, the Mesdag Collection in The Hague presents Whistler. Loving the Netherlands. The painter visited the Netherlands 10 times, resulting in etchings and atmospheric watercolours.

With dandyish good taste, he chastised his Dutch fellow artists: “You Dutch painters don’t know what you’re missing by neglecting your beautiful city of Amsterdam, which I find more beautiful than Venice.” From October 16. Website

Explore some great design ideas

Dutch Design Week is ‘returning to RAW or Rebel Authentic Worth, unpolished and real”, so prepare to get basic. The Sausage Stool (Wuerstelhocker), a sausage-shaped perch on which to enjoy a wuerstel (and future sausage stool), is a case in point.

Eindhoven becomes the focal point of international creative ideas on serious subjects such as sustainability, new materials, technology, education, play and much, much more. October 17-25. Website

Get to know Eve at the Vrijthof

The Fotomuseum aan het Vrijthof in Maastricht presents All About Eve, a retrospective of celebrated Magnum photographer Eve Arnold. The selection of 150 photographs focuses on her work from the 50s, 60s and 70s and includes images of famous filmstars and several series, including Malcolm X and Fashion Shows in Harlem. From October 19. Website

Get a buzz at the ADE

The 30th edition of the electronic music festival Amsterdam Dance Event is about to be unleashed on the capital, featuring, among many others, the Concertgebouw Orchestra playing Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony against the background of Einder, an artificial and ever-changing sky of floaty fabric covering the vast Centrale Markthal.

The ADE is also putting in a special appearance at the Van Gogh Museum (see above) on October 23, when electronic music band Devon Rexi and musician Coby Sey will respond electronically to Whistler’s work Nocturnes. October 21-25. Website

World.title: Young Amsterdammers drink less as ketamine gains ground
World.content:
Young people in Amsterdam are drinking less alcohol, but drugs like ketamine have become far more popular at the same time, according to an annual monitor of drug and alcohol use commissioned by addiction care organisation Jellinek.

The researchers say Gen Z drinks less often and more consciously, partly because of rising prices.

The Antenne Amsterdam 2025 report was published on Wednesday by the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (HvA). It draws on a survey of 1,183 vocational college (mbo) students, interviews with 22 nightlife insiders and five youth workers, and close to 5,000 drug samples handed in to testing services.

Of the students surveyed, 59% had drunk alcohol in the past year and 46% in the past four weeks. Both figures are lower than among their peers at hbo colleges and universities.

Ketamine on the rise

Ketamine use is widespread in Amsterdam’s nightlife and has risen sharply again since 2024, the report says. Ketamine, MDMA and other powder drugs are relatively cheap, going for €25-30 per gram, and are easily obtained via home delivery services.

Demand for 3-MMC, a synthetic stimulant, appears barely affected by a ban on several groups of related substances that took effect on July 1 last year. Drugs sold as 3-MMC often turn out to contain other substances, such as 2-MMC.

Among vocational students, however, 3-MMC is relatively rare: 7% have ever tried it and 5% used it in the past year. Laughing gas has almost disappeared since the sales ban. Just 9% of students said they had ever used it, down from 24% in 2021.

Vaping and gambling

Fewer students smoke than in previous years, but nicotine products remain popular. Some 24% smoke, 18% vaped in the past four weeks, and 7% used nicotine pouches, known as snus.

The share of students who gambled online in the past year has tripled, from 6% in 2021 to 18%. The researchers caution that the question was worded differently in 2025.

Less drinking is a positive development but it brings new concerns, Jellinek prevention specialist Raoul Koning said in a statement. He named vaping, snus, 3-MMC, ketamine, and gambling as particular problems.

If you are concerned about your own or someone else’s use of alcohol, drugs, or gambling, the Jellinek addiction helpline can be reached on 088 505 1220 or at jellinek.nl. The line is staffed in Dutch and English on weekdays, 1pm to 5pm.

World.title: Polish president backs down and approves government’s windfall tax on fuel companies
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. President Karol Nawrocki has reversed course and signed into law a windfall tax on fuel companies’ excess profits that he had previously blocked. The government had been pushing the president to approve the measures amid soaring fuel prices. In announcing his decision on Thursday, Nawrocki, who is aligned with the opposition, insisted that he now expected the government to move to lower fuel prices for consumers. A few hours later, the government confirmed that it would do so, and on Friday morning it announced cuts in VAT and excise duty on fuels. Nie pozwolę rządowi dłużej odsuwać od siebie odpowiedzialności za tę trudną sytuację. Podpisałem ustawę dotyczącą nadmiarowych zysków koncernów paliwowych i zakończę proces ustawiania Polaków w roli politycznych zakładników. To rząd ponosi pełną odpowiedzialność za ceny paliw -… pic.twitter.com/7AX8v4a9Q0 — Kancelaria Prezydenta RP (@prezydentpl) October 1, 2026 The windfall tax will levy a one-off charge of 60% of excess profits from liquid fuel sales, calculated as the amount that would have been generated using a company’s average 2025 fuel sales margin, increased by 20%. It is expected to raise around 4 billion zloty (€914 million). When announcing the plans, the finance ministry said the levy was justified by this year’s “exceptional economic and geopolitical conditions that have led to above-average financial results in a specific segment of the fuel sector, not resulting from improved operational efficiency…but from a supply shock”. The tax was intended to offset some of the roughly 4.7 billion zloty the government spent on keeping fuel prices lower for consumers amid the crisis in the Middle East by cutting VAT and excise duty and introducing a maximum daily price. Those measures were initially in place from March to June. However, in July, Nawrocki announced that he would not sign the windfall tax into law. He instead sent it to the Constitutional Tribunal (TK) for assessment. That process can take years, effectively killing off the bill. The president argued that the proposed measures “raised serious constitutional concerns”. In particular, he criticised the fact that the tax would be retroactive, applying to revenue earned from the beginning of March. Since then, he and the government have been locked in a dispute over the issue, with Prime Minister Donald Tusk arguing that measures to reduce fuel prices, which were briefly reintroduced in the last two weeks of August, can only be restored if Nawrocki signs the windfall tax. Nawrocki’s office, however, has argued that fuel companies would pass the costs of the tax onto consumers, therefore actually increasing prices. President @NawrockiKn has obstructed a planned windfall tax on fuel companies by sending it to the constitutional court, where it could stay for years The tax aimed to offset fuel price protection costs after the Iran war surgehttps://t.co/UojVuYhvdV — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 27, 2026 In September, the government’s majority in parliament passed the windfall tax bill a second time. And Nawrocki has now backed down, announcing in a recorded speech on Thursday evening that he would sign the bill into law. However, he has still asked the TK to assess its constitutionality. Nawrocki declared that he was seeking to call the government’s bluff. He claimed that they were actually hoping the windfall tax would fail so that the treasury could continue obtaining normal tax revenue from high fuel prices, as well as dividends from state oil giant Orlen. By signing the bill, the president said he was “ending the process of holding Poles hostage”. He now expected the government to “immediately” reintroduce measures to bring down prices at petrol stations, as well as the cost of fuel for farmers. To nie ja wygrałem. Wygrali Polacy, którzy już w weekend zapłacą mniej za paliwa. — Donald Tusk (@donaldtusk) October 1, 2026 In response, government spokesman Adam Szłapka told broadcaster TVN that they were ready to make the necessary decisions to reduced prices on Friday and that the measures could be in force already by the weekend. “It’s good that the president has stopped blocking this,” he said. On Friday morning, the government announced that it would reduce VAT on fuels from 23% to 8% and cut excise duty – both measures it also used earlier this year. The new policies will be in place until 31 December. Energy minister Miłosz Motyka told Polskie Radio that maximum daily prices would also be reintroduced. Earlier, on Thursday evening, finance minister Andrzej Domański announced on social media that he estimated fuel costs would be reduced by 1.2-1.3 zloty per litre once the subsidies were reintroduced. According to price monitoring service ePetrol, diesel prices are currently averaging around 9.14 zloty per litre while PB95 petrol is at 8.19 zloty. Those are both record highs. Ustawa o podatku od nadmiarowych zysków koncernów paliwowych właśnie wpłynęła do RCL. Jeszcze dziś będzie ogłoszona. Oznacza to, że już w weekend ceny na stacjach paliwowych będą niższe. Szacunkowo o około 1,2-1,3 zł na litrze. I po co były te gierki, Panie Prezydencie? — Andrzej Domański (@Domanski_Andrz) October 1, 2026 The dispute over financing fuel price cuts comes at a time of growing concern over Poland’s public finances, something Nawrocki referred to in his address on Thursday. Poland has been running one of the EU’s highest deficits, despite the government committing to bringing it down after being placed under the EU’s excessive deficit procedure. Public debt passed the EU’s limit of 60% of GDP for the first time this year. Last month, Moody’s, one of the big three global credit rating agencies, lowered Poland’s rating from A2 to A3, pointing to a “deteriorating” fiscal situation and the “limited willingness or ability” of the authorities to take necessary action. The last time the country was at A3 level was in 2002. World.title: Leading Polish business owners invest in small nuclear reactor venture
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A group of prominent Polish businesspeople have announced that they are investing in a project to develop small modular nuclear reactors being led by the country’s richest man, Michał Sołowow. Among them are Rafał Brzoska, founder of delivery giant InPost, and Mati Staniszewski, CEO of ElevenLabs, a leading artificial intelligence firm. The group is investing 500 million zloty (€114 million) in Sołowow’s Synthos Green Energy (SGE), which, together with 1.35 billion zloty from foreign investors, will secure the company’s financing for the next two years as it seeks to roll out BWRX-300 reactors in Poland, Central and Eastern Europe and the UK. As a European SMR development platform headquartered in Warsaw, Poland’s energy security is of special importance to us. We are proud to announce that today our founder, Michał Sołowow, unveiled a PLN 500 million investment by a group of leading Polish entrepreneurs in SGE’s… pic.twitter.com/J2SerVjIlG — SGE (@SGE_Nuclear) September 30, 2026 The investment, which was formally announced at a business conference in Warsaw on Wednesday, comes as Sołowow seeks to expand his nuclear project beyond SGE’s troubled partnership with Polish state energy giant Orlen, where disagreements have delayed plans to build SMRs in Poland. Alongside Brzoska and Staniszewski, the other new investors are Dariusz Gałęzewski, co-founder of drinks maker Oshee; Krzysztof Pawiński, CEO of food company Maspex; Michał Brański of media group Wirtualna Polska; and Michał Wypychewicz of ZPUE, the largest manufacturer of transformer stations in Europe. “They invested their own private funds because they understood the problem and then believed in the concept and the solution,” Sołowow told Business Insider Polska. SMRs, which are prefabricated in factories before being installed on site, are seen by their proponents as a fast and cost-effective way of installing nuclear capacity. In July, SGE announced plans to build 14 BWRX-300 reactors with a combined capacity of 4.2 gigawatts (GW) across three sites in the UK, which it said would generate enough electricity to meet 11% of the country’s demand. The company also hopes to deploy up to 26 reactors across six locations in Poland. The BWRX-300 is a 300-megawatt water-cooled small modular reactor. Construction of the first ever unit began in Canada in 2025, with completion planned for 2029 and commercial operation expected in 2030. Synthos Green Energy, a firm owned by Polish billionaire Michał Sołowow, has announced plans to build 14 small modular nuclear reactors in the UK. It says that the £35 billion project could deliver enough power to meet 11% of the UK’s demand https://t.co/YTMIzYERuJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 2, 2026 Brzoska said that developing SMR technology “is an investment in Poland’s future”, because without “reliable, predictable and competitively priced energy…it is difficult to talk seriously about further growth in industry, data centres, artificial intelligence, automation or modern logistics”. Staniszewski, whose company recently received an $11 million investment from Poland’s state-owned National Development Bank (BGK) to establish an AI development centre in Poland, said lower electricity prices were important for the sector. SGE notes that demand for electricity is set to rise 40% in Poland over the next 14 years, according to grid operator PSE. Electricity prices have risen rapidly in recent years and are now the second most expensive in the European Union in relation to the cost of living. Poland has recorded the EU's third-fastest rise in household electricity prices this year. The country now also has the bloc’s second-most-expensive electricity, when taking cost of living into account https://t.co/WNLdCfOP16 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 30, 2025 Poland remains the EU’s most coal-dependent country, with more than half of its electricity generated from coal. Over the past decade, however, the country has diversified its energy mix, with the share of renewable energy sources tripling to nearly 30% in 2025. Poland plans to reduce its reliance on coal further, including through the construction of its first nuclear power plant (of the traditional type, not an SMR). The 3.75-gigawatt project is scheduled to be commissioned in 2036. Sołowow has also been pursuing the deployment of SMRs in Poland through Orlen Synthos Green Energy (OSGE), a joint venture between SGE and state energy giant Orlen, Poland’s largest company, to develop BWRX-300 reactors in Poland. OSGE is seeking a so-called contract for difference (CfD) framework, an agreement with a state that guarantees a fixed price for electricity and helps shield developers from market swings, covering 14 reactors at three sites. Polish state energy firm Orlen has announced an agreement to build the country’s first small modular nuclear reactor (SMR). It says Poland will be the first country in Europe to deploy an SMR developed by US-based firm GE Hitachi Nuclear Energy https://t.co/MPWXS3qZ1d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 28, 2025 The project, however, has been delayed by disagreements between the two shareholders. Sołowow told Business Insider Polska that they reached an agreement last month that would allow construction of two reactors to move forward, but said he regretted entering into the partnership with Orlen. “I find it deeply regrettable, because it is precisely due to Orlen’s unnecessary involvement that we are discussing this project in political terms, even though it is not a political project,” he said. Sołowow has argued that a private-sector model can shorten construction times and improve cost control compared with traditional state-led nuclear projects. At the same time, he has highlighted the importance of the state’s role in implementing the project, saying its success depends on coordination between private investors and state policy. This includes contracts for difference, administrative procedures and the preparedness of the nuclear regulator. World.title: Activists launch world’s first abortion pill delivery locker in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Activists in Poland have launched what they say is the world’s first delivery locker that provides women with abortion pills, access to which is normally tightly restricted. They have placed the device opposite parliament in Warsaw, a location intended to send a message to the politicians who have made Poland’s abortion laws among the strictest in the world. The locker (called an “abortomat” in Polish, combining the words aborcja, meaning abortion, and automat, meaning an automatic machine) has been launched by Women Help Women (WHW), a global organisation that provides “self-managed abortion”, and Abortion Dream Team (ADT), a Polish activist group. They emphasise that the installation “is completely real [and] not an artistic performance”. It consists of 22 numbered lockers and a numeric keypad. Women who have contacted WHM seeking an abortion are given a six-digit PIN code that opens one of the doors, inside which is a package containing the pills. Recipients can either take the pills at home or do so in a specially prepared space opened last year by ADT and where the locker is located. The activists emphasise that such delivery mechanisms for abortion pills are particularly important in Poland because of the country’s highly restrictive laws. Abortions are only allowed in two circumstances: if pregnancy is the result of a crime (such as rape or incest) or if it threatens the mother’s life or health. As a result, only 851 legal terminations took place in Poland last year. However, activist groups such as WHW, ADT and Women on Web (WOW) say that they help tens of thousands of women in Poland obtain abortions each year through other means, in particular by providing pills. But they face legal risks for doing so: assisting someone in obtaining an unlawful abortion is a crime punishable by up to three years in prison. In 2023, ABW activist Justyna Wydrzyńska was convicted of that offence. Two years later, the sentence was annulled on a technicality and a new trial was ordered. Polish activist Justyna Wydrzyńska, who was convicted for providing abortion pills to a pregnant woman, has succeeded in having the conviction overturned on appeal. However, the case will now return to the lower court, where it will be heard again https://t.co/U3J5FmXdMw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 14, 2025 “The abortomat transforms a closely guarded, criminalised procedure into something as simple as picking up a package,” wrote ADT. “A door that opens when all others have slammed shut.” They say that the machine is intended for women who have an urgent medical need that means they cannot wait for the several days it takes to deliver pills by post, or who are in abusive, controlling relationships that make postal delivery unsafe. Wydrzyńska’s conviction came after the husband of a woman she helped obtain abortion pills found them and reported the case to the police. However, although assisting a woman in obtaining an unlawful abortion is an offence, the woman who had the abortion is not criminally liable. “The abortomat is not a human being, and the person collecting the pills, in accordance with the regulations, is not breaking the law,” said Wydrzyńska, quoted by news website Wirtualna Polska. WHW and ADT do not collect any personal information from women using the service. The European Court of Human Rights has ruled that Poland violated the rights of a pregnant woman who had to travel abroad to obtain an abortion after her foetus was diagnosed with a birth defect https://t.co/TgckusMxmJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 13, 2025 Under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which ruled from 2015 to 2023, the abortion law was tightened and was strictly enforced. In December 2023, a new, more liberal coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk came to power, promising to liberalise the abortion law. However, it has so far failed to pass any such legislation. In 2024, a move to decriminalise abortion assistance up to the 12th week of pregnancy was rejected by parliament, after the most conservative element of Tusk’s coalition joined the right-wing opposition in voting against it. Tusk subsequently admitted that it would be impossible during the current parliament to soften abortion laws. Instead, his government issued guidelines on when and how abortions can be carried out, with the aim of ensuring that doctors and prosecutors “take the women’s side” when making decisions on the issue.
