World.title: Democracy Digest: Operation Purgatory Snares Former Hungarian Ministers
World.content:
Fico juggles jobs and coalition; another fatal school attack shocks Slovakia

Robert Fico is currently Slovakia’s prime minister and, temporarily, its environment minister. The second job may prove easier than keeping his three-party coalition together. On Wednesday, President Peter Pellegrini handed the environment portfolio to Fico after dismissing Tomas Taraba. Taraba’s increasingly bitter feud with Slovak National Party (SNS) leader Andrej Danko culminated in an unprecedented episode in Slovakia’s recent political history: SNS MPs joining the opposition in voting to remove a minister nominated by their own party, after Fico had rejected a request to dismiss Taraba. The minister’s exit resolves one problem but leaves Fico with a larger one. Back in parliament as an independent MP, Taraba says he remains loyal to Fico, but will decide on how to vote on a case-by-case basis. With 76 votes needed for a majority, the government has little room for such conditional loyalty – particularly with the 2027 budget due in October. If parliament fails to approve it, Slovakia would enter a provisional budget regime, limiting monthly spending to one-twelfth of the current year’s budget. The coalition reckons it has 78 MPs, but that number could fall on individual votes. There is no obvious replacement for Taraba either. SNS claims the Environment Ministry under the coalition agreement and wants Deputy Environment Minister Filip Kuffa, though Taraba himself has questioned Kuffa’s qualifications. Kuffa has also faced criticism from the opposition in the past. The turmoil revived speculation about an early election, an option Fico himself recently put on the table. For now, however, the three coalition parties have strong reasons to keep the government alive. SNS is polling below the threshold for entering parliament, while coalition partner Hlas opposes an early vote, saying it has yet to deliver everything it promised its voters. Fico also has major projects and unfinished legislative business he may want to see through. Moreover, ending parliament’s term requires 90 MPs, meaning the coalition would also need opposition votes. At this point, an early election remains possible, though not probable. Fico and his Smer party have survived bigger challenges in the past, most notably in 2018 after the murder of investigative journalist Jan Kuciak and his fiancee, Martina Kusnirova, and subsequent mass protests. Fico resigned as prime minister, but Smer remained in government until the 2020 election.

Slovakia is again confronting violence in its schools this week after a 13-year-old boy killed a teacher and a classmate in the northern village of Staskov, northern Slovakia. Bozena Mariakova, 61, and the unnamed female pupil died after the boy attacked them with a knife. He also seriously wounded another teacher, whose condition is now reported as being stable. The boy has been placed in a psychological detention facility. At 13, he cannot be held criminally responsible under Slovak law. What happened before the attack is now under scrutiny. Days earlier, the murdered girl had reportedly alerted teachers to an image created by the boy showing a concentration camp with teachers’ faces. He could have had his conduct grade lowered over the incident. Psychologists spent two hours with his class on Monday, while the school had also filed a criminal complaint with police five days before the attack. Police are now reviewing how local officers dealt with that complaint. Little is publicly known about the boy. Residents told Slovak media he was being raised by his grandmother and mentioned unspecified difficulties involving his mother. A woman who knew him from church remembered him as a bright boy who served at Mass and read well, but rarely appeared cheerful. The attack comes less than two years after a student killed two people at a school in Spisska Stara Ves, eastern Slovakia. It also coincides with parliament debating a government bill on preventing radicalisation and mobilisation to violence among young people.

World.title: ‘Tsunami’ of Net Restrictions Leaves Turkey’s Online Media Fearing for Future
World.content:
Turkey’s rapidly expanding use of internet blocking orders has developed into what journalists and rights advocates describe as an unprecedented crackdown.

The independent news outlet T24 is the latest major media organisation to be targeted.

An Istanbul court on September 30 ordered access to be blocked to T24’s website and social media accounts under Article 8/A of Turkey’s Internet Law, citing the prevention of crime and protection of public order.

The decision concerned 118 items on the T24 site that allegedly weaken the “Turkish family structure” and negatively affect young people’s development regarding sexual orientation and gender identity.

T24 was founded in 2009 and is now one of Turkey’s most-read high-quality journalism platforms. T24 said it had removed all 118 pieces within the four-hour deadline it was given. Access to the entire website was still blocked.

World.title: Security Expert Questions Albania’s Readiness to Learn from Spy Chief’s Arrest
World.content:
The arrest of Albania’s state intelligence chief points to systemic failings in the process of her appointment and raises additional questions about the institutional response, according to security expert Arjan Dyrmishi, head of the Centre for the Study of Democracy and Governance in Tirana.

Vlora Hyseni, director of the State Intelligence Service, SHISH, was arrested on September 22 on suspicion of divulging classified information to businessman Ergys Agasi, himself arrested in late August on suspicion of involvement in rigged public tenders issued by Albania’s National Agency for Information Society, AKSHI, which, among other things, runs the state public services portal, e-Albania.

World.title: By Skoda and By Bike: Serbia’s Not Completely Even Election Race
World.content:
On September 19, a Saturday, Aleksandar Vucic posted on Instagram a video of himself driving an old Skoda and singing along to a popular folk song by the Serbian singer-songwriter Toma Zdravkovic.

“Today, for the first time, I’m doing it all myself – both as a driver and as a man of the people,” said Vucic, who was still president at that moment.

Vucic stepped down a little over a week later, to lead the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, SNS, into what promises to be a pivotal election in post-Slobodan Milosevic Serbia.

Both he and the SNS have been in power since 2012 and, despite the rules, regularly deploy state resources to contest elections that observers say have not been free or fair for a long time. The line between party and state has become heavily blurred in Serbia, often tipping the election scales.

World.title: Thousands in Kosovo Protest Again for ‘Fair Justice’ After Hague Convictions
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp



Thousands gather in Pristina in protest against Hague court verdict, October 1, 2026. Photo: BIRN

Thousands of people gathered on Thursday in Pristina’s main square to protest against this month’s first-instance verdict issued by the Kosovo Specialist Chambers, which convicted four ex-leaders of the Kosovo Liberation Army, KLA, of war crimes.

This was the 16th day of rallies against the verdict and coincided with the 29th anniversary of a demonstration in 1997 when Kosovar students demanded the right to return to public schools and educational faculties following years of having to study in private premises under Slobodan Milosevic’s regime.

Ismail Tasholli, representative of the Liria ka emer (Freedom Has a Name) movement, which is organising the protests, told the rally: “We have gathered here for you, we have gathered here for the KLA. We have got together to convey a very important message… because freedom does not belong to any [specific] political party.

“If the KLA is being attacked … then we have a great reason to say we want fair justice,” he said.

Former President Hashim Thaci and former Speaker Jakup Krasniqi were sentenced to 25 years in prison each, and former Speaker Kadri Veseli and former MP Rexhep Selimi to 18 and 13 years respectively, with credit for time served in detention since November 2020.

The court found them guilty of arbitrary detention, cruel treatment, torture, and murder from April 1998 to June 20, 1999, in Kosovo and Albania. The verdict can be appealed and Thaci’s defence has announced they will do so.

Presiding judge Charles Smith III’s choice of words when announcing the verdict, “In the name of the people of Kosovo”, sparked the “Not In My Name” logo that KLA supporters have incorporated into their protest movement ever since.

Many Kosovo Albanians claim the verdict effectively condemns the KLA’s just war against Serbia’s oppression despite the judge insisting that the KLA as a whole was not on trial.

Referring to a visit to Pristina on Thursday by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen, Tasholli said: “We tell her that we believe in European values but we do not believe in double standards when it comes to justice. We tell her: Not in our names.”

Von der Leyen is on a partial Western Balkans tour taking in Albania, Montenegro and North Macedonia. In a joint press conference with Kosovo Prime Minister Albin Kurti earlier on Thursday she said: “Nothing and nobody can rewrite Kosovo’s history.”

Referring to the year of NATO’s military intervention against Milosevic’s Yugoslavia, she added: “1999 is engraved in Europe’s collective memory, the violent repressions, the humanitarian crisis, the suffering endured by your people. The European Union has stood with you ever since.”

Turning to the verdict convicting the four wartime KLA leaders, she said that “this judgment is about the individual responsibility of the defendants. Kosovo resistance was not on trial, and we must respect the memory of all victims from all communities.”

Kurti recalled that the initial allegations made against Thaci, concerning alleged organ trafficking, were not even included in the indictment. “Secondly, the charges of crimes against humanity and widespread, systematic attacks against the civilian population were dismissed,” he said.

“Thirdly, the Specialist Chambers clearly stated that the KLA is not on trial and that their ruling is in no way intended to undermine the justice or legitimacy of the liberation war.”

He claimed the trial had contained some factual and historical errors, and “we expect these issues to be rectified on appeal. Justice must be impartial, and it must be seen and perceived as impartial”.

The Kosovo Specialist Chambers is part of Kosovo’s justice system but is staffed by internationals and seats in the Hague as a hybrid international tribunal. It was created in 2015, pressured by Kosovo’s Western allies. Thaci was one of its main supporters, saying it would prove the KLA’s war was just.

World.title: Bosnian Serb Wartime Leader Biljana Plavsic Dies Aged 96
World.content:
This post is also available in this language: Shqip Bos/Hrv/Srp

Biljana Plavsic at the war crimes tribunal in The Hague, January 2000. Photo: EPA PHOTO/POOL REUTERS/JERRY LAMPEN.

Biljana Plavsic, a senior wartime leader of the Bosnian Serbs, died on Thursday aged 96 in Belgrade, where she had been living since release from prison, the public broadcaster of Bosnia’s Serb-led entity, Republika Srpska, RTRS, reported.

As vice-president of the Serb-led Republika Srpska entity during the 1992-5 war, she was sentenced to 11 years in prison in on February 2003 by the UN tribunal in The Hague after pleading guilty to the persecution of Bosniaks, Croats and other non-Serbs.

In June 2003, she was transferred from The Hague to Sweden to serve her sentence and she released in October 2009, having served two-thirds of her sentence.

She then returned to Belgrade, where she lived a reclusive life and was not politically active. She was divorced and had no children, RTRS wrote in its report on her death.

Plavsic was born in 1930 in the Bosnian town of Tuzla. She was the only woman to be indicted and convicted of wartime crimes by the International Criminal Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia, ICTY, in The Hague.

But she later told Swedish magazine Vi that she only admitted guilt to get the other charges against her dropped, and had “done nothing wrong”.

She told BIRN in 2019 that she could not remember expressing remorse in court for causing suffering during the war. “I try to forget that period,” she said.

A former biology lecturer, Plavsic became the Serb member of Bosnia’s tripartite presidency from November 1990 until December 1992. She was later one of the vice-presidents of the newly-founded Republika Srpska, under Radovan Karadzic.

After the war, in 1996, she became Republika Srpska’s second president, a position she held until November 1998.

The Hague prosecution charged her alongside Momcilo Krajisnik, Republika Srpska’s speaker from 1991 to 1996. Krajisnik was found guilty of deportation and forced displacement; he died in September 2020 due to the consequences of COVID-19.

Since her release from prison, though not active in public life, Plavsic sometimes gave interviews to nationalist, pro-government, pro-Russian or far-right media.

World.title: With Jansa’s Return, Slovenia’s Media Landscape Is Being Reshaped
World.content:
Chokehold could tighten even without Orban

Milosavljevic says it would only be “a wild guess what could happen next”. He points to other important actors on the Slovenian and wider regional market, which recently included United Group deals with the Czech investment group PPF, resulting in the pushing down of N1 and Nova S outlets in the Serbian cable line-ups after PPF sold these to state-owned Telekom Srbija.

Moreover, in 2024, the United Arab Emirates technology and investment group e& acquired a controlling stake in PPF’s telecom assets in Bulgaria, Hungary, Serbia and Slovakia, paving the way for the UAE’s historic entry into EU and EU candidate markets. With his close ties to the UAE, there is speculation that Vucic himself could be “behind the UAE links”.

PPF also received negative publicity for scaling down critical news reporting on Markiza, the largest commercial TV channel in Slovakia, shortly after the populist Robert Fico rebranded himself as a pro-Kremlin nationalist and Orban ally, and then made an improbable return to power in 2023.

“PPF Group might be interested in taking over Telemach, one of Slovenia’s four internet providers,” Ribac says, repeating speculation reported in the Slovenian media in September. At the same time, he says, the group “might be ready to relinquish its ownership of production company Pro Plus in exchange for control of Telemach.”

One of the richest Slovenes, Dari Juzna, is reported to be interested in buying Pro Plus, the largest media house in Slovenia. Pro Plus is part of Central European Media Enterprises, which PPF acquired in 2020 from Time Warner. At the time, the IPI and other press associations raised concerns with PPF’s owner, the late Petr Kellner, regarding media ownership and editorial independence.

“A group of wealthy individuals close to current Prime Minister Jansa might conversely be interested in taking over Pro Plus, as it produces the most popular commercial television channel POPTV and the most visited news website in the country 24.com,” Ribac explains.

This fits with Jansa’s desire to keep a primary focus on Slovenia while maintaining ties with like-minded politicians and businessmen abroad. “Jansa alone has no designs to influence Croatia or other countries near abroad,” Pengov Bitenc tells BIRN, but adds that even if Jansa’s main focus remains domestic, it won’t stop him continuing to make use of the existing network of nationalist leaders abroad to boost his credibility.

Jansa is “now indebted to Netanyahu”, Pengov Bitenc tells BIRN, referring to the involvement of the Israeli Mossad-linked company Black Cube in Slovenia’s election campaign. He argues that Jansa is much more likely to return favours to the sitting Israeli prime minister than to Orban, “who is out of power and the money flows have been turned off”.

Indeed, Israeli Minister of Foreign Affairs Gideon Saar visited Slovenia in September, when he opened Israel’s permanent embassy in Ljubljana and heralded the country’s shift from being one of the most outspoken critics of Israel’s campaign in Gaza and violence against Palestinians in the West Bank to one of its staunchest backers.

World.title: Pro-Russian Voters May Hold Key in Bulgaria’s Presidential Election
World.content:
On October 25, Bulgarians will vote for a new president in an election that highlights old-school East-West divisions in the country.

The election will likely produce a second round run-off between current acting President Iliana Iotova, the frontrunner, who is supported by President Rumen Radev’s ruling Progressive Bulgaria, the pro-Kremlin Bulgarian Socialist Party and the smaller nationalist far-right party VMRO-BND.

On the other geopolitical side of the race is former interim prime minister Andrey Gyurov - a pro-EU, Western-oriented candidate supported by the centre-right opposition parties We Continue the Change and Democratic Bulgaria.

Apart from Gyurov and one other candidate, former agriculture minister Ivan Hristanov, almost all the contenders are fronting Eurosceptic, nationalist campaigns, which often border on Russia-sympathetic sentiment.

Experts say voters who support such stances might back various rivals to Iotova in the initial round, but switch to her if she faces a pro-EU candidate like Gyurov in the second round, in early November.

World.title: Croatian Banks Hold Serious Wealth, but Inflation is Eating it
World.content:
October the 2nd, 2026 – Croatian banks are holding some serious wealth, but inflation is continually eating it and reducing its purchasing power.

According to the Croatian National Bank (HNB), in June 2026, Croatian citizens held 33 billion euros in current and savings accounts, and an additional 10 billion euros in term deposits. Emilio Gucec reports for Poslovni that due to inflation, Croatians are losing around 430 euros of purchasing power per year on bank deposits, and the difference compared to investing after ten years can reach almost 10,000 euros per inhabitant.

This is a decline in purchasing power, not the disappearance of money from accounts: the nominal amount remains the same and, with interest, even grows slightly, but because of inflation less can be bought with it over time. Current and savings accounts in practice carry no interest, so with the latest published inflation of 4.2 % (August 2026) that part of the money loses value at the full rate of inflation. Shorter-term deposits currently yield 1.45 %, so the real loss on them is 2.75 % per year. According to a calculation by the investment platform Finax, this together means a loss of purchasing power of approximately 430 euros per year per inhabitant, or around 1.7 billion euros at the level of the entire country.

A similar picture was seen throughout 2025, when that loss amounted to around 360 euros per inhabitant, and it was particularly pronounced in 2022 and 2023, when inflation in Croatia reached 10.8 % and 8.4 % annually, which in just two years meant a real decline in the purchasing power of money in bank accounts of almost 20 %.

“Money held in current and savings accounts today practically carries no interest, so every month it quietly loses value at the full rate of inflation. When we translate that into figures, the average inhabitant of Croatia loses around 430 euros of purchasing power per year in this way, and at the level of the entire country it is almost 1.7 billion euros every year anew,” says Emilio Gučec, country manager of Finax for Croatia.

If the total of 43 billion euros that today lies in households’ current, savings and term accounts were invested in a globally diversified ETF portfolio with a historical average return of around 7 % per year, that amount could grow to around 84.6 billion euros in ten years. If everything remains as it is, the same amount in bank accounts would grow to only around 44.5 billion euros. The difference of almost 40 billion euros at the national level amounts to approximately 10,000 euros of lost potential value growth per inhabitant.

“A bank account provides many Croatians with a sense of security, but that same ‘security’ in the long term costs them the real value of their savings. The old saying goes: he who saves, has. But in today’s conditions, money that simply sits in a current or savings account without any interest quietly loses exactly what it was supposed to preserve, which is why it is suitable only for a short-term reserve, and not for the long-term building of assets. According to the HNB’s projection, according to which inflation should settle at around 2.8 % by 2028, such money could after about thirty years have less than half of its present purchasing power. With investing the exact opposite rule applies: compound interest works quietly, but from year to year more and more noticeably,” Gučec adds.

Inflation, he says, for years slowly and almost imperceptibly melts the savings deposited in banks, while compound interest in investing works in the completely opposite direction: it multiplies funds from year to year. And the longer the money remains invested, the stronger that effect is, while in a bank account time, on the contrary, works against it.

World.title: Croatian Subjects Have Been Tested for “Forever Chemicals”
World.content:
October the 2nd, 2026 – A group of Croatian subjects were tested for the presence of so-called “forever chemicals”, and they were unfortunately discovered, in levels that are much too high.

Of the ten Croatian participants included in a new European study, six had the sum of four long-chain PFAS compounds, also known as “forever chemicals”, above the health-based reference value set by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA). Vedran Salvia reports for Index that a worrying seven of the participants were from Gospić, and five of them were above that threshold.

forever chemicals were discovered in all participants

The study covered 110 people from nine European Union countries. All four analysed long-chain PFAS compounds were found in every participant. However, in 27 of them, or 25 percent, their sum was above the EFSA reference value. The study was commissioned by the Greens/EFA group in the European Parliament, and the interpretation of the results was carried out by researchers from Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Additional data on the Croatian participants was obtained by Index from the Greens/EFA office in the European Parliament. Thus we learn that, in addition to the seven people from Gospić, two more from Knin and one person from Pula were tested.

what exactly were they tested for?

The long-chain PFAS compounds for which the participants were tested are PFOA, PFOS, PFNA and PFHxS. These are four “forever chemicals” that EFSA considers together, i.e. it adds up their concentrations into the value ΣEFSA-4. If that value is above 6.9 ng/mL, it is considered to exceed the health-based reference threshold of EFSA. This does not mean that a person above that threshold will develop health problems, but that it is a level above the one EFSA considers health-acceptable for long-term exposure.

The participants were also tested for five ultra-short-chain PFAS compounds (TFA, PFPrA, TFMS, PFEtS and PFPrS). In the results, TFA stands out, while the remaining four compounds were found in traces or were not detected at all and are not of greater significance for this study.

how dangerous is all of this?

“Forever chemicals” is the popular name for a large group of synthetic organic compounds that are extremely difficult to break down and therefore remain in the environment for a long time and can pose a significant danger to human health and environmental quality. People are exposed to PFAS compounds primarily through food and drinking water, and some types can also enter the body from the environment in which they accumulate for years.

We previously dealt with the topic of “forever chemicals” in the case of the illegal disposal of thousands of tonnes of waste in Lika, where PFAS were found in groundwater. At that time we spoke with Prof. Dr. Branimir K. Hackenberger from the Department of Biology at Josip Juraj Strossmayer University in Osijek. He explained that PFOS remains in the body for three to five years. Another of the more problematic PFAS compounds is PFOA. For that “forever chemical”, Hackenberger says that the International Agency for Research on Cancer classified it in 2023 among substances carcinogenic to humans, while PFOS was classified among possible carcinogens.

what is tfa?

TFA stands out in particular – an ultra-short-chain PFAS compound that was found in all participants in this study. TFA can accumulate in water resources and plants, including crops used for human nutrition. It accounted for as much as 81.4 percent of the total mass of the six detected PFAS compounds, and its concentrations were on average 4.6 times higher than the sum of the four long-chain PFAS. The authors also note that the median TFA levels measured in this study are the highest recorded so far in human serum. The study states that TFA is relatively quickly excreted from the body, with an estimated half-life of 16 to 60 hours. The authors therefore conclude that the measured levels “probably result from frequent exposure to significant amounts of TFA in everyday life.”

As for this European study, it is important to emphasise that the findings in the tested residents of Gospić are not linked to the local waste landfill. This is an independent study of PFAS exposure among citizens of several European countries.

the croatian results stand out

The Greens/EFA office notes that in the entire sample that threshold was exceeded by a quarter of the participants, while among the Croatian participants it was as many as 60 percent, or six out of ten. They also note that the Croatian participants stand out in that their median ΣEFSA-4 (the line in the middle of the blue box in the photo below) is among the highest among the countries covered, while the median TFA (the line in the middle of the green box) is among the lowest.

The study also showed some patterns related to PFAS levels. Among the most important factors were sex and age: men had a median ΣEFSA-4 of 7.3 ng/mL, compared to 3.7 ng/mL in women, and levels increased with age in men but not in women. Higher levels of long-chain PFAS were associated with more frequent consumption of meat and fish and seafood. The authors warn that the study is not representative and that the number of participants per country is too small for reliable comparisons. They estimate that to detect even moderate differences between countries, at least 20 to 30 participants per country would be needed.

“pfas compounds must be banned”

Gordan Bosanac, MEP from Možemo and member of the Greens/EFA group, told Index that they launched the testing campaign in order to identify the best-known PFAS compounds, but also those that chemical lobbies are trying to protect by claiming that they do not accumulate in our bodies.

“The result is a clear reality: forever chemicals are in our blood. We tested 110 people in nine European countries and in every single person we found TFA, the smallest and most persistent compound from the PFAS group, and this is a substance that the European Chemicals Agency (ECHA) classifies as reproductively toxic. Subsequently, in the Croatians tested, very high levels of the four ‘classic’ long-chain PFAS compounds were also found. There is no alternative: PFAS compounds must be banned, and the gradual phasing out of their production and use must be systematically planned, supported and implemented. We can no longer wait, nor can we allow ourselves to continue being the ones who pay the price. The biggest polluters, primarily chemical companies, should bear the costs of cleaning up the pollution. If the Commission and the Member States vote against a PFAS ban, they will be directly responsible for crimes against the environment and public health,” he explained.

He adds that through the revision of the REACH chemicals regulation we must ban the placing of PFAS in new products and packaging.

“However, banning the creation of new PFAS is not enough. We must also change our attitude towards existing PFAS that is already in products on the market, that is already in our waste, that is already in the nature around us. As we know, these are forever chemicals and they will not disappear on their own. At the level of the entire EU, we need a strategy to combat PFAS waste – how we dispose of and treat that waste and how we ensure that it does not penetrate into nature and pollute our environment and community,” he adds.

“the ec is aware of the harmfulness of pfas”

“At our request, and following the case of 37 thousand tonnes of illegally imported and disposed international waste in Gospić, where analyses established the presence of PFAS compounds in wastewater, two weeks ago the European Parliament discussed the dangers of PFAS compounds to human health.

Colleagues across Europe recognised the danger of this situation and Commissioner Várhelyi emphasised that the Commission is aware of the harmfulness of PFAS and is ready to help Member States in the disposal of toxic waste and the fight against cross-border economic crime. I’d once again like to call on Commissioner Várhelyi, Commissioner Roswall, as well as Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to come forward as soon as possible with concrete proposals on how Member States can effectively dispose of waste contaminated with ‘forever chemicals’ and protect their citizens and nature,” he says.

World.title: Croatian Man Pushes Serbian Man into Sea, Hajduk Fans Pay Fine
World.content:
October the 2nd, 2026 – A Croatian man has pushed a Serbian man into the sea in Makarska for refusing to remove a Crvena Zvezda (Red Star) shirt, and Hajduk fans have paid his fine.

The Society of Friends of Hajduk Makarska announced via its official Facebook page that the full amount needed to cover the fine and court costs for their member has been successfully collected. Index reports that the Croatian man was fined after he pushed a man, a citizen of Serbia wearing a Red Star Belgrade (Crvena Zvezda) football club shirt, into the sea on the Makarska waterfront. In their post, the Makarska fan association stated that their member “enabled a certain tourist from abroad to swim.”

The incident received a legal epilogue at the misdemeanour court, where the 43-year-old attacker was given a fine (between 700 and 4,000 euros) for disturbing public order and peace, after which he was released. However, a subsequent police investigation led to an unusual turn of events in which the attacked man himself ended up behind bars.

By reviewing his social media profiles, police officers established that the mentioned Serb had, in earlier public posts, glorified the convicted war criminal Ratko Mladić and also insulted Croatia and its citizens with derogatory content. Because of these offences, the attacked man was sentenced to 14 days in prison.

World.title: BioMania Zagreb Named Among the 10 Best Restaurants in the World
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – Tripadvisor, the world’s leading review platform for the hospitality and tourism sector, has ranked BioMania Zagreb, a 100% plant-based and organic restaurant, among the top 10 in the world in the Vegan & Vegetarian category.

Less than two years after opening, BioMania Bistro Zagreb has entered the Tripadvisor Travellers’ Choice Best of the Best category for 2026. Fewer than 1% of all restaurants registered on the platform – and there are more than 5 million of them – make it into this category. Best of the Best is not awarded by a jury. The ranking is calculated based on the number and quality of reviews from guests who actually dined at the restaurant, backed by an editorial review process that places the winners among the top one percent on the platform.

Alongside BioMania, the world’s top 10 in the Vegan & Vegetarian category include restaurants from Peru, Greece, Vietnam, Canada, Scotland, the United States and the Czech Republic. The Zagreb restaurant is rated 4.9 out of 5 on Tripadvisor, based on more than a thousand reviews.

“We are truly overjoyed that, after our seasonal bistro in Bol, our year-round Zagreb restaurant has also received this prestigious award and been ranked among the top 1% of restaurants in the world. Being among the top 10 in the world in our category is truly a dream come true. I would like to sincerely thank our entire team and all our wonderful partners, especially the many small producers of organic and biodynamic fruit, vegetables and herbs. Finally, of course, I would also like to thank our many guests, who show their appreciation by leaving reviews, coming back in great numbers and telling their friends, acquaintances and relatives about us. In this way they help our guest numbers grow steadily, which is also helped by the fact that the vast majority of our menu is gluten-free. In just under two years since opening, we have welcomed more than 40,000 guests, and we are especially pleased that over 70% of them are from Croatia.

“We were also surprised that more than 80% of our guests are ‘omnivores’, which further shows us that, both conceptually and gastronomically, we have succeeded in attracting a very broad range of guests,” said Dario Kožul, founder of the BioMania brand.

World.title: Dani Olmo Donates Two Percent of His Salary to Vukovar
World.content:
Dani Olmo has never hidden how much his time in Croatia meant to him, and now another detail has come to light, showing how attached he remains to the country where he took his first big steps in football.

Well-known Croatian agent Andy Bara, the man who brought Olmo from Barcelona to Dinamo, spoke about the Spanish international and his character. Especially striking is the story of Vukovar, a city that left a powerful impression on Olmo when he was a teenager playing for the Zagreb club.

Olmo donates 2 percent of his gross salary to Vukovar.

“Dani Olmo is extremely attached to Zagreb and Croatia. I’ll tell you something the public didn’t know until now, and I just hope Dani won’t hold it against me. Since leaving Dinamo, at every club he has played for, Olmo has donated two percent of his annual gross salary to Vukovar. Given that he earns serious money, these are large sums,” Andy Bara told Podcast Inkubator, adding:

“He did it while playing for RB Leipzig, and he still does it today at Barcelona, and he has never wanted to talk about it publicly. His big wish is to finish his career at Dinamo, and he hopes it will come true.”

Olmo arrived in Zagreb in 2014 as a 16-year-old from Barcelona’s La Masia, and a trip to a tournament in Vukovar was one of the key moments at the start of his Croatian story. After that tournament, he was promoted to Dinamo’s senior squad.

He later spoke about his Vukovar experience on several occasions. He explained that he talked with people who had lived through the war, began learning more about what had happened in Croatia, and felt a need to help, in some way, the people who still feel the consequences of the war today.

Olmo left Dinamo for RB Leipzig in early 2020 and returned to Barcelona four years later. He clearly never forgot Croatia, Dinamo, or Vukovar.

World.title: Global Event Industry Comes to Hvar: RSVP Symposium Croatia 2026.
World.content:
October 1, 2026 – The global event industry is coming to Hvar with RSVP Symposium Croatia 2026.

From October 5 to 8, Hvar will host leading professionals from the worlds of luxury events, destination weddings, creative design, and event production. The RSVP Symposium is being held with Sunčani Hvar Hotels acting as host and co-producer, supported by the Hvar Town Tourist Board and the Split-Dalmatia County Tourist Board.

From October 5 to 8, 2026, Hvar will become a meeting point for leading professionals in the global event industry. RSVP Symposium Croatia—part of the international RSVP community dedicated to the luxury events sector—brings together event organizers, wedding planners, designers, creatives, producers, and other professionals shaping the industry’s future.

This year’s edition is held under the theme “The Power of K(no)w,” a play on words combining the power of knowledge with the equally important ability to recognize when to say “no.” Two days of educational programming will feature discussions on knowledge, decision-making, professional relationships, and contemporary industry challenges, with a focus on exchanging experiences and networking among participants.

RSVP Symposium Hvar 2026 is being realized with Sunčani Hvar Hotels as the host and co-producer, supported by the Hvar Town Tourist Board and the Split-Dalmatia County Tourist Board, and in partnership with the Croatian planning team AMAVERA Collective. The collaboration between the hotel sector, destination tourism boards, and specialized partners shares a clear objective: to showcase Hvar and Central Dalmatia to an audience directly involved in selecting venues for international weddings, luxury private events, incentive programs, conferences, and corporate gatherings.

Joining Sunčani Hvar Hotels and AMAVERA Collective for this year’s edition are MihociStudios (photography and video production), The Bombay Lettering Company (stationery), Julie and Lisa—along with Camilla from CJC Hair & Makeup—(beauty services), The Collective (entertainment), Altera (rentals, furniture, linens, and tents), and Xcape (yacht experiences). This blend of international and local creatives, producers, and destination partners further demonstrates Hvar’s capacity to host complex events requiring high production values ​​and creative excellence.

The program is designed to ensure that Hvar is not merely a venue, but an integral part of the experience. Educational sessions will take place at the historic Hvar Theatre, while the social program will feature the Adriana, Palace Elisabeth, and Beach Club Hvar, as well as a maritime excursion. Local heritage and the island’s identity are woven into the concept of each evening—ranging from the atmosphere of a Dalmatian island to Hvar’s agave lace, which serves as the inspiration for the gala dinner at Palace Elisabeth.

The arrival of the RSVP Symposium is particularly significant for further positioning Hvar as a premium, year-round destination. The luxury events and MICE tourism segment naturally builds upon Hvar’s established international image—featuring high-quality hotel offerings, authentic cultural heritage, gastronomy, the sea, and a range of attractive locations within a compact area—while simultaneously creating opportunities for tourism activity outside the peak summer months. 1.

2. Statement from the Hvar Town Tourist Board

“Hvar may not be the largest destination in the MICE and premium events sector, but we see this as our very advantage. We boast unique locations, a strong city identity, and high-quality hotel and creative partners.

It is particularly valuable for the destination that, on this occasion, Hvar will be experienced not only by guests but also by professionals whose business decisions could lead to new events and visitor arrivals in the years to come.

We also value the fact that events like this involve local hoteliers, restaurateurs, transport providers, and production and creative event services, ensuring their impact remains within the local community.

The RSVP Symposium is an opportunity to showcase Hvar to the people who directly select and recommend destinations for international business and premium events. It is also a chance to highlight what makes the town and island of Hvar so special—where the location is not merely a backdrop but an integral part of the experience, lending the event something unique through its spaces, people, rhythm, and character—qualities that cannot be replicated elsewhere.

RSVP Symposium Croatia takes place in Hvar from October 5 to 8, 2026.

RSVP Symposium Croatia 2026

October 5–8, 2026 | Hvar

Theme: The Power of K(no)w

Host and co-producer: Sunčani Hvar Hotels

Supported by: Hvar Town Tourist Board and Split-Dalmatia County Tourist Board

World.title: Zagreb Mayor Tomislav Tomašević: We Won’t Pay Workers for Their Strike
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – Zagreb Mayor Tomislav Tomašević has stated that the workers who went on strike from both ZET and Zagreb Holding won’t be paid.

After three days, the strike by ZET and Zagreb Holding workers has ended. Trams and buses are running again, and Čistoća has resumed regular waste collection. The County Court in Zagreb today declared the strikes at ZET and Holding illegal and ordered them to stop.

The unions then suspended the strike and announced they would appeal the rulings. Index reports that ZET has announced that from today onwards, all tram and bus traffic will again run according to the regular timetable.

what you need to know…

Mayor Tomislav Tomašević has stated that none of the workers who went on strike will be paid for the time they spent striking. A ZET union lawyer has stated that he received two drastically different rulings. Municipal workers and ZET workers have now formally ended the strike after the court banned the ZET workers’ strike and the municipal workers’ strike.

After three days, the strike of ZET and Zagreb Holding workers has ended. Trams and buses are running again, and Čistoća has continued regular waste collection. The County Court in Zagreb today declared the strikes at ZET and Holding illegal and ordered their termination. The unions then suspended the strike and announced appeals against the rulings. Mayor Tomislav Tomašević stated that workers will not be paid for the days spent on strike. ZET published that from tomorrow all tram and bus traffic will again operate according to the regular schedule.

The strike had caused significant disruption in Zagreb for three days, with no trams, buses or regular waste collection.

World.title: Butković: We’re Signing Largest Contract in History of Croatian Railways
World.content:
October the 1st, 2026 – Transport Minister Oleg Butković has stated that today the signing of the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways will be signed.

Minister of Maritime Affairs, Transport and Infrastructure Oleg Butković announced the signing of a contract for the reconstruction and upgrading of the Dugo Selo – Novska railway line, worth almost 900 million euros. Index reports that this is the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways.

The Dugo Selo – Novska line is part of one of the main corridors that runs through Croatia towards the east of the country. “This is truly the largest contract in the history of Croatian Railways – almost 900 million euros for 83 kilometres of track reconstruction and the construction of a second track. We’ve been working on this project for a long time, preparing it, a public tender was carried out and now the procedures are complete,” said Butković.

first cooperation with an indian company

After the realisation of this project, he added, the Okučani – Vinkovci section will still remain. “Then we will have a fully reconstructed and built railway line from the Slovenian border, because Savski Marof – Zagreb has been reconstructed, that is, from Zagreb to the border with Serbia,” the minister said. Butković confirmed that this is the first time a company from India has won a job in such a tender. “As far as we have inquired and according to the documentation they submitted, they have very good references. They have worked on one of the largest projects in India and the world, so I believe everything will be as it should,” he said.

The minister is aware that large projects also bring challenges. “Some things today you cannot predict and you cannot influence them. I hope there will be as few of them as possible,” he said. The start of works is planned for the first quarter of 2027 and they should last five and a half years. Butković expressed the hope that there will be no new major crises in the world that could, like previous ones, cause disruptions and price increases.

the lowland railway project

The minister also spoke about the lowland railway, a project that has been in preparation for a long time. “We have started with the Hrvatski Leskovac – Karlovac section. As for the reconstruction of the lines around Zagreb, mostly everything has been reconstructed: towards the west, towards Zagorje and towards Bjelovar. By the end of the year we are finishing Dugo Selo – Križevci, which is actually almost done, and Križevci – Koprivnica – Hungarian border,” he said.

He emphasised that it is now important to move towards Rijeka, where the most expensive section from Karlovac to Rijeka remains, whose value is estimated at more than 2.5 billion euros. “There has been an increase in prices due to all the disruptions I spoke about, but we have accelerated the entire project.

A tender for technical assistance is currently underway. We would go for the so-called Alliance model, in which design, obtaining building permits and execution of works would be in one package,” he explained. Under that model, the selected contractor would lead all procedures, which would shorten public procurement and appeal procedures, and the deadline for construction of the line would be five to six years.

another decade before any real change

Asked when passengers will feel real progress and get fast trains, Butković replied that passenger transport around Zagreb is already functioning well. “We’ve more than 70 new trains in passenger transport. Of those, 42 trains have been procured in the last four years. Contracts are constantly being signed and funds secured. This was also shown these days during the strike, when the trains helped a lot, especially in the suburban area,” he emphasised.

Nevertheless, the complete reconstruction of the railway network will still take time. “I always say that we have to be patient for another ten years or so. In those ten years we would manage to mostly reconstruct and build everything on the main corridors and reconstruct a large part of the regional lines. We have already spent around 900 million euros on the reconstruction of local and regional lines across Croatia,” he said.

the continuation of motorway construction

The minister also commented on motorway construction. He announced that the Istrian Y will be completed by the end of the year or the beginning of 2027. “We’re strongly and decisively going ahead with the construction of the Adriatic-Ionian Corridor, Križišće – Žuta Lokva. Two contracts have been signed there. Today we received the building permit for the first section and we are starting the works. That is around 400 million euros,” he said.

Bids have also been opened for the first section of the motorway towards Dubrovnik. Although the new bids are also above the estimated value, the tender will not be cancelled again. “We would not have cancelled the first one either if there had not been really large differences in price compared to the estimated values. The bids that arrived in the new tender are around 40 to 50 million euros lower compared to the previous tender,” Butković concluded. He said that they are decisively proceeding with the completion of the Adriatic-Ionian Corridor, that is, the motorway towards Dubrovnik and the Križišće – Žuta Lokva section.

World.title: Minister floats network‑fee compensation to ease winter power costs
World.content:
The government is considering options for how to ease the impact of high energy prices on consumers this coming winter. The simplest measure would be compensating the network fee, says Minister of Energy Erkki Keldo.

Keldo (Reform Party) said the government received an overview on Thursday of global gas prices, electricity price forecasts, and the possibilities Estonia has to offer more price stability.

Keldo stressed that Estonia cannot influence the global gas price in any way. The final price of electricity, however, does not consist only of energy — it also includes various fees, and one of the easiest and least bureaucratic areas to intervene in, according to Keldo, is the network fee, which makes up a considerable share of the end‑consumer price.

"One option we could compensate is, for example, the network fee," Keldo pointed out.

The minister said it is not yet known what the electricity price will be this winter, but it is wise to be prepared for different scenarios. A possible decision to ease the network fee also requires communication with the Competition Authority, and electricity sellers must be able to make technical preparations. For this reason, Keldo considered it sensible to present this measure to the government early enough as one possible option.

Keldo declined to say at what price level the threshold would be where the government should decide that some step must be taken.

"If I were to name a specific price, that would already be speculation," Keldo noted, agreeing with energy‑market participants who say the state should be able to help those who need assistance the most.

"But on the other hand, we must ensure that we do not interfere with the normal functioning of the market — meaning the government's task is to find a balance. For that, we are making the necessary calculations, such as what it would mean to compensate fifty percent of the network fee: how much it would cost the state budget, how much network operators could reduce it," Keldo explained.

In the end, however, Keldo said it must be understood that this money comes, one way or another, from the consumer or taxpayer.

To those who consider network fees an unnecessary burden on people, Keldo reminded that they are intended to ensure energy security and supply reliability.

"We want electricity to be available in every region of Estonia. All these network fees go toward strengthening the electricity grid and making investments. They do not go anywhere else. We must also understand that this fee is charged so that we have continuous security and high‑quality networks across Estonia," the minister explained.

World.title: Former mayor: Church and power entangled in Narva 'prayer breakfast' row
World.content:
Raik says the event later this month is being held by three local churches in cooperation with the city government.

Raik was ousted as mayor following a vote of no-confidence in July, with Jaan Toots (Center) taking her place.

Organizers of the prayer breakfast say both Mayor Toots and council leader Urbo Vaarmann (Plan B) initially considered covering the costs from the city budget.

On October 15, an event called "Palvushommik" ("Prayer Morning") is to be held at Narva Town Hall, organized by Dmitri Andrejev, pastor of the Christian Narva congregation, Artur Põld, senior pastor of the Jõhvi congregation of the Estonian Methodist Church, and Aleksandr Gurkin, Bishop Lazar of Narva and Peipsiveere of the Estonian Christian Orthodox Church.

The Estonian Christian Orthodox Church (Eesti Kristlik Õigeusu Kirik) was formerly the Estonian Orthodox Church of the Moscow Patriarchate (MPEÕK), and changed its name in September 2024.

Vaarmann did not deny it was he who made the proposal, saying he had seen how similar events had worked well in Tartu and elsewhere. He said the city is not involved in organizing it, and is not funding it. Since all Narva city councilors have been invited, the council office forwarded the invitations to them, which he said is standard practice. "If someone organizes something like this and does it with their own money, then I see no reason why it is not a good idea," he said.

Katri Raik. Source: Dmitri Fedotkin/ERR

Toots meanwhile said the city provided premises for the event, which organizers pay rent for like anyone else. "There are such set-ups in Tartu as well as in other cities, and we agreed to give them the space," Toots said. On Raik's criticism, Toots said the breakfast is not a political event even as Raik was portraying it as such. "For Katri Raik, everything is political; even her time in office was highly political, rather than about getting work done," he said, adding that he did not know the prayer breakfast was included in the Center-Plan B coalition agreement, as Raik claimed.

Pastor Andrejev wrote on social media that the event was prompted by the city's political situation and is intended to bring different political forces together. "It has been difficult for me and, I believe, for all Narva residents to watch how unstably our city council has worked in recent years," he wrote. He added all council members and senior officials have been invited, and that budget funds will not be used for the rental of the premises, the piano or other expenses. He also thanked Vaarmann and Toots for being willing to consider covering the costs from the city budget.

Raik is now in opposition and chairs the Respekt faction at the Narva City Council. She called the prayer breakfast a political event, backed by Plan B and the Center Party. "This is a very strange story, because as we know, this 'Tsar's Route' and the prayer breakfast are the two things that people remember from the latest coalition agreement. And the idea of the prayer breakfast was indeed written into the coalition agreement. Now, somehow, the city government is trying to distance itself from it and says that the city's coat of arms ended up on the announcement by accident," Raik said.

The Tsar's route (Tsaaritee) is a controversial tourism route proposed by Vaarmann which would connect Narva and Tartu, marking the historical path once traveled by Russian Tsars when Estonia was part of the Tsarist Empire (1710-1918).

"This event has this political and murky flavor to it. To this day, I have not grasped exactly which denomination the organizer represents. In principle, I am not against different churches cooperating, but right now this really is a very dubious event with a political flavor. Power and the church have somehow become mixed up with each other here," Raik added. Raik noted she would not be attending the event herself.

An event like this could instead increase tensions, she added. "Narva is Estonia's third-largest city, which is located exactly where it is and where there are plenty of concerns. There is no need to ratchet up additional tensions, which in my view is exactly what this is doing right now," Raik went on.

Ilmo Au, an adviser in the Ministry of the Interior's religious affairs and civil society department, told ERR that allowing local government premises to be used for organizing religious or other events is up to each local government to decide. "The Ministry of the Interior has no objections if representatives of these congregations take part in organizing an ecumenical event for the local community, but we recommend also involving representatives of other congregations operating in Narva," Au said.

While prayer breakfasts in the U.S. have come to be associated with both of President Donald Trump's administrations, the tradition dates back to Dwight D. Eisenhower's presidency and has been attended by Democratic presidents as much as Republican ones — though Democratic participation has declined sharply in recent years.

World.title: Photos: Major overhaul progresses at Tallinn's Kadriorg Stadium
World.content:
At Kadriorg Stadium, work is underway across the entire territory, and renovation of the main building as well as construction of the opposite stand of the main arena has begun.

On the main arena, new drainage and irrigation systems are being built for the stadium's grass field, and the track surface has been removed, said Margus Jurkatam, head of the Tallinn Sports Center's Central District

Construction of the opposite stand of the main arena is also underway. In the future, it should accommodate about 5000 spectators.

Construction work on the main arena will be completed in the fourth quarter of 2027.

Renovation of Building A has also begun, and a connecting tunnel between Buildings A and B is being built. Construction work on Building B is in its final stage, and the building's completion deadline is December, Jurkatam said.

Building A is the historical main building of Kadriorg Stadium, while Building B is a completely new building that will house service and changing rooms, conference rooms, and a strength and warm‑up hall.

"A football training arena with a stand is also being built, with a completion deadline in the second quarter of 2027," Jurkatam said.

The completion deadline for the entire complex is January 2028.

ERR wrote in April this year that construction of the stadium will cost €17.1 million without VAT, and the work is being carried out by Nordlin Ehitus OÜ, the winner of the public procurement. With separate procurements, the athletics training arena was renovated by 2021, and by spring 2023 the lighting of the stadium arenas was renewed and its electrical supply improved.

World.title: Estonia not invited to U.S.-led meeting on NATO's future
World.content:
Estonia did not receive an invitation to a meeting in Poland led by the United States, where NATO allies will discuss the future of the alliance. This is not an official NATO meeting, says Prime Minister Kristen Michal.

On Wednesday, the U.S. publication Politico wrote that the United States will leave several allies, including the Baltic states, out of next month's gathering of NATO members that will discuss the future of the alliance.

When ERR asked ministries for confirmation regarding the claims made in the article, the response was that allies consult with each other continuously in different formats. It was also said that in NATO, in addition to official formats, there are various groupings among allies where security and defense issues are discussed.

Prime Minister Kristen Michal emphasized that this is not an official NATO meeting.

"The format that began in Bergen at the initiative of the United States is not a NATO meeting," Michal said. "It has been held in different formats, with participation from defense ministers, foreign ministers, and ambassadors, but NATO decisions are made at the NATO working level."

According to Michal, the JEF format is important for Estonia. "We also communicate in the North‑Baltic region, which is outside NATO but still largely includes an allied format," he added.

Defense Minister Martin Herem noted that if Scandinavian countries are invited to the meeting, then they are also interested in standing up for Estonia's interests. "In all this Baltic Sea security issue, they cannot manage without our security. Therefore, they cannot leave our interests aside there in any way," Herem said.

According to six diplomats familiar with preparations for the event, the planned meeting in Poland, led by Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby, is essentially a working group focused on NATO's future.

Reportedly, the United Kingdom, France, and the Baltic states will be left out of the meeting.

MP Raimond Kaljulaid (SDE). Source: Priit Mürk/ERR

MP: no point in putting on a good face in a bad game

Member of the Riigikogu National Defense Committee Raimond Kaljulaid (SDE) wrote on social media that the Baltic states have no reason to put on a good face regarding being left out of the meeting. According to him, being left out of the meeting sends Russia the message that the three Baltic states are a special zone.

"This fact, that Estonia is not at the table when questions about NATO's future are discussed in a narrower circle under the leadership of NATO's leading ally, the U.S., is of course a minus sign, not a plus sign or neutral," he noted.

According to Kaljulaid, the explanation that this is not an official NATO format is irrelevant. "The question is why we are not there."

He drew attention to whom the U.S. is holding these discussions with. "Finland, Sweden, Norway and reportedly in the future also Denmark, that is the Nordic countries, and Poland, Germany and the Netherlands. The Baltic states are out, as are the UK and France."

In the case of the United Kingdom and France, Kaljulaid believes one may speculate that the issue is that these countries have not responded very forcefully to the USA's calls to increase defense spending and strengthen European sovereignty.

According to Kaljulaid, the explanation for the Baltic states being left out may also be purely practical. "One cannot invite one of the three, but putting all three small ones at the table already makes the circle very large, the risk of leaks etc. increases."

At the same time, Kaljulaid admitted that a somewhat more believable explanation is that the Baltic states simply are not considered so important.

The worst thing, in Kaljulaid's view, is that being left outside the door sends Russia the signal that the three Baltic states are like some special zone or special case.

"The Baltic states have the same status as NATO and European Union countries as Poland, Germany or Finland," Kaljulaid emphasized. "Should we state this more clearly also from the government? I would recommend doing so."

"We have good bilateral relations with all the invited countries and of course also with the U.S., but that does not mean that from our point of view it is acceptable that matters directly concerning us are discussed without us," Kaljulaid said.

Marko Mihkelson. Source: Siim Lõvi / ERR

Mihkelson: I wouldn't overdramatize this

According to MP Marko Mihkelson (Reform Party), chair of the Riigikogu Foreign Affairs Committee, the fact that the Baltic states are not included in the meeting should not be overstated.

"I wouldn't dramatize this news in any way; it truly isn't an official meeting," Mihkelson said. "This Bergen group has met before as well. Elbridge Colby, if I'm not mistaken, met with the countries of this group for the first time in June."

Mihkelson emphasized that discussions about European security take place in different venues and in different formats. In the NATO context, he said, the most important thing is what happens at NATO headquarters and what is decided at the North Atlantic Council (NAC) table.

He also recalled that just a week ago there was news about how the United States will continue its military presence in the Baltic states and increase its presence in Poland.

"Understandably, through good allies we know what is being discussed at these meetings," he added.

According to Mihkelson, meetings of this sort do not weaken NATO unity. "I believe that Colby's goal in promoting the NATO 3.0 idea, of which he is the author, is ultimately still the strengthening of NATO," he said.

"We should not fuel speculation that NATO is no longer united or that there are different groups within NATO that are supposedly ready to move at different speeds, or that the Baltic states are even seemingly in some kind of isolation," Mihkelson said.

Mihkelson does not agree with Riigikogu member Raimond Kaljulaid, who said Estonia should express its displeasure over being left out of the discussion more sharply.

"Estonia has always benefited from smart diplomacy. Estonia has been very capable, despite its relative smallness, of representing its interests well in international organizations and in bilateral relations. This must continue — I call for continuing smart diplomacy," Mihkelson said.

Tony Lawrence, a researcher at the International Center for Defense and Security (ICDS), also believes that staying away from the meeting taking place in November is not a major tragedy, because no decisions are made in discussions of this format. The initiator of the meeting is Pentagon policy chief Elbridge Colby.

"The list of invited partners published by Politico consists of only six people from six countries. In total, there are 32 allied countries. So Estonia has not been excluded — it simply does not belong to that list," Lawrence said.

The article has been updated with comments by Raimond Kaljulaid, Marko Mihkelson and Tony Lawrence.

World.title: Flash estimate: Prices up 0.5 percent in September
World.content:
Estonia's harmonized index of consumer prices (HICP) rose 0.5 percent in September compared with August according to a flash estimate from Statistics Estonia.

The HICP rose by 3 percent on year to September, the agency added.

The rise was driven primarily by continuing increases in petrol and diesel prices linked to the armed conflict in the Middle East, said Lauri Veski, Consumer Price Statistics Service Manager at Statistics Estonia.

"Compared with September 2025, the index was primarily influenced by the continuing rise in petrol and diesel prices, which is due to the ongoing armed conflict in the Middle East," Veski noted.

The HICP includes the expenditures of tourists, which is generally higher in the summer months; the consumer price index (CPI) uses weights reflecting the average expenditure structure of those residing in Estonia only.

The above figures are flash estimates which will be refined once more detailed data on September prices are received.

The CPI data for September is due to be published by Statistics Estonia next Wednesday, October 7. The full HICP data for September will be published on October 15.

World.title: Russia detains cargo ship bound for Estonia's Sillamäe port
World.content:
Russia's border guard detained a cargo ship in the Gulf of Finland that was headed for the port of Sillamäe. The vessel Västerbotten, sailing under the Cypriot flag, passed through Russian territorial waters, which ships have the right to transit.

The Police and Border Guard Board confirmed the detention of the ship.

According to the application Vesselfinder, the ship Västerbotten was anchored in Russian waters on Thursday. When looking at the ship's trajectory in the map application, it appears that the ship passed through Russian territorial waters before being detained.

At the same time, Russia, Estonia and Finland have an agreement that ships may pass through that location, because that route is safer for large vessels than sailing between the shallows in Estonia's maritime area.

In 2025, Russia detained the oil tanker Green Admire, which had departed from the port of Sillamäe. It was the first similar incident.

To avoid similar situations, the Estonian Transport Administration decided that in the future ships to and from Sillamäe will be directed through Estonia's territorial sea.

On Thursday afternoon, Västerbotten again began moving toward the port, and according to the Vesselfinder application, the ship was located in the Sillamäe port on Friday morning.

No explanation why the ship was detained

The head of the Transport Administration's vessel traffic management department, Are Piel, explained that although this was an unpleasant situation, it is not unusual.

"Every country has the right to exercise control over ships in its territorial sea, and apparently the Russian administration considered it necessary to inspect this ship when it passed through their territorial sea," he said.

Piel said that peaceful passage through a state's territorial sea is permitted for all ships, but he emphasized that this does not mean the state does not have the right to inspect the ship.

For a time, Russia imposed a restriction on passing through the area, but this has now been lifted.

Piel noted that although relatively few ships go to Sillamäe, Russia's territorial sea is not passed through just in case — precisely to avoid such inspection raids.

The Estonian Transport Administration has no explanation from the Russian side as to why the ship was detained.

The article has been updated with Are Piel's comment and the ship's location as of Oct. 2.

World.title: US Marines deploy to Baltic Sea region for NATO's Baltic Sentry mission
World.content:
Personnel from the United States Marine Corps are being redirected to the Baltic Sea region as part of NATO's enhanced vigilance activity Baltic Sentry.

The marines will number around 50 and will aid in supporting and protecting critical undersea infrastructure, the Pentagon has announced.

The personnel come from the 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group, based at Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. They are to operate alongside Finland's Coastal Brigade, providing advanced expeditionary surveillance and tactical reconnaissance capabilities.

The deployment comes as Estonia, Finland and other allied nations continue to grapple with a series of cable damage incidents in the region. Most recently, in December 2024, the EstLink 2 power cable between Estonia and Finland and several communication cables were ruptured, with authorities suspecting deliberate sabotage. NATO launched Baltic Sentry in response to these incidents.

Baltic Sentry is a highly integrated collective defense effort, led by European allies under Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum and Allied Maritime Command, with the U.S. Marine Corps serving in a supportive, enabling capacity.

Marine Corps Maj. Gen. Daniel Shipley, commander of U.S. Marine Corps Forces Europe and Africa, said the operational design was a premium example of European allies leading regional maritime security while the US provides specialized capabilities.

"Our participation in Baltic Sentry demonstrates the dynamic agility of the Marine Corps to rapidly project specialized capabilities where they are most effective," he said. "Working side by side with our Finnish allies strengthens our collective readiness, ensuring we can operate seamlessly as a cohesive, lethal team to deter hybrid threats in the Baltic littoral."

The rotation will use reconnaissance Marines' capabilities, including small unmanned aerial systems and littoral sensors, to feed data into NATO's shared operational picture.

"The experience, skills and systems of the US Marine Corps are perfectly suited for supplementing our situation picture and supporting our monitoring of the Baltic Sea," noted Finnish Navy Capt. Johan Tillander, Finland Navy Command chief of operations.

What is Baltic Sentry?

NATO launched Baltic Sentry in January 2025 to protect critical undersea infrastructure in the Baltic Sea, including power and data cables, following a series of suspected suspected sabotage incidents. The mission incorporates naval vessels such as frigates, maritime patrol aircraft, naval drones and new sensor technology. Allies are integrating national surveillance assets to improve detection and response. It is led by Allied Joint Force Command Brunssum, based in the Netherlands, with Allied Maritime Command playing a central role in its maritime operations.

Founded in 1775, the U.S. Marine Corps is the the U.S. military's amphibious and expeditionary force, and has been deployed in the Baltic region in various capacities since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine.

World.title: National e-calculation math competition returns for 3rd year on October 8
World.content:
Organized by Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) in conjunction with public broadcaster ERR and major bank SEB, the contest asks participants to solve 12 school math problems, with €1,234 in prize money up for grabs, as well as other prizes.

Twelve math problems covering the school curriculum from grades 1 to 12, though adults are eligible to take part too. The questions will be available on the site: erehkendus.err.ee. The winner will be the first person to correctly solve all 12 problems by 1 p.m. Since the questions go live at 10 a.m. on the same day, time will be of the essence.

This year's theme is anxiety about math —the fear or tension associated with learning or solving math problems, which in a vicious cycle can make it harder to concentrate and lead to worse results. e-rehkendus' creators say it offers a playful, low-pressure environment to help ease it.

Organizers also note that adults' attitudes matter too: Research shows that teachers' and parents' own math anxiety is easily passed on to children.

"Mathematical thinking is the foundation for those choices, and e-rehkendus helps highlight its importance in a playful and inclusive way," said SEB board chairman Allan Parik, commenting on the bank's third year supporting the initiative.

Prizes include, for the best high school student, a place on a freely chosen bachelor's program at TalTech without the usual entrance exams; a micro-degree program for the winning adult, and awards for the best primary school pupil, student, teacher, lecturer or researcher. Special and lottery prizes are provided by Tele2, Piletilevi, Enefit, the Energy Discovery Centre, Prisma, Domino's Pizza and Raw Edge drinks, as well as by the organizers, TalTech, ERR and SEB.

Last year's competition attracted nearly 30,000 people, while the high schools with the highest turnouts were the Nõo Reaalgümnaasium, Gustav Adolfi Gümnaasium and Narva Gümnaasium. Cellphone network provider Tele2 and electronics firm Scanfil performed well among companies.

The e-rehkendus competition takes place on Wednesday, October 8, from 10 a.m. to 1 p.m., and is open to all.

The main prize, the €1,234 donated by SEB, will be divided up equally by all those who solved all 12 problems correctly.

Results solved with the help of artificial intelligence will not be admissible.

The problems were created by members of the Estonian Mathematical Society's (Eesti Matemaatika Selts) School Mathematics Association (Koolimatemaatika Ühendus).

World.title: Asian stocks drop as oil spike fans rate hike bets, eyes on US jobs
World.content:
Hong Kong – Asian stocks dropped Friday as investors grow increasingly concerned about surging oil prices and bond yields, while key jobs data later in the day will be pored over for an idea about the Federal Reserve’s next interest rate move.

Yields on US Treasuries and government debt in many other major economies spiked Thursday amid fears that the surging cost of energy caused by the Middle East crisis will force central banks to ramp up borrowing costs well into next year.

And while they eased back in early business Friday, angst continues to flow across trading floors, compounded by fresh worries of another flare-up in the US-Iran war.

Both main crude contracts edged up to extend the previous day’s rally with Washington and Tehran deadlocked on ending the crisis and unable to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.

Adding to unease, Axios said the US military was sending more warships, jets and troops to the region amid speculation US President Donald Trump could resume the war.

It said the USS Theodore Roosevelt aircraft carrier and its strike group could arrive in the Middle East next month.

Constantly high fuel costs have pushed up inflation since the start of the war at the end of February, fanning rate hike bets and pushing bond yields to levels not seen since the 2000s.

“Bond markets are now pricing in four further 25-basis-point rate hikes by June 2027,” said FOREX.com’s Fawad Razaqzada.

“That marks a dramatic shift in expectations from before the US-Iran war at the start of the year, when markets were anticipating at least 100 basis points of rate cuts over the same period.”

He pointed out that the Bloomberg Commodity Index had jumped more than 37 percent on-year and was set for one of its largest 12-month gains since the 2022 energy crisis.

“The scale of the advance points to a renewed wave of commodity-driven inflation, complicating the outlook for central banks as borrowing costs continue to rise,” he warned.

A positive lead from Wall Street was unable to provide any support to Asian stock markets, with Hong Kong losing more than two percent and Tokyo, Singapore, Wellington, Manila and Jakarta also down. Shanghai is closed for a holiday.

Seoul, however, was supported by another jump in chipmakers SK hynix and Samsung, while Sydney and Taipei were up, too.

US non-farm payrolls figures later Friday are in focus as traders try to ascertain the Fed’s next move after last month’s rate hike.

A below-forecast read on the bank’s preferred measure of inflation this week helped ease concerns for a second successive lift on October 28, but a strong jobs read could strengthen the case for such a move.

Optimism for a hold has been given a shot in the arm this week by some officials calling for a measured approach.

Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said policymakers should make a decision after “carefully examining trends in the data”, adding that “my colleagues and I will need to come to our own judgment, which may take more time”.

And another official, Michelle Bowman, said she did not “currently see an urgent need for further action”.

The remarks came after New York Fed chief John Williams said “there is no need for urgency, and we have time to gather more information”.

Still, Dallas president Lorie Logan warned: “I currently estimate the target range needs to rise an additional 50 basis points or more to appropriately balance the outlook and risks for our dual mandate goals.”
