World.title: Saudi coalition accuses Houthis of drone attack on Medina
World.content:
Riyadh – Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis struck an electricity distribution station in the holy city of Medina in Saudi Arabia, the Saudi-led coalition said Thursday, sparking strong condemnation from the Muslim world.

The alleged attack came as fighting intensifies in Yemen, where government forces said they carried out attacks on Houthi targets and AFP journalists heard explosions in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa.

The Saudi-led coalition said a drone struck Medina’s Taibah electricity distribution station, which provides power to the Prophet’s Mosque, as the Houthis denied involvement.

Medina, the burial place of the Prophet Mohammed and home to the Prophet’s Mosque, is one of Islam’s holiest cities alongside Mecca.

Coalition spokesman Major General Turki al-Maliki said a drone struck the Taibah electricity distribution station at 5:11 am (0211 GMT) on September 29.

“The investigation and evidence gathered by the competent authorities have confirmed the involvement of the Terrorist Houthi Militia in planning and executing this cowardly terrorist act, based on after-action review and the wreckage of the drone used,” he said in a statement.

The coalition said one transformer was taken out of service without affecting the wider electricity network. Al-Maliki said the facility supplied electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque.

“This cowardly terrorist act, targeting a civilian facility providing electricity to the Prophet’s Mosque in Madinah, is a continuation of this extremist militia’s attempts to target the Two Holy Mosques,” he said.

– Explosions in Sanaa –

The accusation came as fighting intensified in Yemen.

AFP correspondents heard loud explosions in the Houthi-held capital Sanaa on Thursday evening, while the internationally recognised government’s military said it had carried out strikes on Houthi targets in Sanaa, Saada and Taiz.

A spokesman said the military had conducted a “high-value targeting operation” in Sanaa and struck 11 targets in Saada.

He added that 27 air strikes had targeted an “integrated military system” belonging to the Houthis in Taiz.

The Houthis, who control Sanaa and much of Yemen’s Red Sea coast, have repeatedly launched drones and missiles at Saudi Arabia since the kingdom intervened in Yemen’s civil war in 2015.

Attacks linked to Islam’s holy cities, however, are rare.

On Thursday, a senior Houthi official again rejected accusations that the movement had targeted Islamic holy sites, according to Houthi media.

– ‘Provocative attacks’ –

Turkey strongly condemned the alleged attack and voiced support for Saudi Arabia.

“We strongly condemn the Houthis’ attack on civilian infrastructure” in Medina, the foreign ministry said.

“These provocative attacks, which threaten Saudi Arabia’s sovereignty and security and target the sacred values of the Islamic world, must cease immediately and unconditionally.”

Turkey said it reiterated its “strong support for Saudi Arabia” and called for steps to prevent further escalation.

Qatar also condemned the attack. In a statement, Doha said it was “a grave assault on the sanctity of Islamic holy sites”, a violation of Saudi sovereignty and international law.

It reaffirmed its “full solidarity” with Riyadh and said the kingdom’s security was an integral part of Gulf security.

The League of Arab States joined the chorus, calling the attack “an unacceptable transgression”.

The organisation said the attack “provokes the sentiments of Muslims worldwide” and represented a dangerous escalation.

Al-Azhar, the Cairo-based institute of Sunni Islamic learning, also denounced the incident.

It said “targeting Medina provokes the sentiments of Muslims worldwide”.

World.title: Effective Altruism: the philosophy behind Silicon Valley’s AI fears
World.content:
Washington – Dario Amodei says he is not part of it. But the Anthropic chief’s personal and professional circle is entwined with Effective Altruism (EA), a philanthropic movement that has become one of the most contested ideas in Washington and Silicon Valley.

To its proponents, EA is a rational, evidence-based way to do good. To many in the Trump administration, it fuels unfounded and exaggerated fears about artificial intelligence — the kind of warnings Amodei has become known for.

Here are some facts about EA:

– Philosophical roots –

EA is a loosely defined movement that uses evidence and reason to work out how to do the most good with a person’s money and time.

Its intellectual roots can be traced to Australian philosopher Peter Singer.

If reasonable people would agree it is morally right to ruin one’s clothes to save a drowning child, he argued in 1972, they should also sacrifice greater resources and comforts to save lives in foreign lands — because the distance should not matter.

The idea took hold among wealthy donors who felt a moral obligation to give, but wanted their money to do as much good as possible.

– Giving what you can –

EA took shape as a decentralized movement during the heady, techno-optimistic days of the late 2000s and early 2010s — when many believed social media and smartphones would promote empathy and democracy.

In 2007, financial professionals Holden Karnofsky and Elie Hassenfeld quit their jobs to launch GiveWell, which produced data-driven analyses of charities’ effectiveness.

Karnofsky was once Amodei’s roommate, and is now married to his sister Daniela, who co-founded Anthropic with him.

Two years later, Oxford University philosophers William MacAskill and Toby Ord launched “Giving What We Can,” encouraging people to donate at least 10 percent of their income to tackling global poverty.

“The critique of the status quo was that existing attempts to evaluate the work of charities and nonprofits focused on things like overhead and executive pay,” Theodore Lechterman, a philosophy professor at IE University in Madrid, told AFP.

GiveWell and others wanted to ask, “How much good is this organization actually doing in the world?” Lechterman said.

EA’s three big causes today are global poverty, factory-farmed animals and “the most controversial one — global catastrophic risk,” said Richard Chappell, a professor at University of Miami and an EA proponent.

That worry about the future is where AI comes in.

– Data-driven –

Over the last 15 years, EA has found eager followers in American tech and some corners of Wall Street.

“Since the movement is data driven, it’s a relatively easier sell to people who…make decisions on the basis of data,” Lechterman said.

That numbers-backed thinking means engineers, software developers or entrepreneurs might all find it more appealing than humanities graduates, Lechterman said.

Among them was Sam Bankman-Fried, the crypto-finance wunderkind sentenced in 2024 to 25 years in prison for fraud.

A vocal champion of the movement, Bankman-Fried said he went into finance to make a fortune he could give away.

He also was an early investor in Anthropic.

– EA and AI –

As AI worries grew, EA philosophers such as MacAskill were “kind of thinking about the future of humanity,” said Brian Berkey of the University of Pennsylvania.

The result was long-termism, a philosophy that “came to play a very central role” in the movement.

MacAskill reportedly brokered contacts between Bankman-Fried and Elon Musk.

Musk was for years outspoken about the threat he believed AI posed to humanity, and in 2015 helped create OpenAI to guard against it.

EA’s focus on AI also owes much to a neighboring movement, rationalism — an online community that grew up around writer Eliezer Yudkowsky, who has warned since the 2000s that superintelligent AI could wipe out humanity.

The two movements overlap heavily in membership and ideas, sharing an emphasis on reasoning through evidence and probabilities, and a conviction that preventing human extinction should be a top priority.

Both converged last month on Jacob Coxon, a 27-year-old researcher who quit Anthropic warning that AI companies were “gambling with our lives.” His post was viewed more than 100 million times.

Days later, Amodei published a lengthy essay arguing that AI’s mounting risks warranted a slowdown.

World.title: Anthropic’s Dario Amodei: AI’s most visible CEO and enigma
World.content:
New York – The surge in artificial intelligence and the heated debate around its risks have made Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei the most visible tech leader — though the 43-year-old remains an enigma.

“I think he is one of the great legends in tech and business,” says Alex Karp, CEO of data-analytics specialist Palantir.

The San Francisco native built in just five years a company that could be valued at 2 trillion dollars when it goes public this fall.

“There’s obviously Dario, there’s Sam Altman, there’s still your Jamie Dimons and your Bernard Arnaults of the traditional economy,” says Stephen Henriques, a senior fellow at the Yale Chief Executive Leadership Institute.

“He’s probably one of the most well recognized CEOs.”

With unruly hair, round glasses, an affable demeanor and a taste for V-neck sweaters, Amodei is worlds away from the corporate executive archetype — and seems to be motivated by something his peers are not.

This both fascinates and irritates venture capital barons and President Donald Trump’s inner circle, who struggle to decode his approach and bristle at what they view as catastrophist warnings about AI’s dangers to humanity.

Even more perplexing was his decision in March to confront the Pentagon over certain military and security uses of his AI, at the risk of losing everything.

– ‘Idealistic’ or operator? –

Some see a humanist concerned about AI’s impact on society, able to attract the world’s best researchers to history-changing projects.

Others describe a skilled operator willing to exploit collective fears about technology to serve Anthropic’s interests.

“He was very idealistic…in a technical or scientific sense,” recalls Michael Berry, an associate professor at the Princeton Neuroscience Institute who advised Amodei’s doctoral work in the late 2000s.

“He wanted to try to tackle big problems with big impact.”

A physicist by training, Amodei turned to biology for his doctorate. He was interested, Berry says, in “developing skills that would maybe at a later point allow him to cure various diseases.”

But not everyone remembers him that way.

“I never saw someone engaged in a strong moral or ethical quest,” says Olivier Marre, who worked with Amodei at Princeton on a retinal analysis device.

“Dario was ambitious, eager to succeed and be recognized for it, but not excessively or abnormally,” says Marre, now a research director at France’s INSERM. “He wasn’t a megalomaniac who crushed others.”

After Princeton, the keen swimmer took a postdoc at Stanford focused on protein analysis.

The period coincided with major advances in AI, particularly future Nobel laureate Geoffrey Hinton’s work showing that bigger models perform better.

“The pivotal moment for me comes when he became interested in both AI and Effective Altruism, which determined his trajectory,” says a witness who spoke on condition of anonymity.

“Before that,” the person says, “I frankly think he could have gone into less original things, or at least things with less spotlight.”

Amodei is considered a leading figure in the effective altruism and rationalism movements, which aim in part to reduce AI’s risks.

Anthropic told AFP that Amodei has repeatedly said he does not identify as part of the EA community, and that the company is focused on solving problems rather than driven by any particular movement or ideology.

Gregory Diamos watched the son of an Italian immigrant make that turn.

Both then working at Chinese search giant Baidu, he recalls an application from a physicist and biologist with no engineering or AI background.

“The first impression was, well, I thought it was completely irrelevant,” says Diamos, a pioneer in harnessing Nvidia’s powerful GPU chips for AI.

He read the candidate’s earlier work anyway — a computational chemistry project called ProteoWizard.

“It was some of the best code that I had ever seen. And so I was thinking to myself, if this person that has no background in computer science, other than being self-taught, can come up with this, he can figure out whatever we’re working on.”

Some trained engineers looked down on him, but “he really outworked everybody,” Diamos says. “He caught up quickly because he devoted his whole life to it, for every waking hour and then some.”

– Internal battle –

It was during that short year at Baidu that his public personality came into focus.

On a team of 300, “he had one of the strongest personalities of anybody in the group,” Diamos says, always ready to argue over research directions. “He didn’t have a problem confronting much more experienced researchers.”

That extended to management. “If he would disagree with …the direction of the company, he would say it,” Diamos says. “I think that’s what ended up leading to him leaving — eventually the disagreement got to be so big that he felt like it was not worth continuing.”

He left Baidu for Google, and later left OpenAI as well over strategy, believing AI safety there had been sidelined.

“When you realize the impact the work will have, people can’t help but weigh in,” Diamos says — which helps explain Amodei’s many sprawling essays.

Last weekend, a “Saturday Night Live” sketch cast him as a tortured figure, barely masking his dread of AI.

“You’re seeing a lot of an internal battle on what he thinks of AI, which is encouraging,” says Henriques. “Are there other marketing strategies embedded in that? Maybe.”

World.title: OpenAI says three staffers fired for mishandling ‘sensitive’ info
World.content:
San Francisco – ChatGPT-maker OpenAI said Thursday that it has fired three researchers for allegedly mishandling “sensitive information” and violating company policies, including work that involved an external organization that evaluates artificial intelligence models.

The San Francisco-based AI lab did not confirm their identities, but at least two of the employees worked on safety and alignment, according to the Wall Street Journal and Bloomberg.

“We have parted ways with three individuals,” OpenAI told AFP in a statement.

“Our investigation confirmed that these individuals mishandled sensitive information outside established company procedures, violating our policies and breaking the trust essential to our work.”

The firings come amid a tense debate about AI safety and whether the technology presents an existential risk to humanity.

Last month, a 27-year-old researcher named Jacob Coxon resigned from Anthropic with a stark warning that the leading AI labs, including OpenAI, where he previously worked, were “gambling with our lives” by racing toward developing ever more powerful models.

The three researchers fired by OpenAI are Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, according to the WSJ. The researchers did not immediately respond to AFP’s request for comment.

All three have regularly posted about AI safety-related issues on X in recent weeks.

“i am at OpenAI and i think AI is >10% likely to kill all humans,” Balesni posted on September 10, echoing statements made by other AI employees in recent weeks.

As speculation swirled about why employees at OpenAI and Anthropic were speaking so freely about their personal beliefs, Korbak jumped into the public discourse.

“I’m quite unhappy with much of what OpenAI does. I am very happy that Im allowed to say ‘I’m quite unhappy with much of what OpenAI does,'” Korbak wrote on September 11.

“It’s hard to overstate how dangerous speeding towards RSI is,” Wang posted in response to Coxon’s resignation, referring to recursive self-improvement, which is a technique where software is designed to continuously teach itself.

Leading US tech companies signed a voluntary pledge this week to regulate themselves on safety after meeting with President Donald Trump at the White House.

Trump called it a “morally binding” commitment to build adequate safeguards on the fast-moving technology.

Executives from Nvidia, Google, Meta, xAI, OpenAI and Anthropic signed the agreement.

– Safety concerns –

Concerns about the safety of advanced AI models have escalated in recent months.

OpenAI canceled the release of a new model, Astra 6.1, because it deemed the model unreliable and found that it frequently ignored instructions.

Instead, the company launched GPT-6.1 Sol, an updated version of a different model, during its annual DevDay conference on Tuesday from San Francisco. OpenAI said Sol would cost one-fifth the price of Astra.

In July, AI agents developed by OpenAI attacked Hugging Face, an AI model and application library, during an incident where the autonomous software escaped its confined testing environment.

Since then, additional security incidents have been reported that involved models developed by OpenAI, Anthropic and Google.

On Thursday, cybersecurity firm Asymmetric Security said in a report that agents developed by OpenAI covered up their own tracks after gaining unauthorized access to government websites.

The Federal Trade Commission launched a broad investigation into artificial intelligence safety practices at Anthropic and OpenAI, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday, though the scope of the inquiry is unclear.

World.title: ORA Iraq signs deal with CRC Dorra to build first phase of Madinat Al Ward
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – ORA Iraq has officially signed a contract with CRC Dorra to build the first phase of its massive flagship project, Madinat Al Ward (City of Flowers).

A ceremony was held in Baghdad to sign the deal in the presence of Naguib Sawiris, Chairman of ORA Developers, and Mohamed Dorra, Vice Chairman of Dorra Group.

The partnership represents the official transition into structural building activity after POWERCHINA, a Chinese state-owned business, completed the earthworks and ground preparation.

The first phase of the master-planned integrated city will require a large expenditure of $10 billion. It will take eight years to complete and will include residential, commercial, and administrative units, as well as hotels.

Named after the late Iraqi sociologist and scholar Ali al-Wardi, the new city project will span 61 million square meters on the southeastern side of Baghdad.

The new residential city will include 120,000 different housing units along with green spaces, urban amenities, and smart city technology to apply cutting-edge standards in sustainability and environmental preservation.

One of its most remarkable features is a unique five million square meter public park, which demonstrates ORA’s dedication to developing urban landscapes that value social well-being and environmental sustainability.

World.title: Iraqi, Gulf oil exports via Hormuz recover to previous levels
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Kpler recorded on Thursday a large number of oil tankers passing through the strategic Strait of Hormuz with US escort.

Iran has largely blocked the strait following the start of its war with the United States and Israel in late February 2026.

Between September 22 and 28, the average flow of non-Iranian crude oil from Gulf countries and Iraq through the Strait of Hormuz reached 13.5 million barrels per day, a figure comparable to pre-war levels.

This recovery comes as Iranian oil exports themselves face disruption due to the naval blockade imposed by the United States on Iranian ports.

According to Kpler’s data, at least ten oil tankers departed the Saudi port of Yanbu loaded with crude oil over the weekend, including one bound for Fos-sur-Mer in southern France.

On Sunday, 9.5 million barrels of oil were exported from the Yanbu terminal—the highest daily volume since the conflict began.

Global maritime traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remains below pre-war levels, while vessels traversing the strait continue to face the risk of attack.

Prior to the conflict, about one fifth of the world’s oil passed through the Strait of Hormuz, which has become a major point of contention between Tehran and Washington.

World.title: Iraq receives new shipment of US dollars from Federal Reserve Bank
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The spokesperson for the Iraqi government confirmed that Iraq received on Wednesday a new shipment of US dollars from the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

In a statement to the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), al-Aboudi explained that the step comes within the framework of bilateral understandings reached between Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi and US officials during his recent visit to the United States.

The arrangement aims to keep foreign currency flows and meet legitimate domestic cash demands.

The United States halted physical dollar supplies to Iraq in April 2026, including a huge cargo worth $500 million, to force Baghdad to limit the influence of Iran-backed armed groups and minimize illegal financial flow.

Washington decided to keep the supplies going in response to the Iraqi government’s efforts to tighten monitoring on dollar distribution, reduce currency abuse, expand electronic payments, and phase out the traditional currency auction system.

The revenues Iraq generates from international oil exports are officially stored in a designated account under the custody of the Federal Reserve Bank, giving Washington significant structural power over Baghdad’s access to physical cash.

The new funds will be used largely for travel-related activities and foreign transfers approved by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI).

World.title: Gujarat UCC Bill gets President Murmu’s nod paving way for implementation
World.content:
NEW DELHI: President Droupadi Murmu has given her assent to the Gujarat Uniform Civil Code Bill, 2026, completing the key legal process required for the state to enact the law.

The Gujarat assembly had earlier passed the Gujarat

Bill, 2026, making the state the second in India after Uttarakhand to pass legislation seeking to implement a Uniform Civil Code.

However, the provisions of the bill will not apply to members of Scheduled Tribes (STs).

While tabling the bill in the Assembly, chief minister

had said that the UCC was among the key reforms that Prime Minister Narendra Modi was determined to implement. "The key aim of introducing the bill is to ensure social harmony and national unity. The Supreme Court has also suggested that UCC will ensure women's rights are secured," the CM said.

The bill proposes mandatory registration of marriages and divorces, with a fine of up to Rs 10,000 for non-compliance.

It also makes registration of all live-in relationships compulsory, while requiring couples to notify authorities when such relationships end. Children born from live-in relationships will be considered legitimate children of the couple, while women deserted by their live-in partners will be entitled to seek maintenance, according to the bill.

The legislation bans polygamy and provides for up to seven years' imprisonment for marriages conducted through coercion or force. Divorce through any means other than a court decree will be punishable with up to three years in prison.

World.title: For Kolkata’s football fans, Brazil was love before first sight
World.content:
As the city gears up to host Vini Jr & Co for tomorrowâs friendly, stars of Indiaâs golden era talk of a lifelong romance ignited by match reports and the odd footage

From Argentine greats Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi to Germanyâs Oliver Kahn, Kolkata has hosted some of footballâs greatest icons down the years.

Yet, the city holds a special place for Brazil, a love affair that began with its first breakout stars and is now set to only deepen when Vinicius Jr and his teammates arrive for the friendly they play against India on Saturday at Salt Lake Stadium.

Coach Carlo Ancelottiâs boys are ranked No.6 in world football. India are a distant No.138. Some veterans have commented on the audacity of a lowly-ranked side taking on one of the giants of the game, but when Brazil first captured the imagination of football fans in India, it had more to do with a sense of kinship than purely adulation.

Dreaming without visuals

Brazilâs rise coincided with Indiaâs emergence as the superpower of Asian football, a golden era â notwithstanding the missed chance of taking part in the 1950 World Cup in Brazil â marked by triumphs at two Asian Games (1951, 1962) and a fourth-placed finish at the 1956 Olympics. As Brazil shook up football with its working-class, mixed-race team playing a unique brand of free-flowing football, India turned to it for inspiration.





âDuring our time, we only wanted to play like Brazil. Because they were the No.1 team and we also wanted to be No.1,â former footballer Shyam Thapa told TOI. âWe used to read a lot about Brazil in newspapers and were instantly drawn to this image of a team that might be economically poor like us but had the gift to conjure magic on the field and boss over European elites,â recalls Thapa.

This was before the era of live telecast and highlight shows, with imagination filling in the details that reports could not convey.

âRemember those were pre-TV days and we didnât have the opportunity to watch Brazil live. So, we used to visualise their football magic in our own way. When Chuni-da dribbled past with one of his famous body feints, we would marvel at the move, saying it would make even Garrincha proud,â says Gautam Sarkar, a star footballer of the 1970s, referring to Indian legend Chuni Goswami and the Brazilian master considered to be among the greatest dribblers of the game.

âIn my mind, I discovered my Brazil through Kajol Mukherjeeâs control and touch, Bengal Nagpur Railway star Rajendra Mohanâs running with and without the ball and, later, in Surajit Senguptaâs artistry,â adds Sarkar.

But it wouldnât be long before Kolkata found it could put faces to the names that set the cityâs football pulse racing.

Coach Dattaâs Projector

Amal Dattaâs career as a footballer never matched the ripples he would later create in his coaching avatar.

Giving up his playing career prematurely to travel to England for a one-year FA coaching course, he returned in 1960 with a certificate that made him Indiaâs first professional coach. In his luggage was a projector and grainy video clips that would give many in the city their first glimpse of Pele, Garrincha, Didi, Vava and Zagallo en route to winning the 1958 and 1962 World Cup finals.

âAmal-daâs clippings on the projector screen became an absolute craze in the city during the 1960s.

He also used to tell the audience to focus on and study the Braziliansâ movements on and off the ball,â recalls Sarkar.

Then, in the 70s, came the documentary called, âGiants of Brazilâ. âWhen it was screened for the first time at Lighthouse cinema, it resonated profoundly with the public,â says Gautam Roy, a football statistician. âReading about Brazilian football and their artistes in newspapers and magazines was the sole source for firing our imagination.

But seeing the documentary just drove up the craze,â he adds, noting how the hype would go on to hit stratospheric levels during Peleâs 1977 visit.

Pele Comes Calling

When Pele and his New York Cosmos club came calling, two of Indiaâs top club sides presented a picture of contrasts. For Mohun Bagan, the club synonymous with awakenings of national pride, those were turbulent times. Their city rivals, East Bengal, had emerged as the undisputed rulers of Indian football and were still basking in the glow of their 5-0 thrashing of Bagan in the IFA Shield final of 1975.

But, in 1976, Bagan general secretary Dhiren Dey pulled off a coup by snatching a host of players from East Bengal. It was around the same time that he learnt of Cosmosâs proposed tour of Asia. He quickly chalked out a plan to cash in on the visit. âI had already committed myself to East Bengal when he (Dey) proposed that I play for Bagan and grab the opportunity of taking the field against Pele. It was an offer too tempting for me to ignore,â says Shyam Thapa, who scored in the 2-2 tie against Cosmos at Eden Gardens on Sept 24, 1977.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Saturdayâs friendly comes at that time of the year when a sense of festivity drifts into Bengalâs air. As Kolkata gears up for Durga Puja, it will also look to embellish a deep bond that beats as part of its footballing heart. For both Sarkar and Thapa, the arrival of the Brazil team is like the journey coming full circle. Whatever the result, they know nothing can take away the bragging rights won nearly 50 years back: âthe pride of playing against Peleâ.

World.title: Centre identifies 28 spots in Ladakh for inclusion on official Survey of India map
World.content:
28 spots identified in Ladakh for inclusion on official Survey of India map

Standard names for Ladakhâs geographical features

Gogra, Hot Spring among identified features

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre has identified and standardised 28 places and geographical features in Ladakh by their official place and feature names for inclusion on the Survey of India (SoI) map, the Ministry of Home Affairs said on Thursday.The exercise was carried out in consultation with the Union Territory administration of Ladakh and is aimed at ensuring accurate recognition of the locations and creating greater awareness about them, the ministry said, news agency ANI reported.The 28 identified locations include peaks, mountains, passes, glaciers, valleys, rivers, lakes, water bodies and land areas.The list includes Atisha Giri, Kanishka Peak, Martand Giri, Zorawar Peak, Rinchen Zangpo, Sakyasri Giri, Marpa Lotsava Ri, Milarepa Kangri, Shiva Ri and Maheshvara Ri among the peaks.Karun Pir, Drak Karpo and Jolmori have been identified as mountains, while Chapchingal Pass and Shachmirk Pass have been designated as passes. Parpik and Skamri have been identified as glaciers, while Shkorga Valley and Yangpa River are also among the features formally recorded.The list also includes Gogra, Dehra Compass, Brangsa, Kuksel, Kumarayana Point, Panglung and Shamal Lungpa as land areas. Guru Rinpoche has been identified as a lake, while Hot Spring has been listed as a water body.The standardisation of geographical names is part of maintaining official cartographic records and ensuring consistency in the names used for geographical features across government maps and records.The exercise also covers strategically significant locations in Ladakh, including Gogra and Hot Spring, which were among the friction points during the India-China border standoff in eastern Ladakh.The Survey of India, the country's national mapping agency, is responsible for surveying, mapping and preparing official maps of India. The formal inclusion of the 28 locations is expected to provide standard references for the features and improve public awareness of their names and locations.

World.title: The midnight rescue of Karachi's Mahatma Gandhi
World.content:
One of the first things I did when I returned to Pakistan in early 2000, this time as the Indian High Commissioner, was to pay my respects to an imposing bronze statue of Mahatma Gandhi.

One of only two Gandhi statutes in Pakistan, Bapuji stands tall at the lobby of the Indian High Commission in Islamabad, famed walking stick in hand, gazing into the distance.

The tale of how a pre-Partition statue found its way to its eventual home in the Indian High Commission is a fascinating saga reflecting the tangled tumultuous history of our two countries. It is a journey in which I was honoured to have played a small part.

Gandhi statue in the Indian High Commission, Islamabad (Picture credit: Haider Sherazi)

According to several accounts, the statue originally stood outside the Sindh high court on what was known as Kings Way in Karachi. It had been commissioned by the Indian merchant association sometime in the 1930s to commemorate the historic Karachi session of the Indian National Congress. The plaque underneath the life-size monument apparently read: âMahatma Gandhi â the reputability of freedom, truth and nonviolence.





â

Partition brought the inevitable dislocation. With communal riots engulfing Karachi in 1948, there was fear that the statue would be torn down amidst mob fury. Accounts vary on what exactly happened, but apparently after the intervention of Jamshed Nussranwanji Mehta, a Parsi and former Mayor of Karachi, the statue was surreptiously taken down and moved quietly to the home of the Cowasjees, a leading Parsi family of Karachi.

And there it lay for more than thirty yearsâ¦

A few months into my first stint in Pakistan as Consul General in Karachi, a middle aged Parsi gentleman approached me. He was a well known Karachi businessman, activist and columnist whose name I am withholding. Over the course of several meetings he told me his incredible tale. How he as a young man along with several of his school chums insouciantly removed the Gandhi statue in the dead of the night armed with some basic tools and a lorry â all while Karachi seethed with fear and hatred.

It was then ferried to his fatherâs home, initially meant as a temporary abode until a handover to Indian representative could be organised. Unfortunately, the then Indian High Commissioner to the Dominion of Pakistan could not assure a safe passage and refused. And that was how the Cowasjees became the involuntary guardians of Gandhi in Pakistan

The Parsi gentleman was clear that his part in the story had to come to an end.

We were now in the early 1980âs. General Ziaâs Islamisation project was well underway. Sharia laws had been introduced into the legal system. Strict Islamic punishments were to be meted out for crimes like adultery, theft and drinking of alcohol. Educational curriculums were being rigorously overhauled to promote religious studies and conformity with orthodox Islamic principles.

Dress codes, especially for women, were being enforced. The sari, once common amongst upper class Pakistani women, was fast disappearing.

An ongoing media clampdown weeded out content deemed as un-Islamic.

Though historically Parsis, unlike other minorities in Pakistan, have enjoyed a somewhat protected status and though Ardeshir was and continued to be a fearless and outspoken critic of the political establishment, he was no longer comfortable with his role as the statueâs custodian. He asked me if the long delayed handover of the statue could finally take place.

I immediately agreed. I was determined that the statue, now a priceless historical artifact, should come home on my watch. There was, however, a tricky logistical issue to navigate. Constant surveillance by Pakistani intelligence was a fact of life. So how could we transport the statue without compromising the Cowasjees.

After clearance from Delhi, we decided to replicate the original midnight run. A non-descript truck, organised by the Consulate, picked up a large wrapped item from the Cowasjee residence and quietly brought it to the Indian mission late one summer night.

I personally inspected the precious cargo. Through all its travails, the statue had endured some damage. One hand was broken and the glasses were cracked, but otherwise Gandhiji stood tall. We arranged for some minor repairs, and after a few weeks, the statue took pride of place in the Chancery reception. Suddenly confronted with this majestic but serene statue, surprised Pakistani visitors were often curious about its origins, but we remained tightlipped.

Eventually, once the statue was properly restored, we arranged for its transportation to the High Commission in Islamabad. In hindsight, that last trek from Karachi to Islamabad turned out to be as consequential as the original journey in 1948. In 1993, following the demolition of the Babri Masjid, furious mobs in Pakistan attacked over 30 Hindu temples and in Karachi ransacked both the Consulate and the Consul Generalâs residence in which I had once lived.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Valuable art was vandalised, including a beautiful painting by B. Prabha.

Post the 1993 attacks, the Indian consulate in Karachi closed down. It remains shut to this day. In Islamabad, however, the Gandhi statue still stands, an enduring testament to âfreedom, truth and non-violenceâ true to its original plaque.

G. Parthasarathy has served as Indiaâs Consulate General in Karachi and as Indiaâs High Commissioner in Islamabad.

World.title: SP to field third candidate in UP Rajya Sabha polls? How move would trigger contest with BJP
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party (SP) MP Virendra Singh on Friday announced that the party will field a third candidate in the upcoming Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, despite only two SP candidates being assured of victory.

If the SP fields a third candidate, it would set up a contest with the ruling BJP for one seat. Seven BJP candidates are assured of victory. Polling for 10 vacant Rajya Sabha seats from the state is scheduled for October 16.

âWe will decide our third candidate today and the nomination will be filed by October 5,â Singh told PTI.

The Chandauli MP further remarked that the SP would adopt the âsame strategyâ the BJP used to secure the election of its candidates in the previous Rajya Sabha polls.

âWe will get all three of our candidates elected through the same route by which the BJP had got its candidates elected in the last Rajya Sabha elections,â Singh added.

He also claimed that several BJP MLAs seeking SP tickets for the 2027 Uttar Pradesh assembly elections were in touch with the Akhilesh Yadav-led party.

Singhâs remarks came a day after Akhilesh Yadav declined to confirm whether the SP would field a third candidate, suggesting that the BJP could put up ânine or even 10 candidates.â





The SP on September 30 nominated veteran party leader and Akhilesh Yadavâs uncle, Ram Gopal Yadav, and Reliance Industries executive Dhanraj Parimal Nathwani for the elections. Both subsequently filed their nomination papers in Lucknow.

The arithemtic

The number of first-preference votes required to win a Rajya Sabha seat in Uttar Pradesh depends on the number of vacancies and the number of MLAs eligible to vote. With 10 seats up for election this time, the winning benchmark is likely to be around 37 first-preference votes.

The BJP currently has 255 MLAs in the 403-member Uttar Pradesh assembly, while its NDA allies have another 33, taking the allianceâs combined strength to 288.

The SP has 101 MLAs. Three legislators who defected to the BJP are currently unattached, while rebel MLA Puja Pal remains listed with the SP despite having joined the BJP. The Congress, an SP ally, has two MLAs.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In the 2024 Rajya Sabha elections in Uttar Pradesh, the BJP won all eight seats it contested, while two of the SPâs three nominees were elected.

The SPâs third candidate, Alok Ranjan, lost.

Rajya Sabha elections are conducted through proportional representation using the single transferable vote system. Under this system, surplus votes received by winning candidates can be transferred to other candidates based on votersâ subsequent preferences.

As a result, if more than 10 candidates enter the fray, the contest could hinge on the distribution and transfer of votes, making electoral arithmetic and strategy crucial.

(With PTI inputs)

World.title: Why Indian pilots struggle to take jobs abroad
World.content:
NEW DELHI: At a time when pilotsâ mental health has emerged as a key concern post some recent events, with flydubai cockpit fight being the most recent one, Indiaâs restrictive rules for cockpit crew to leaves domestic airlines only after serving long notice periods could be adding to their stress.

The rule for a co-pilot to serve six monthsâ notice and a captain a year (which has been challenged legally), has made it difficult for foreign airlines to hire Indian aviators as they mostly want people to join in three months. Now with Captain Smit Machchhar proving his mettle in flydubai, the budget arm of Dubaiâs mega carrier Emirates, Indian pilots hope foreign airlines â primarily in Gulf and other places like Sri Lanka and South Korea â keep the Indian reality in mind while giving them offer letters.

âWe usually donât hire direct from India and prefer if a pilot has worked in a second country before onboarding them,â a senior official of a leading West Asian airline had recently told TOI. The reasons are two-fold: Indiaâs notice period requirement, which remains binding for pilots even if the employer in India defaults on contractual obligations like paying on time, and then informal tie-ups with big Indian carriers against âpoaching.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines





â

A senior official of an airline here said: âBecause of the notice period requirement, some pilots here give âfake resignationâ in advance and then look for jobs so that they can leave in three months of getting a job abroad. And if they donât get a job, they take the fake resignation back.â

The notice period rule has been challenged by pilots in court and the matter is sub judice. âThere are concerns about pilotsâ state of mind due to what could be going on in their personal lives. This notice period rule, meant to ensure schedule integrity of airlines by preventing sudden mass resignations, has outlived its utility. Today India has two big and well-funded airline and a few emerging ones. Now it is only protecting airlines that are unable to pay,â said a pilot.

World.title: Captain Smit Machchhar: A steady hand, in and out of the cockpit
World.content:
Long before he was the captain who held a cockpit together despite stab wounds, Capt Smit Machchhar was the pilot who interacted with loaders, engineers, ground staff, catering people, all with equal respect.

âSmit is the most calm, composed and down-to-earth person you could ever meet,â said Capt Dharav Gosalia, a friend since his flying school days.

On Wednesday, that steadiness was tested at altitude. flydubai flight FZ1073 was carrying 174 people from Dubai to Tel Aviv when, according to Israeli officials, Machchharâs co-pilot stabbed him and tried to crash the aircraft. The jet reportedly dropped nearly 14,000 feet in under 30 seconds.

Seriously wounded, Machchhar managed to open the cockpit door, letting passengers and crew overpower the attacker. The plane landed in Saudi Arabia.

Those who know Machchhar, 39, are not surprised by how he behaved. What shocks them is that it was ever required. âHe is one of the calmest and most fun guys possible,â said a friend, a B737 pilot who requested anonymity. âMaybe it is his upbringing. He is always in fun mode, but he is family-oriented too.â





.

Machchhar earned his commercial pilot licence at Mainland Aviation College in New Zealand in the late 2000s, where he became the classmatesâ go-to person for hard subjects. âAnyone with a problem in air navigation, aircraft technical or any subject went to him,â the pilot said. âBecoming a line trainer at flydubai was the best thing that could have happened to him.â

The instinct to help was visible earlier, too. At M D Bhatia School, where he passed Class 10 in 2003, school friend Bhavin Jethva remembers him as âstraightforward, bindassâ.

âHe didnât like to lie,â Jethva said. âHe was never fake and he couldnât pretend.â Amit Soni, a childhood friend who played cricket with him, called him cheerful and lively.

At Swastik Heights in Mumbaiâs Tilak Nagar, where Machchhar lived until about 2022, neighbour Laxmikanth Joshi remembers practical kindnesses. After returning from Kenya, Joshi realised he had bought too little coffee to share with friends.

Machchhar arranged for a pilot colleague to bring back more. Joshi also remembers Machchhar going straight to the hospital after landing in India when his father underwent bypass surgery about six months ago.

He stayed through the treatment. Then there were the Independence Day and Republic Day celebrations. He recalls Capt Machchhar taught them to tie the rope into a knot just right. âOne pull and the flag unfurled,â recalled Joshi.

Akshay Joshi, his immediate neighbour, recalls tense moments at his place when his parents learned about the attack. Late in the evening, though, Machchharâs parents informed the societyâs WhatsApp group that their son was recovering.

Capt Machchhar moved to Dubai around 2022 after leaving SpiceJet, and flies the Boeing 737 as a captain and line trainer at flydubai. He and his wife, Sonal, have two children: Krishay, 2, and Ziva, 9.

Friends and colleagues tried to reconstruct the sequence. A B737 commander said the co-pilot would most likely have used the âcrash axeâ, which is carried on the flight deck for use during emergencies, such as cutting through panels and debris, or the cockpit window to exit the aircraft after an accident. âAt the Dubai airport, even shoes and belts are removed at security,â he said. âThereâs no way the co-pilot could have got onboard with a pocket knife.

â

Another colleague said the co-pilot âapparently stood up and hit Machchhar on the side of the headâ. This colleague added that the captain was also struck in the chest, before he regained control after the dive. A third pilot said Machchhar appeared to have squawked â7500â, the hijack transponder code. A B737 commander also pointed to a gap: âWe have SOPs for a hijack scenario, but not for a cockpit where the aggressor is inside.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

â He noted that Capt Machchharâs bravery boils down to two acts: first, he managed to get the aircraft straight and level after that precarious dive, despite being attacked; second, though he had lost a lot of blood, he managed to open the cockpit door before he passed out.

At M D Bhatia School, former classmates have been posting prayers for his recovery on their WhatsApp group. âWe are proud of him,â Jethva said.

World.title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches Vettri Payanam scheme, expanding no-fare bus travel for women
World.content:
Tamil Nadu Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay launched the ‘Vettri Payanam’ scheme on Friday (October 2, 2026), expanding no-fare bus travel for women and transgender persons, at the Koyambedu bus terminus in Chennai. Coinciding with Gandhi Jayanthi, Mr. Vijay kickstarted the scheme by issuing free tickets to women passengers.

The Vettri Payanam scheme will benefit 84.32 lakh beneficiaries every day.

In the expanded scheme, women can undertake no-fare travel in the Ordinary, Express, Limited Stop Service (LSS), and Deluxe buses in cities and towns, Ordinary buses in mofussil areas, and Ordinary buses in Ghat sections over 40 km.

Also read: What is the Vettri Payanam Thittam launched by Tamil Nadu CM Vijay? | Explained

S. Malar, a resident of Chennai who was on board one of the buses at Koyambedu, said, “It was pretty surreal and exciting to see the Chief Minister issue tickets to passengers.”

K. Abhirami, a resident of Tiruvallur, said she was glad the scheme was being expanded. “I had the opportunity to even take a photograph with him (Mr. Vijay),” she added.

A total of 12,695 buses under the seven State Transport Corporations have been brought under the Vettri Payanam scheme, and 1,68,500 trips (singles) will be operated.

Bypoll restrictions

It is to be noted that the scheme will not be implemented in Chengalpattu and Tiruppur districts, owing to the bypolls in the Madurantakam and Dharapuram Assembly constituencies, where the Model Code of Conduct is in place.

Mr. Vijay, on August 24, announced the expanded scheme under Rule No. 110 in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly.

World.title: ED conducts searches at seven locations in Hyderabad, Kadapa in Vivekananda Reddy murder case
World.content:
The Enforcement Directorate (ED) on Friday (August 21) conducted searches at seven locations in Hyderabad and Kadapa in connection with the 2019 murder of former Andhra Pradesh Minister Y.S. Vivekananda Reddy.

The searches were conducted under the provisions of the Prevention of Money Laundering Act (PMLA) at the residential premises of key accused in the case. The ED said incriminating documents and digital devices were seized during the searches, besides ₹24 lakh in unaccounted cash and two locker keys from the premises of YSRCP Lok Sabha MP from Kadapa, Y.S. Avinash Reddy.

Also Read: ED summons Kadapa MP Avinash Reddy in money laundering case linked to Vivekananda Reddy’s murder

Vivekananda Reddy, paternal uncle of former Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister Y.S. Jagan Mohan Reddy, was found murdered at his residence in Kadapa on March 15, 2019. The Andhra Pradesh High Court had directed the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) to conduct further investigation into the case in March 2020.

The CBI subsequently registered a case under Sections 302 and 120-B of the Indian Penal Code and filed three chargesheets, naming Avinash Reddy, his father Y.S. Bhaskar Reddy, YSRCP functionary D. Siva Shankar Reddy, T. Gangi Reddy, Y. Sunil Yadav and others as accused.

According to the ED, the CBI’s chargesheets alleged that Siva Shankar Reddy, along with Avinash Reddy and Bhaskar Reddy, was unhappy with Vivekananda Reddy’s growing political influence and that a conspiracy was subsequently hatched to eliminate him.

The ED’s money laundering case is based on the CBI FIR and chargesheets, with Sections 302 and 120-B of the IPC being scheduled offences under the PMLA.

The agency said Shaik Dastagiri, who was part of Vivekananda Reddy’s staff and later turned approver, had told the CBI that the murder conspiracy was allegedly hatched about a month before the killing. He reportedly alleged that Gangi Reddy had told him about the involvement of Siva Shankar Reddy and some senior politicians and that ₹40 crore was promised for the murder.

The ED said Dastagiri had also disclosed that he was allegedly offered ₹5 crore as his share and received ₹1 crore from Sunil Yadav. The CBI had subsequently recovered and seized ₹46.70 lakh in cash and unaccounted jewellery from the locker of Dastagiri’s friend Syed Munna and his mother, the agency said.

Further investigation is underway.

World.title: ‘Don’t Trouble The Trouble’ movie review: Fahadh Faasil and Ssara Palekar carry this uneven drama
World.content:
Don’t Trouble The Trouble, written and directed by Shashank Yeleti, marks Fahadh Faasil’s first Telugu film as a solo lead. The film is an example of what it could have been versus what it actually is. Aiming to appeal to children and the childlike in adults, it makes for an easy watch without violence or gore. Some genuinely funny moments had children and adults in the hall cheering, but the narrative also has stretches that offer little excitement.

The three principal actors — Fahadh Faasil, child actor Ssara Palekar and the adorable beagle Snoopy — are fantastic. Shashank has some fun ideas, from Aladdin and his magic lamp to an invisible character seen only by two characters and spells that should appeal to Potterheads. But not all of these ideas translate into an immersive experience.

Don’t Trouble The Trouble ends up as a partially enjoyable film that does not quite realise its potential to be the full-on, fun children’s film we don’t get often.

Don’t Trouble The Trouble (Telugu) Director: Shashank Yeleti Cast: Fahadh Faasil, Ssara Palekar Runtime: 158 minutes Storyline: When an ambulance driver tries to kidnap a child to demand ransom, little does he know everything from that point spells trouble.

The story follows Suri (Fahadh Faasil), an ambulance driver who will go to any length to make quick money, without much remorse. The opening episode establishes what he is capable of. He does not care about the consequences of his rash driving, always has a trick up his sleeve, and even puts his closest friend’s safety at risk to make more money. Why does he resort to shortcuts? There are not enough answers. He is a grey character without the usual sob-story justification. That isn’t necessarily a problem, but the dull stretches that follow are.

The entire Old City episode around Charminar is populated by stock characters, including those played by Mahesh Manjrekar and his team. Even when Suri is pushed against the wall and has to make money within a short time, there is little sense of urgency or danger, thanks to the caricaturish goons and lame situations built around them.

The film gathers momentum when Suri meets Divya (Ssara Palekar) and her dog, Snoopy. The pre-interval episode is a riot, with all three delivering their best acts in the film, aided by Kaala Bhairava’s music and the technical team. If only the portions leading up to this had been interesting enough. This is also when the film raises the stakes.

The film soon meanders before reaching its core plot — finding Divya’s parents. The police are on the trail, a relative wants answers, a child finds herself in a strange situation, and Suri is cornered and, for the first time, fearful of what he is up against. Some of these arcs work well, while others feel stretched as the magic tricks become repetitive. When an innovative suspension of disbelief is used too often, it inevitably loses its hold.

Don’t Trouble The Trouble was shot across Hyderabad in real locations, adding to its authenticity. The cinematography by Brad Francis, Rama Rajamouli’s costume design, and the production design by Mohan Nath Bingi and Sandeep Suvarna stay true to the milieu of Suri’s modest home and the people he encounters.

Fahadh Faasil and Ssara Palekar carry the film. As the story begins to explore the bond between them, Fahadh is convincing in portraying Suri’s change of heart. His Telugu diction can occasionally be distracting, though it also adds authenticity for cinephiles who have followed his Malayalam and Tamil films over the years. Ssara’s performance balances childlike innocence with the maturity the role demands. She is a terrific find, and it will be interesting to see what she takes on next.

Towards the end, the film takes a melodramatic turn, but it completes Suri’s character arc. It contrasts with the opening portions while providing emotional closure for both him and Divya and cementing the bond they have developed.

Don’t Trouble The Trouble has its heart in the right place and entertains in parts. What it needed was a little more magic in the writing.

World.title: Asian Games 2026 LIVE: Lovlina punches her way to Asian games gold
World.content:
Lovlina Borgohain ended India’s 12-year wait for an Asian Games women’s boxing gold, defeating China’s Ziyi Bao in the 75kg final. Olympic medallist Lovlina defeated Bao by a 5-0 unanimous decision to upgrade the silver she had won at the last edition, where she had lost to another Chinese boxer, Li Qian, in the final.

With the win, Lovlina became only the second Indian woman after legendary MC Mary Kom to win an Asian Games boxing gold.

India’s women’s recurve team produced a sensational performance under pressure to stun 10-time Olympic champions South Korea 5-3 and clinch a maiden Asian Games gold medal on Friday (October 2, 2026).

Seasoned campaigner Ankita Bhakat, Kirti Sharma and 17-year-old Kumkum Mohod held their nerve in challenging windy conditions to outshoot the defending champions and script a historic triumph.

Also Read | Asian Games 2026 medal tally

The Indian women’s hockey team will take on China in the gold-medal match at 3:30 p.m. IST. The Indian side will look to finish on top and secure the Asian Games title, with qualification for the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games also at stake.
